----Brand New Review----
So in the beginning Conan Exiles had a horrible start, and everyone now and then some servers are still a bit choppy. The easy fix for that is: Find a server that works, like I did.
Now to all the bad reviews: Get over it! It is an Early Access Game afterall. If you don't know what that means, than you shouldn't even be buying games in this section...
Now to all others who like this game or are thinking about getting this game:
It is very similar to Ark and other survival crafting games with an rpg aspect. That means you can level your character through crafting, gathering and fighting. Every time you level up you get a certain amount of skill points for Melee damage, Ranged damage, Vitality, Stamina, Encumberance (how much you can carry), and Survival (how much slower your hunger and thirst are). You also get recipe points, which you use like in Ark, to unlock new crafting recipes.
For an early access game, this game has a ridiculous amount of content in character creation, skills, recipes, npc and wildlife variety, and the world in general.
As for Multiplayer: It is immense fun playing with friends or with strangers and creating a clan, and working towards creating a great village, city or castle for your clan and for others to visit and trade.
This game all in all is 9/10, and is absolutely amazing already!

This is a story; a novel of the events you are playing through. Gameplay is only half of what makes up Valkyria Chronicles. The other half consists of fully voiced and animated skits that explain the daily lives of what the soldiers are going through. It ranges from discrimination, comaraderie, love, and unfortunately death. Watching and hearing the events unfold definitely made me think more about how black and white war can be made out to be. Another portion of that half consists of a "sim" aspect where the player can upgrade weapons, soldier classes, and tanks through a tree-based upgrade system. Classing up soldiers can yield them learning special skills and a new title even. Characters can be recruited and dropped from the current roster at anytime so there's no fear of losing a favorite if they're not needed so swap away. A very welcome touch this game brings to thee table is that every character has a bio and major characters have bios that continuously update as the player progresses through the story. Not only that, you can view their different outfits, if applicable so if you wanted to make a replica or just see them up close. Feel free. Music is top notch. Some familiar faces from a certain Dreamcast/Gamecube port make appearances. I highly recommend this for anybody who enjoy the likes of Advance Wars, Fire Emblem or likes JRPG's in general.

: NIS America, INC
==========
Long have I been a fan of Disgaea, and at last it has found it's way to Steam! I still own physical copies of each currently available installment, but I couldn't help but obtain a copy of this PC port of the first title. Is it a good port? I think so, but it does have a few problems here and there, as well as some quality issues that really should have been addressed by now. Regardless of these issues, it's still fun to play. Following the exploits of Prince Laharl and the series' signature humor are more than enough reason to check it out.
==========
Disgaea is the first in a long line of strategy RPGs developed by Nippon Ichi Software. If you've ever played anything like Final Fantasy Tactics or Ogre Battle, you know more or less what to expect. It's simple to learn...select a unit, tell it where to go, then what to do. You have the chance to commit any action or redo your selections before ending your turn. Once all of your units have had an action, it's the enemies' turn. Turns go back and forth until you either win or lose.
There are a few interesting mechanics Disgaea introduced to mix things up a bit, the first and foremost of which is the Dark Assembly. Here you can spend Mana (obtained by individual units by defeating enemies) to do all sorts of things, including creating new characters. The more Mana you spend, the stronger the new unit starts out and will become as it levels up. Another interesting thing to note is that stats can get RIDICULOUS. The level cap is 9,999, and your basic stats (Attack, Defense, Speed, etc) can reach BILLIONS. Yes, you read that right! You do not have to reach insanely high levels to clear the game's main story though (only about 50-70, depending on your skill level and party composition), but you do have to put in some work to overcome it's greatest challenges.
There are a lot of other features and mechanics, but I don't want to spoil the surprise! I need to leave some things for you to discover yourself.
==========
Here is one of this port's major problems...In some aspects, it is obviously improved over it's original PS2 version, but other aspects look like no work was put into them to make it look better. Character sprites look just like they did in the olden days, but dialog portraits look amazing. Battle animations could have used some touching up as well. This isn't a HUGE deal, but while playing it's sometimes glaringly obvious that they got lazy in some areas.
==========
I didn't really notice any improvements in this area, but it's good enough as it is. The music can be quick catchy and quirky, and add a somewhat playful tone to the overall game. Nearly all the main characters are fully voice acted, and are voiced in most scenes. The voice acting overall is very good.
==========
The game ran beautifully on my lower mid range custom rig, with stable framerates and no lag or stuttering. My only issue is movement controls in battle. It's like they took a D-Pad and tilted it a bit. You press Right and the Cursor goes Down. Press Up and the Cursor goes Right. This takes a bit to compensate for, and it is annoying...but there's no real way around it. Just takes getting used to. I used a controller for my playtime, and it worked almost as well as the console PS2 version.
==========
If you are looking for a quirky strategy RPG to keep you busy for awhile, Disgaea will definitely scratch that itch. Hopefully NIS America ports the next few installments of the series to Steam in the future. They've already started putting some of their other titles up here, such as Phantom Brave (which I'd also recommend!!).

Real money makes your life a lot easier, but there's also the possibility of acquiring Platinum (the real money currency of the game) selling your drops to other players. Word of advice: to really succeed in this game, it's way easier if you're social. Frequent the forums, engage in trading and try to join a guild ASAP. Good luck out there!

The Mass Effect trilogy does for sf video games what Babylon 5 did for sf tv shows. The player should expect to encounter distinctive characters who operate in a zone of interpersonal conflicts and political machinations, an ambitious tapestry of story woven from many interlocking sub-plots, and impressive attention to worldbuilding. Clearly a labour of love as much as a product of simple commercial interests. Oh, and the gameplay isn't bad either.

(Note: This is a review of the port quality and not the game itself)
When this port first hit Steam it was kind of a huge mess. NIS has been pretty good at taking feedback and continuing to support/update the game, though, and I can honestly say that it is now a pretty decent PC port.
There are still some issues with it, especially in the visual department. You have to understand that it is an older game (and it already "looked old" on its native PS2), but that's not where the visual mess comes in. They tried to add a bunch of fancy effects like shadows and edge blurring and such, but it just looks baaaad. Fortunately, you can turn most of these horrendous things off and everything is A-Okay. The biggest offender is the "new textures" applied to game maps. They look terrible. REALLY terrible. They just don't mesh with the surrounding art at all. Thankfully, again, you can turn them off and just use the classic map. (Whew.) The updated character portraits in the interface look fantastic, but the updated interface itself is sort of jarring. Unfortunately, if you turn off the updated interface you don't get the updated character portraits. You have to use both or neither. But you can get used to the interface so it's not TOO bad.
My biggest complaints when the port first came out were the control issues. I like playing Disgaea with a controller and you'd think that part would have ported over just fine, considering the game was ORIGINALLY for controllers. But the character movement at the hub had an insaaaane acceleration issue, the cursor controlled kinda wonky, and all of the button cues on the interface were just generic numbers instead of the actual buttons. Not to mention huge, inexplicable framerate drops that would happen from time to time. BUT ALL OF THIS HAS BEEN FIXED. Character movement is now fine, cursor is fine, button cues show the actual buttons (on my 360 style controller at least), and I'm no longer experiencing framerate issues.
I would have been VERY hesitant to recommend this port when it first dropped on Steam, but I feel like it's now in a pretty good place. It isn't flawless, but it's plenty good enough.

I put off playing this game for quite some time despite it being recommended to me over and over. Something about it being a console port and ‘Yet another game set during WW2’ put me off. I was deeply mistaken. This is one of the best strategy games I’ve played, as far as the style of play goes it is very similar to X-Com: EU but the story and characters resonated deeply with me and I played it more for the story than for the battles themselves (which are nonetheless great). Only a few minor things give away that this was originally a game for the PS3, the port is very well done although I know some people dislike the controls. The graphics have aged well; the watercolor style which permeates the game is beautiful and the higher resolutions that modern PCs are capable of do it great justice. The game also runs without stutter on my weaker non-gaming laptop.
Interestingly, while I would normally never consider watching anime in anything but its original language I found the English script of this game to be superior to the Japanese, the latter is quite dry at times and I feel the English voice actors are actually a better fit for their respective characters. And the story and characters are really what make this game stand out. Games that go out of their way to elicit strong emotional responses never make an impression on me, but this one did. As we follow the story along, the characters are occasionally thrust into situations where they must do battle for one reason or another, this using a delightful combination of strategic top-down and tactical first-person gameplay that few other games have tried. While not especially realistic, it works well and you feel very in control of your soldiers’ actions.
In the broader perspective however, Valkyria Chronicles’ depiction of a large 1900s military conflict from a squad’s point of view is very realistic and includes a number of scenarios that ring familiar to anyone used to games set during WW2 – the dramatic beach landing, an assault on an unassailable fortress, a liberation of a small town, a sneak through the forest to avoid detection, and so forth. The considerable variation in battles keeps the game interesting and it never felt like a grind to me. Eventually, supernatural elements (the titular Valkyria) are introduced and the story kicks it up a notch into epic territory. Few games these days become so noticeably better the more you play them.
As for negatives, I don’t think the game is very enjoyable if you focus on getting the highest possible ranking from every encounter, as this rewards speed over all else. A few battles are nearly impossible to win on the first try without prior knowledge about what challenges await you once the mission starts, meaning you may find yourself having to start over with a different strategy. The game lets you save both between and during battles, however, so this can usually be alleviated by simply backing up a few turns. There are fairly few achievements and they range from trivial to almost impossible; a few more in the middle range wouldn’t have hurt. I also dislike the fact that you have to play through the game twice to access some content.
Summing it up, this game is fantastic. It combines all the elements of a good anime and a good turn-based strategy game, with enough of its own flavor to be unique and spectacularly enjoyable. My main problem with it is that it only took me about 45 hours to complete and I fear the next game I play won’t be nearly as good.

The random encounter element leads to some interesting scenarios, its fun to go through and try to unlock more stuff. The combat starts really slow, but speeds up as you progress through the story, in the end its not super compelling, and at times can be a bit grindy, especially on runs where you have bad luck with weapons. But ultimately it didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game, and at times it can feel really badass to zip from enemy to enemy countering and deflecting ranged attacks while building up a massive combo.
It is definitely a unique take on deckbuilding, as you have to balance risk and reward, you can hand-tailor the difficulty by including more challenging/risky encounters to make the game even more intresting. I feel like $25 is a fair price if a bit on the high end of what I personally think the game is worth, if the game is currently on sale, I would definitely recommend buying it.
At the time of review, I've spent about 11 hours with the game, beaten the story mode to completion including the final boss which was a very interesting and challenging encounter, you're in for a treat. But there is still plenty left to do, I have only unlocked about 80% of the available cards and every journey into endless mode has been very different. Sometimes the deck is generous and I can spend several floors feeling like a god, and others I'm smited down immediately by seemingly insurmountable odds, but either way, it can be a single encounter that changes the course of the game, it keeps it very engaging.

"Unreal Gold" includes the base game "Unreal", and its mission pack "Return to Na Pali". It also uses the menu from Unreal Tournament, rather than the one from the Unreal disc version.
Today, Unreal could almost be called a hidden gem. It was big back in 1998, but over the years it has somewhat faded into obscurity, at least compared to games like Doom and Quake, which are still widely known and popular. Perhaps this is because Half-Life, a great, but in my opinion inferior game, released at the same time and received vastly more media coverage. Or because the multiplayer version, Unreal Tournament, would become the flagship of Epic Games.
Unreal remains one of the very best single-player FPS to this day. The gameplay could be described as an in-between mix of action-packed shooting (Quake) and atmospheric exploration (S.T.A.L.K.E.R.). The shooting isn't quite as polished and fleshed out as in the id games, but the leveldesign is top-notch. Together with the great music, it creates an immersive atmosphere that's rarely seen in games. Unreal will lead you through so many unique and memorable places over the course of the campaign that it's hard to list them all. You'll explore ancient temples, and it will make you feel as if you were Indiana Jones. You'll also make your way through the decks of a crashed spaceship, and you'll feel just like Ellen Ripley. Add a village in the sky here, an alien mothership there, the leveldesign will take you from one highlight to another.
The arsenal consists of ten weapons and, seeing as this is an older game, you can carry them all. All weapons have two fire modes, while some have additional depth to them, such as the ASMD that can do combos or the 8ball that can load up to six rockets or grenades at once and fire either spread out or close together and even lock on enemies to fire heat-seeking rockets.
All weapons are different from one another, most are interesting and innovative. Unfortunately, they are not balanced. Different weapons have different strengths and weaknesses, but some are outright better than others. The Flak Cannon is a strong counter for the quick and aggressive enemies that like to engage the player in melee combat, and will be your preferred weapon for most encounters as long as you have enough ammo. The more powerful hitscan weapons also pack a good punch and are overall strong and versatile. The most common enemy creature in the game, the Skaarj, is agile and very good at dodging, which makes it a real challenge to inflict meaningful damage with weapons that fire projectiles. Those weapons tend to become easily replaced as your arsenal grows.
Unreal pits you against a number of enemies, from small insects to huge monsters. They really fit into the world and make you believe as if those creatures are actually living there, and not just random mobs placed into the maps by the leveldesigner. Most enemies are distinctively different from one another and require different tactics and weapons to defeat. Each level usually has a prevalent enemy type that makes up most of the population in that area, while the other, general types will take more of a backseat but are still there. The Skaarj, which you'll see throughout the game, come in about a dozen variations with varying stats and skins. Noteable is an AI that is impressive even today, almost two decades later. The pathfinding may let enemies find you even from far away through terrain that is difficult to navigate. Most enemies are reckless when at full health, and cautious when injured. Their ability to lead with projectiles as well as Skaarj's mobility and agility make for a formidable challenge on higher difficulties.
Unreal does have multiplayer, though it's probably hard to find online games after all these years. The multiplayer always seemed to lack
that ended up making it feel unfinished, though I could never point out exactly what that was. Perhaps it's the weapons which are designed to slay monsters, though they are still potent and perfectly capable of fragging players once you get good at the game. If you want to give multiplayer a more serious try, I'd suggest checking out Unreal Tournament, what's basically a polished version of the multiplayer released as a new game, and the best of its kind only challenged by Quake 3 Arena.
It's also possible to play with bots, and they give inexperienced players a good run for their money. Filling DmFith, DmHealPod or DmMorbias with 16 bots and just reveling in the carnage it would unfold kept me entertained for hours on end in a time when internet access wasn't readily available. It's definitely worth checking out.
I'd also like to mention that, on a technical level, Unreal could quite possibly be
most impressive game relative to release date, which makes a worthy history lession second only to Wolfenstein 3D. And if you had a 3dfx Voodoo card in 1998 you know exactly why. We were used to playing Duke3D and Quake when Unreal came along with its colored lightning, reflective surfaces, glow effects, volumetric lightning, and and and... it was eyecandy on a level that put Crysis to shame. Even the AI was and still is amazing, only really outdone by F.E.A.R.. And yet Unreal is more than a simple tech demo. It's actually a good game, solid in every aspect. And the first game that earned the right to call itself a "Quake killer". Did it kill Quake? No, but the attempt was more than respectable.
If you like FPS, you'll love Unreal. It's one of the best single-player FPS ever made, and a must-play for any shooting enthusiast. Its leveldesign, music, graphics and AI raised the bar in 1998 and still hold up today.

I do like the concept of the game and I want to make clear that this is not a bad game, it is however not a very good game either and I can't recommend it in its current state.
This game is a mixture of 3D Brawling and a pen & paper card game.
The p&p part is the "strategic" part of the game.
You navigate through a grid of cards which are spread out on a table, face down.
Each card represents a "step" and is revealed once selected, these cards tell a story and can have positive and negative effects. You can find equipment, be blessed, cursed, walk into traps or get assistance on your journey.
Once in a while you encounter opponents you need to fight which brings us to the combat.
You enter a tiny 3D combat arena, facing enemies specified by the card revealed.
The controls are limited to attack, stun and dodge, if you have a shield equipped you can additionally block ranged attacks and counter melee attacks. Combat usually takes about 30 seconds to a couple of minutes.
All this sounds great on paper but there is major caveat which runed my entire experience. The game is trivially easy or impossibly hard and unfair.
The campaigns can be completed by simply hitting "enter" all the time moving to the next card.
Your strategic choices hardly matter because combat is practically an extended QTE sequence. Block when you are told to block, counter when you are told to counter and tumble when you are told to tumble.
Since the combat is trivial, any choices you make improving your combat skills by buying weapons, armor and shields, seem irrelevant and of little consequence. After a while I simply stopped buying stuff, skipping any treasures or risky opportunites for improvement, since they are simply not required.
After a while the difficulty does indeed increase, however, not because more skill is required but simply because the combat is clunky and insufficient. You will encounter situation in which you will take damage no matter your equipment, because you are forced to react quicker than the games combat system allows you to do.
So again, your equipment and skill do not influence the combat but chance and luck are the dominant factors.
After the third or fourth campaign you are allowed to enter "Endless Mode" which does up the ante a bid since the cards no longer have to match your level of development. While challenge went up a bit, the meat of the game did not change, it is still playable by simply hitting "enter" all the time and having a small QTE sequence every now and then.
The game has potential, I do like the idea, but for now it is not worth 20 bucks.

Murdered: Soul Suspect is an adventure detective game, which was released in mid-2014 on PC, PS3, PS4, 360 and Xbox One. The game was developed by Airtight Games; which hadn't released anything worthwhile for a while before this game.
You play the role of detective Ronan O'Connor, based in a town called Salem in USA. The story is based around hunting down a serial killer by the name of "The Bell Killer". Ronan is killed by the serial killer at the beginning of the game and you are revived as a ghost and must find the killer before he can move on to the afterlife.
The game is played in a third person view as you wander around the town of Salem, the town is split into a couple of separate areas, such as churches, graveyards petrol stations etc. As you progress through the story, you learn a few different abilities, such as being able to teleport yourself short distances, being able to possess other living beings allowing you to read their minds or being able to influence their decisions in dialog scenes. The main game play element is solving the mystery of the killer; you do this by investigating the crime scenes for clues on the killer, and trying to predict their next move. This takes on a similar way of doing things as games like LA Noire has done; in that you have to find specific items of evidence scattered, and sometimes hidden around the crime scene in order for you to put them all together in order to resolve the scene. This can lead to quite a few moments of where you need to study all the evidence put in front of you in order to solve it giving it a real detective vibe.
On top of these detective scenes, there is a small element of combat in the game - as you are a ghost, living humans are not able to detect you; however the demon souls of the death world can. You have to remain hidden to these ghosts in shadows before being able to pounce out behind them to kill them by pressing a few key sequences in a small QTE - these combat scenes are very few and far between however and aren't really anything to rave about as they become very monotonous as you progress in the story.
Visually, Murdered: Soul Suspect looks nice. The whole game takes place in the time frame of one evening, so the darkness of night gives the game a very eerie feel to it. It doesn't have ultra-realistic graphics, but all of the characters are well animated. There are a couple of poor quality textures, however given that this is a sort of open world game, this can be forgiven somewhat.
The story in Murdered: Soul Suspect is something really special. From the opening scene, I was completely drawn into the plot and was able to fully immerse myself in this world being unfolded in front of me. As you progress, you come across other characters who aid Ronan in his efforts to solve the mystery and you grow attached to them too. The story is 100% linear though; there are no game changing decisions which you have to make which disappointed me slightly. But the overall plot which is being shown here is really interesting.
As this game is being categorized in the horror genre, I would of expected a little more from the sound effects, but I was let down by the fact that there isn't anything really that scary in Murdered: Soul Suspect; the scariest I came across was the demon's you encounter; and even they are tame and the lack of any jump scares or horrifying scenes was a let-down too. Every character you find in the game is fully voice acted to a high quality though. None of the voicing sounds off or cringy which is always a plus.
I found that there was next to zero levels of difficulty in Soul Suspect; the lack of any real combat leaves this game without any skill element, and is purely based on your ability to solve the crime scenes by finding the relevant clues - I was able to resolve all of the crime scenes with a 3 star rating 99% of the time (you are scored out of three). The hardest point I found has to be due to the game's controls which I will go into on the technical issues section of this review.
Murdered: Soul Suspect is a vast open world game; you are able to go wherever you want, whenever you want (within reason). There is absolutely tons of stuff to explore and investigate not related to the main plot. There are a number of side investigations you can complete in the early chapters, but these slowly become less and less common as you progress and focus more on the main plot. Another huge part of this game is finding the collectables; this has to be the game with the most collectables in I have ever played - there are hundreds to find.  Each level has its own version of collectable items, and there are also the overall games collectables which unveil even more about the main character's past, and information about the killer. Due to the fact that there are so many of these to find; I felt a little overwhelmed by trying to find them all and just sort of with the approach of picking any up which I come across whilst completing the investigations.
I finished Murdered: Soul Suspect in just over thirteen hours; this was with doing all of the side investigations, and collecting over a hundred collectables. I also took the time to playout all of the dialog options with all of the characters and spent a lot of time exploring the town of Salem. Sadly though; there is no reason what so ever to play through this game for a second time; you are not able to change the story in anyway nor are you able to ramp up the difficulty simply because there is no difficulty there in the first
I had a couple of technical problems whilst playing. Firstly I was playing on my high end rig, on 1080p settings and even though the majority of the time the frame rate was over 100 fps, it still felt like it was stuttering at times. I had to play with v-sync off because otherwise this locked gameplay to 30fps which looked horrendous. Cut scenes are also played out in 30fps in the game graphics, which makes the transitions between gameplay and cut scenes feel a little off too. The game's controls during the combat scenes also came across as clunky too; I often found myself not actually completing the QTE presented because it's not clear which buttons you have to press and what you can let go of which meant a lot of running and hiding from the demons due to failed attempts at killing them.  Finally the last issue I had was there are quite a few invisible walls to be found to, these often are in places where you would not expect them, leading to moments where you'll find you are suddenly floating in mid-air because you've walked into a wall and are trying to climb up it - this is something which can affect the immersion of the game and it's a shame that it is still in it given it's been out for well over a year now.
I am going to recommend Murdered: Soul Suspect; it has an amazing story which you really do need to experience in order to fully appreciate it, and has an original concept. The linear gameplay, lack of any many action scenes, and a couple of technical issues renders me unable to recommend it more than just that, a recommendation to play. The full price of £19, 99 is also slightly over marked too, so you may even want to wait for it to hit the sales before purchasing.

Murdered: Soul Suspect is by no means a great game, neither is it a bad game. It is relatively short; the storyline takes about 11 or so hours. As for those who have played Euro Truck Simulator 2, you will find this game to be very much similar. Truthfully, the only really noticeable differences would have to be the landscape(s), traffic, trucks, e.t.c. The performance and everything is slightly better, (in my case), and it was excellent to begin with in ETS2. I would highly recommend it to anyone who enjoyed the ETS series, and for anyone thinking of trying out the series for the first time.
As for the newcomers, keep in mind this is not a game designed for freeroaming, constantly popping in and out of any vehicle you want, or for professionally managing a business; it's a truck driving sim. You drive trucks under an employer until you make enough money to buy your own truck. From there on you haul various types of cargo to build your wealth. You then move on to expand your garage(s), buy more trucks, hire drivers, and make money. From a broad standpoint, yes it does simulate business, but that's not the primary goal of the game; it's for driving trucks.
Summary summed up: if you want to drive anything you please any time or manage a business from a professional standpoint, this game is not what you're hunting. If you want to drive a semi, (and make money doing so), haul lots of different things, and design trucks for your employees to drive, this is what you want.

I heard about the
series for a while now but never had the chance to play them until I finally picked them up off a
sale. There were many aspects I liked about the game as soon as I jumped in. Personally, I find that when you play a single player, first person shooter game, it can go one of two ways. Firstly it can either be a good mix of an action/first person shooter/and or adventure game, keeping one drawn in with various tasks, different sceneries, and things to do besides move and shoot. However, first person shooter games could just be that. With no real motivation to do any specific tasks you could quickly find yourself noticing all you do is move and shoot. I can tell you with ease that this isn't the case with
. I liked that the game kept it from feeling like most bad first person shooter games and instead followed my first description; various tasks, different scenarios and things to do. I also liked how the story had multiple endings, it added replayability to the game. Especially because you have to work through a single play through to get to one or the other of the endings. Possibly making your second play through different then your first. Amongst other things, I also really liked the weapon customization. It's always a better experience when you play a game and get to make things your own, i.e. naming characters, making decisions and or customizing things.
To be honest, there isn't a whole lot I don't like about this game. While usually I try to make sure I throw some points in for the other side of the argument, I honestly can't think of some genuine things that you could dislike about the game.
I don't like the outside segments and really the only reason for this is because of how perceptive you need to be
. What I mean by this is that the outside can be overwhelming your first time through. It'll seem like there's so much to explore and it'll seem like it'll be easy to miss something. Which it is. However, I don't feel as though this is a flaw in the gameplay and don't see this as a argument to be made not to buy the game.
Would I recommend this game? Yes! I feel as though it's one of the better (if not best) first person shooter games I've played in a long time. I like the stealth mixed into the gameplay. Personally, I'm always a huge fan of stealth so that was a big thing for me. I liked the weapon customization along with the story. The moral choices and the alternate endings are a plus as well as it adds on replayability.

The game does have nudity in two levels that you can't skip by and can't select an option for it not to be. As much as I don't have a problem with this, I feel as though it should be included in this review!

For those of you who have never played Disgaea, this is a tile based RPG. You do have to strategize for some stages, but most of the time, you can just go into a level and grind.
When you encounter them in a stage, geo panels are important to pay attention to. You can tip any map in your favor. If you plan on using the optional Item World to level up items, you should be preapred to encounter several geo panels.
The geo panels are randomized, much like the levels themselves. Meaning that all you need to do is pay attention and act accordingly. For example, if you want your character to stay put until the next turn after moving as far as you can, you shouldn't put them on a warp panel.
Other than the geo panels, there isn't much strategy involved in the levels. Height differences between characters don't seem to have much of an impact on attack or defense.
The pace of the game is casual and there are a few really challenging stages. But if you're ever having difficulty on finding a good grinding spot, or you're just stuck in general, there are so many good walkthroughs online.
Once a stage feels too easy, I like lifting monsters and throwing them on other monsters to create monsters of a higher level. You can do this until you are getting your butt whopped. It is a great way to level characters quickly, so long as you can handle it.
Stages are infinitely replayable. So if you find a grinding stage that you love, you can contrinue replaying it. This is fantastic because mid-way through the game it is going to get harder to progress. Each chapter usually gives one new grinding stage that will allow you to keep your characters ahead of the game.

I'm still working my way through the introduction of the game (haven't gotten past the first city), but so far I'm loving it! I'm playing on the Classic difficulty, and there are two difficulties higher than this one.  My characters are now level 7, but this is still an early review, as I have yet to complete act 1.
Pros:
1.) Combat is incredibly tactical. There have been a couple of fights where I got my butt handed to me because I didn't think to exploit the terrain or the destructibles placed in the battlefield.  Height matters a lot more in this game, especially if you have a huntsman.
2.) Oddly, the soundscape is amazing.  Walking through town you can hear the bustling of people walking around. It sounds great when you're in a dungeon, along the beach, and everywhere.
3.) Voiceovers, world building, and characters has been spot on so far.  I have found some characters to be really funny, and others to be incredibly intriguing, such as Losche.
4.) The game doesn't prevent you from doing things out of order.  Once you escape from Fort Joy, it really opens up and allows you to wander around the map in any direction.
Cons:
1.) Don't get me wrong, the UI is pretty well done in this game.  However, there are some UI'isms that I would like improved.  Such as being able to send all of my "wares" to one character (who has the highest bartering skill).
2.) Saved game bloat bug.  Right now there is an issue with saved games getting extremely bloated to the point where it can take a long time for my computer to upload the saved games to the cloud.
Closing Thoughts:
This is definitely a CRPG that has had a lot of love and time put into it.  It will ask a lot of you (time wise) to get going, but so far, it has been a really enjoyable ride!  I definitely recommend it so far, and I will update as I get further into the game.

First thing to say is this game has some solid ideas for the MMO genre such as the in depth crafting system, ownable land (have to pay a subscription) and naval combat but it is overshadowed by systems that are designed to force the player into paying money to be competitive in pvp.
One system is labor which is a very slow regenerating resource that is used for everything from crafting to gathering to opening coinpurses, yes monsters don't drop gold, they drop coinpurses that require labor to open.  If you run out of labor it is extremely limiting in what you can do but guess what.  If you pay a monthly subscription you can regenerate more labor offline and online and you can even buy labor potions with real life money...that alone is pay to win.
In addition to labor being an unnecessary annoyance the best gear in the game is crafted.  And there is another component to getting the best gear that requires luck in gambling or as people like to call it "RNG".  This comes into play in the regrading and socketing systems.  You use a regrade scroll to try to get from say celestial to divine in weapon or armor that jumps the gear's stats.  One thing to note is at the higher tiers gear can break at a regrade attempt!  These chances are extremely low at the higher tiers and people will generally get charms that can increase your chances.  Someone ends up having to pay real life money (p2w) to bring these charms into the economy.  There is also luck involved in socketing gems into gear and anything after 1 gem has a chance of breaking all the gems in that gear.  Does this sound like fun to you?  Didn't think so
You can have someone come into this game with literally no playtime and buy their way to the top by buying APEX, selling for gold and buying the best gear in the game since the best gear is craftable.  If this isn't pay to win I don't know what is.  This is a perfect example of overly greedy companies destroying good ideas and it is a trend that seems to be prevalent in many mmos as of late (I'm looking at you ESO).  And the only people who defend this are the ones who spend an ungodly amount of money on the game and don't want to feel like a sucker (buyer's remorse) or apologists for a company that doesn't care about them.  It's people like these that reward shady business practices and they are a blight on the gaming community.  Well, I think the gaming community deserves better.  The second a sandbox MMO with equal graphics and some of the better ideas of Archeage comes out without soul sucking systems such as labor or RNG in crafting Archeage will die.  ♥♥♥♥ this game

I wanted to really love this game, but I feel like there is some big room for improvement.
First, I must say that the concept is great. It makes for interesting and variable playthrough. I think with a few improvements this could easily turn into one of my favourite games.
So the big problem I had is that the combat became very dull and one dimensional about halfway through the game. I felt like as soon once the number on enemies faced in each combat scenario got high enough I ended up just tapping the counter key constantly and could not do much else, and without a shield the was no hope of completing more than a couple of combat scenarios.
The deck also started to feel unbalanced partway through the game, which I suppose added to the difficulty, but it seemed like too many cards had a 75% failure or epic failure chance with signifcant consequences and samll chance of reqrd, which was frustrating at times.
I think encorporating a bit of dungeon crawling could really liven things up as well. Rather than just being thrust into an arena for each combat, creating a larger level where you could approach the enemies and the combat situation in multiple ways would really improve the gameplay.
I am a bit torn about recommending or not recommending this game; I still think it is an interesting concept and worth a playthrough, but there is definitely a lot of room for improvement.

Let me start by getting this out in the open: This game is not for everybody. In fact, the list of things wrong with the game seemingly far outweighs the good, but for some reason, this game really struck a chord for me, and honestly has become one of my favorites.
It's a pretty tight experience, fitting a decent amount of narrative into a relatively short (~7-10 hours) game. Most of the game plays like an adventure game, you wandering around a hub area collecting clues and then linking them together with an in game system. Unfortunately, the game REALLY holds your hand during these parts. There were a couple times throughout the game where I felt a little cheated by the solving aspect; it isn't hard at all, just sometimes a little nonsensical. Apart from the investigations, exploring is rewarded with a decent amount of collectible objects spread around, as well as little notes with bits of story on them. Very fun, slightly spooky and mysterious, but ultimately casual gameplay, which might turn some off.
Then there are the action sequences.. For some silly reason the developers decided to toss in some minor combat and running mechanics against enemies, usually at least a few per section. They provide no real challenge, and are really just an annoying distraction from the bread and butter of the game. Mechanically, they usually function to push you in a direction, but really end up taking away from the final product. Luckily they aren't featured -too- heavily, and are in most cases fairly short bits.
All in all, I do recommend this game, just be aware that it doesn't play quite like what  you would expect going into it, and that it really is a very simple game with a few annoying parts. The atmosphere and music are both very solid, and the story is pretty cool, if a little predictable. The worst part of the visual aspect is that the main character is wearing that stupid ****ing hat.

Unreal Gold is an Action FPS game that runs on the original engine of the same name (The Unreal engine). To this day it haunts my dreams with it's large open maps, complex level design, and stunning graphics (for its time). You can't go wrong if you are into older FPS games and this game has always stood out and been unique.
This particular Edition comes with the Return to Na Pali expansion (Which is lower quality imho, but it's still worth a playthrough.)
It features a lot of pretty unique weapons, all designed to show off different aspects of what the engine could do, and they end up being so different that it's actually refreshing. The levels and environments are also varied and interesting. Some of the levels in this game are seriously impressive (I'm looking at you, sunspire). The game is still pretty damn pleasing to look at as well, despite it's lack of polygons and lower res textures, the level design really makes great use of the engine and puts a lot of other 3D shooters of the day to shame.
Where I feel this game really excels above all else, is it's music. It has some of the best video game music I've ever had the pleasure of hearing. Seriously it's an amazing soundtrack, check it out, especially if you like Alexander Brandon.
The game does have a story, but  it's not shoved down your throat. Instead it's told through a universal translator item you obtain near the start of the game, it will pick up various messages from dead bodies, books, computer terminals, and can be read to learn about the world and characters in it. The translator also often tells you what a switch does or provides important clues to progressing (This game can be a bit troublesome to navigate compared to most of the linear games we get these days).
Return to Na Pali actually has some "cutscenes" that are basically monologue of the main character over a section of the map, these can be skipped and some of them weren't even working for my last playthrough.
So now for the downside, this game has some crashing problems, and by some, I mean a lot! There is a good community made patch that you really should seek out before playing, as it removes a vast majority of the crashes.
tl;dr: Awesome and unique FPS with a lot of variety in weapons and environments and some of the best music I've ever heard.

If you have not yet played a Disgaea game then buy this game! Although it's lacking many of the gameplay conviniences provided by the sequels this game has without a doubt the best soundtrack and story in the series. Disgaea is a strategy JRPG where you spend A LOT of your time leveling up gear, units, skills, discovering new classes, and upgrading gear and weapons to make your team as overpowered as possible.
Even if you don't like Anime the game is packed with super funny moments and it also tackles greater moral values about the perception of good and evil. The main character is a demon prince named Laharl who sets out to prove himself as the new overlord after finding out his father King Krichevskoy had passed away from choking on a pretzel. He is accompanied by an untrustworthy vassal, Etna and a love freak Angel, Flonne who was sent to the netherworld to assasinate the already dead Overlord.
Gameplay wise it's a grid based rpg reminiscent of games like  Final Fantasy Tactics or Fire Emblem. But what Disgaea does differently and what makes it so great is the freedom and customization to do whatever you want with your characters. While some classes are more proficient in the speed they learn skills with certain weapon types than others, you can teach any class to use any weapon. Want to make a thief that uses a sword rather than a gun in order to train faster in the long run? It will take some extra  time at first but go for it. Want to teach your Magic Knight every elemental spells in the game? Then research the mentor system.
I recommend not reading too much into starter tips and just to test out all the classes and monsters for yourself. Once you reach the endgame is where you really start to need online help and strategy guides.
So if you're looking for a good time killer looking no further than Disgaea. I've unregrettably spent hundreds of hours on this series. If you have a Playstation 3,4, or Vita there are even better Disgaea games. I prefer this game to be handheld but console/PC is just as good.
Please release more DIsgaea ports!

I haven't played Ark or Rust (which everyone else is comparing this game to), but I have played (and enjoyed) 7 Days to Die.
I like what this could be more than I like 7 Days to Die.
There are optimization and animation issues, but it's early access. That excuse will only stand for another two or three weeks.
So, I'll address things that I don't think are necessarily bugs:
- Blocking is unresponsive and useless
- Gear breaks way too quickly, and it takes like 12 bars to repair a sword that shouldn't even comprise that much iron
- Monsters teleport
- Archery sucks. Can't shoot through windows and building block hitboxes (especially fences) are out of whack.
- Character progression could use more choices, like a perk system, rather than just attributes and recipes.
- NPCs are dumber than the shipping container of rocks it took to build your wheel of pain. Archer thralls will stand on your walls and shoot arrows in the direction of their target even if there's an obstacle in the way. If that obstacle happens to be you, they will shoot you, and it will hurt. Melee thralls will wander around and sheathe/unsheathe weapons over and over and never attack enemies.
~Recipes are earned by levelling up; I would rather they were found in the world, as in the aforementioned zombie game.
Pros:
+ Graphics are good enough
+ Character customization
+ Melee combat, once they work out the kinks, will be pretty solid (archery needs an overhaul), however simple.
+ Building is easy, block types allow for varied structures
+ It's just fun
EDIT/UPDATE:
After playing for however many hours I'm up to now, I still recommend this game, but singleplayer "endgame" is lacking. Once you've got your castle and your thralls there's nothing left to do. I hope, once they get this game out of the mire of bugs and performance issues, Funcom adds some kind of NPC raids so you can see your castle in action. Obviously, in MP you won't have this issue, as long as you have competitors.

Early Access should only be for indie developers, not a large scale publisher like Funcom who should actually have the time and capital to finish a game before releasing it to the public. You guys got greedy.
I attempted to play this for roughly 86 minutes before getting a refund. Beyond a couple crashes and some Lefty-unfriendly keybind problems that forced me to use a controller, the game simply failed to hook me. It's unpolished, slow-paced, and just plain boring in it's current state.
Seeing as the focus was on the multiplayer aspect, something I just don't do anymore, it leaves the single player mode aimless and uninteresting. If a game offers both modes of play, it has to be able to stand up on it's own with it's single player experience. In this case, the single player mode is currently like Conan dying on the Tree of Woe except Subotai is nowhere in sight to rescue him.
I can only recommend this to die-hard Conan and/or open-world survival fans willing to patiently sit and wait for Funcom to actually finish this because you believe in the potential of the product. Everyone else, steer clear. Check on it again in 4 months. If it hasn't made significant progress by then, then it's probably a lost cause.

Unreal Gold is simply one of the best First Person Shooters that I've ever played. Unreal Gold is an updated version of Unreal, which was released in 1998 among other FPS classics. Unreal is pretty much what happened when Epic Games looked at Quake 2 and said "Yeah that's good and all, but what if we did that, with awesome graphics (for the time), exelent lighting, a unique weapon lineup, and an amazing soundtrack?" And from that, Unreal was born. In Unreal, you go around from map to map (which are generally really huge), fighting an alien race known as the Skarjj, while occasionally helping out another alien race known as the Nali. Unreal has amazing variety in the themes of levels, one minute you're in a crashed prison ship, the next you're in a mountain area, and then the next you're in a mine, and it keeps going on, introducing new and varied areas. Unreal also has an amazing soundtrack, who it's composer would later work on games like Deus Ex. I love the soundtrack in this game, as it has inspired other soundtracks from games that arn't even in the same genre (Freedom Planet for example). The graphics have aged decently. While the texture quality and low poly enviorments and NPCs look bad by today's standards, the lighting in this game is absolutely amazing, and puts other games with great lighting like System Shock 2 to shame. Unreal also has AI which is extremely impressive, even to this day, that almost moves around like another player at times. Unreal's biggest strength however, lies in it's unique weapon lineup, which inclueds the Upgradable Energy Pistol, The Razorjack, The Bio Launcher, and The Flak Cannon to name a few of the awesome weapons. If I had to choose a favorite weapon, it would probably be the Flak Cannon, as it gives a satisfying punch to when you shoot an enemy at point blank. I don't have too many problems with this game to be honest. If I had to nitpick any problems, it would probably be that you do move a bit too slow for my liking, and that sometimes these maps can be extremely confusing to first time players. I also really didn't like the Return To Na Pali expansion included, as many of the changes made to it break the fundamentals of Unreal, and it just doesn't hold up too well. If you like old school FPS games, then Unreal Gold is a game that you should play before you die. I highly reccomend patching the game with The OId Unreal patch, that fixes many bugs the game had, and allows you to run the game in modern resolutions. It's completely Unreal that a first person shooter like is this awesome. If you're a fan of Old School first person shooters, or even FPS games in general, then I reccomend you check this one out. In 1998, Epic Games brought us the original Unreal. The game was unlike anything PC gamers had seen before, it had innovative weapons, beautiful graphics (for the time), and a very complex story that some people thought was boring, while others found it worthy of a literature adaptation. But with Unreal Gold, you can experince this game in the way it was truly ment to be played. This package not only contains a slightly modified version of the original 1998 game, but it also contains an expansion pack that practically continues the story of the original Unreal game, this expansion pack goes by the name of The Return to Na Pali. In all seriousness The Return to Na Pali is a really good expansion pack (albeit shorter than the original game) that contains new weapons, enemies, and levels (obviously). I must warn you that the original Unreal and The Return to Na Pali are quite possibly the hardest FPS games you will ever play in your life. Seriously, there were some levels in these games in which I died more than 10 times.  But don't let the difficulty scare you, Unreal Gold is a compilation that every FPS game fan should have in their possesion. This compilation is totally......UNREAL!!!!  P.S. This game contains realistic violence and gore. Gamer discretion is strongly advised.

I made a video review for this game, it can be seen here:
Long story short, one of my favorite games of all time. Not much bad to say about it, but it's not without a few faults. Near perfect.

The story that was attached to the game was ok, some might even say good.  The problem is, most of the story is covered in the over 200 artifacts that you collect.  We're not talking about audio logs like Bioshock where you can hear that part of the story right away. Instead these story parts are tucked away in the menu for you to open and read.
The game only has one type of enemy which you can either sneak by, or if you feel like it you can kill it.  This would be less of an issue if other aspects of the game made up for it.  I guess the problem is, as a ghost in a human world there's not a lot to stop you.
On the upside I had little to no technical issues with the game. Graphics were fine, control was fine, camera was mostly fine. But there were no bosses or hellish netherworlds to navigate - nothing to stand out. Even when people ascended to heaven it wasn't very interesting.
With no challenge, no replay value, an ok storyline that might keep you busy around 6 hours at most... I can't really recommend it.  For folks out there that really like ghost stories or detective type games (I do!), this might make the game a bit more palatable, but overall wasn't worth it to me.

Pros:

Cons:

To be clear this isn't a bad game however when compared with Euro Truck sim 2 it’s hard to recommend this game over it. If you’re an American this may be different but the appeal to me is to drive around with my truck following the laws of the road and enjoying myself. I know that many people won’t enjoy this style of game, but then again I don’t enjoy Fifa (other football and sport games are available).
The game looks much better than European truck simulator the cities and even down to small details such as cracks in the road. At the end of a job the parking process is much better as you get to choose how you want to park selecting from what is effectively; hard, medium and don’t park. The increase in fuel stations is good as in euro truck you could only buy fuel in a city if you had a garage upgraded. The coast roads look absolutely incredible (but with faster trucks in euro truck would be more fun there).
I know more trucks and roads are coming but I find myself thinking why don’t I just play euro truck instead? The current engines available are low on power and the GPS likes taking you down extremely small roads. Also The game makes the ‘highways’ have more bends in them than the motorways in Britain and Europe. The police surprise attack you every moment you are speeding and they are very sneaky arriving just after a 30 sign that I happen to miss seeing. When you finally crawl up to speed on a ‘highway’ you are forced to slow down as the road just arrives in a city or town that you have no idea about until you either get fined for speeding or crash into cars waiting for traffic lights!!!
In conclusion although American truck Simulator is a good simulator I still feel like Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a better game. On euro truck I have put in 110+ hours (had none steam version for a while) and I have experienced that game to about the full whereas American truck simulator I only have about 3 hours of which I know isn’t a lot but still it is difficult for me to recommend.
So in it's current state I cannot recommend this game, with more trucks and roads in future this may alter my view.
*Disclaimer*
I know more trucks and roads are coming and I know that you can get mods for removing the police and increasing engine sizes but I wanted to play this game properly but despite this I wasn’t levelling up very quickly and I wanted to see what truck options were available so I had to use an XP cheat mod so I could see the options.
Edit:
The traffic light situation was improved but the game still isn't as good as ETS2

at a little over 351 hours I write this review, having spent about a week running through the really scenic and engaging main storyline and other questlines that give you the chance to explore and understand the depth of each region. I have played about 100 hours in the alpha, which a lot of the current negative reviews are stemming from.(Oh no, an as-yet unreleased game has issues, better go sign off on it being bad before they fix 'em)
I have about 250 hours post-release and 350 hours in-game total. In this time I have;
o Bred polar Bears on a farm
o Stolen money-pouches from nearly every living non-player thing in sight
o Crafted extremely intricate and time-intensive pieces of gear, items, food, drink, potions, gems, jewelry, ships, wagons, rowboats, mounted ship weapons, and many other awesome things that REALLY matter in-game. your name is on that gear forever, so you can make a name for yourself.
o Sunk someone's battleship.
o Caught a huge marlin while waiting for a war to end in an area I wanted to trade in.
o traded goods and services across the continent and across the sea for great profit.
o Crushed my enemies, and seen them driven before me while listening to the lamentations of their women.
o waged a war between ghost armies of long-dead kingdoms who haven't yet given up the fight.
o picked archeum from the branches of a snooty tree who only drinks designer water imported from scenic Auroria, literally thousands of miles away.
o tutored players learning the ropes and helped them on their quests while being rewarded for the task handsomely.
o drank literally enough fruit punch to give one-eighth of Africa Diabetes.
o had a running battle against pirates trying to steal tradepacks from a friend's caravan. It was intense and they made off with one.
o Built a house in a scenic dusty plain with ocean view and access to a main trade route, and proceeded to fill it with the exploits of my adventuring days that I continue to accrue, as well as a handsome painting of myself.
If you want an MMO that is MMO in every sense of the word, doesnt require a subscription to keep playing, has an extremely sandboxy feel to it, and has equal depth in both PVP and PVE content with regular update releases that YOU DONT HAVE TO BUY TO HAVE ACCESS TO(ahem, WoW/EQ/EQ2/etc) along with an active moderator community, this is the game for you. you may live your fantasy life how you wish, and can access everything on one character without making alts to drastically change your playstyle because each of the skillsets you use(you may have 3 active at once and build your overall class' skillset from there) levels independantly from you. with enough time you could swap in and out of every role, but you could still only use 3 skillsets at one time allowing for extremely in-depth customization of what your character can do exactly, and that is expanded each time the level cap is raised, leaving new options open for what can be done. I would recommend this game to anyone who wants to live in an MMO fantasy world that values the player-driven content in a sandbox environment where you can accomplish much more solo than say, EVE, and much more with a group than, say, WoW

One the most fun games I've seen in quite a while,
a game that explore a rarely touched aspect of RPGs and do so very well.
PROS:
* well-designed trading system with a lot of depth to it.
* a simple yet fun combat system that doesn't overshadow the main focus of the game.
* very good writing, made me genuinely laugh more than a couple of times.
* the goals system is pressuring but not actually too hard, and very different than the dangers depicted in other games.
CONS:
* ranged attacks only fire in four directions, wouldn't hurt in a turn based system, but that is not the case here.
* while the goals are manageable and generally a good feature, it leaves little room for the experimentation I feel needed with such a unique game system.
* lack of camera control in dungeons, not too bad but sometimes items/enemies get behind some of the scenery and its kind of annoying.
in short, not perfect but tons of fun and highly recommended.

I like to blame this game for ruining my childhood as it came with the first computer my family purchased and thus sealed my fate as a gamer for years to come.
I remember opening the box and hooking up my Gateway 2000 and installing Unreal. It was one of the earliest forms of awe I can recall when I was navigating through the wreckage of the prison ship and going outside onto an alien planet to confront brutes and skaarj and all the other nasty crap. The story was pretty neat, the graphics, at the time, were awesome. The mechanics were, and still are, pretty solid. This series, including the follow up Unreal Tournament, were easily one of my favorite games to play as a child and experiencing it again as an adult took me down nostalgia avenue and socked me right in the feels.
The action, again, feels smooth and the fights all feel pretty visceral as you blow your enemies to chunks. The environment is as much fun to look at as it is deadly because among being a great FPS it's also got some decent platformer elements combined with some slight puzzle solving areas. Keep in mind none of this is really too difficult but some secret areas can be accessed for more loot or plasma pistol upgrades which really go a long way to making the end game less difficult. As you go through the levels you will find data pads or letters or messages that sort of reveal parts of the story as well as adding some depth to some of the weird scenes you come across. Bodies laying around a room full of guns or some lone crates with chunks of what used to be people beside it tell a story which really adds a lot of immersion to your playthrough.
My only real issue with the game is that some of the graphical settings don't seem to really work but this could just be my machine. Brightness and screen size seem to be constant issues. The only setting that seems to work without issues is 800x600 which is fine, but since I can't really adjust the brigthness level and it seems too dark. Minor gripe for a great classic game.

SHORT VERSION OF REVIEW:
This is a great game that can last you as long as you want it to, and even far beyond that (trust me, I CAN NOT stop playing this game, even with as many hours as I have). Whether you pay full price or pick up this title on a 90% sale, I can guarantee you will be more than satisfied with getting far more than your money's worth. The only way a person could really dislike this game is if they don't give it enough of a chance (this is one of those games that's very easy to give up on at first), or if it's simply just not the type of game that's suitable for that person. [READ ON FOR MORE DETAILS]
INFORMATION ON CLASSES:
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare has 4, well-balanced classes that allow for a wide variety of playstyles per person. There are 2 heavily armored classes, the Knight and the Vanguard, and there are 2 light armor classes, the Man-At-Arms and the Archer.
The Knight class is the most heavily armored class (which means most HP) with a variety of deadly, high damage hammers, axes, swords, and flails (ball and chain) of both the one and two-handed variety, at his disposal.
The Vanguard, noticably less armored than the knight, specializes in polearms, with all of his weapons being very lengthy and high-damage. Swords, bardiche, halberd, billhook, variety of thrusting spears, polehammer; with these weapons, the vanguard class allows you to stay out of reach of your opponents attacks whilst you seemlessly decapitate them, whereas the Knight class's weapons force you to get up close and personal. The Vanguard is the only class that can not equip a shield.
The Man-At-Arms; master of evasion, equipped with the unique dodge ability that, if timed well, can evade an enemy's attack with ease, while at the same time, opens an oppurtunity for a counter attack. The Man-At-Arms is equipped a variety of one-handed swords, axes and hammers (the same weapons as the Knight's secondaries), as well as a two-handed quarterstaff. The MAA's lack of HP is made up for by his speed and agility that, if utilized properly, can overwhelm any class.
And finally the Archer... those pesky archers... with a weapon choice between bows, crossbows, and throwing spears/javelins of varying speeds and damage, the archer can range and pick off their opponents, especially those who are wounded or distracted. On the flip side of their ranging abilities, the archer is at a disadvantage in melee combat due to its very low-damage melee weapons and miniscule HP.
GAME MODE INFO:
Chivalry offers a variety of official game modes including but not limited to; Team Objective (within this game mode there is a wide variety of objectives that vary between defense and offense, Ex: Tainting the enemy's water supply by dumping a cart-load of corpses into it.), Team Deathmatch, Last Team Standing, and Free-For-All. There are also dueling servers available for sharpening up on your skills. In team-based game modes, you have the option of siding with the Agatha Knights (blue, gold,white), or the Mason Order (Red & Black). The Mason Order, once part of Agatha, are a rebelling force fighting for freedom of Agatha's rule and fighting for power.

Pretty much ETS2 with American trucks and a smaller, but highly detailed map. You play as a truck driver who has no cash, no truck, nothing. You do quick jobs by driving for other companies till you can afford your own truck. Once you own a truck, you are free to explore and discover cities where you can find pickup and drop off points for trailers, truck dealers, recruitment agencies, and more.
Once you've earned a considerable amount of cash, you can upgrade our garage and buy additional trucks and hire drivers for added income. You can buy more garages in different cities to further expand your business.
Pros:
- Very vibrant and beautiful graphics
- Easy to use interface (Carried over from ETS2)
- Highly detailed map with excellent attention to detail
- Highly detailed trucks with interior
- Realistic Driving physics
- Realistic Driving laws
- Simple to use Sat Nav
- Controller, wheel, joystick support
- Mods support
- Photomode and World of Trucks
- Multiplayer mod (Truckers MP)
Cons:
- Very poor optimization; you may need a good GPU to run smoothly
- Small map (Free & Paid Expansions soon to come)
- Limited truck selection (More to come within the next few months)
- Daft AI (Similar to ETS2)
- Police cars spawn too often and are not forgiving when speeding
- Spawn rate of certain AI cars are unrealistic
- Lack of slip roads on freeway intersections
- Horn sounds like a computer making error noises

I gotta admit, I did not expect this. This is a unique game to be honest, because it surprised me, a whole lot.
Imma do it like they all do, cus it's easier to understand reviews, so here:
PROS:
-An unique experience (for now)
There aren't many games with it's concept being you die and become a ghost solving your murder (not really a spoiler, because the title spoils it all then), and this one is from my perspective done exceptionally well.
-Voice Quality
I can't say this is the best voice quality I heard, but the voice is mixed and put together, doing its job of keeping you on your toes, really well.
-Graphics
For the graphics maniacs and the graphicsrexics this is a meet down the middle. For its scenery and location, the graphics fit really good, since it gives this dark, mysterious vibe with a dash of detectiveness.
-Story
Oh. I absolutely loved the story (I haven't finished it yet (at about 7,5 hrs right now) but I know I'll be too lazy to edit this review, but I know I'll love it, so y'know), and some moments in it are a really well done,unique, some other important adjective of a moment. It's what it is - great.
-Demons
Well, I wasn't really expecting them and I was scared sh*tless at first (still am at times ;D), but you get used to them. They offer a new type of enemy, but in an interesting form, making it something you probably won't see soon.
-Clues
These little sons'a'b*tches are tricky but fo' real entertaining and I think that with time I started enjoying myself, when I got the answers to various questions about, ''why this happened'', ''why that happened'' and them putting them together, reminds me of Sherlock Holmes in a way, yet unclear to me. Checking IGN guides on where stuff is also happens quite often (often being almost everytime).
-Collectibles
A lot of em. A lot. Which is good (?), but what's even better is, that at any time when you're in the town, you can go to various interiors (since collectibles are more or less spread out across interiors), and collect the ones you might've missed.
CONS:
-There aren't any cons
I enjoyed it, and the achievements make for some work, but you get the hang of it.
Also, when this first came out, I was oh-so-not interested in it, but after time (time being about a year later), it was on sale and I said ''why not''.
P.S I don't think I regret it.  (1murderedcop/10)

To be clear this isn't a bad game however when compared with Euro Truck sim 2 it’s hard to recommend this game over it. If you’re an American this may be different but the appeal to me is to drive around with my truck following the laws of the road and enjoying myself. I know that many people won’t enjoy this style of game, but then again I don’t enjoy Fifa (other football and sport games are available).
The game looks much better than European truck simulator the cities and even down to small details such as cracks in the road. At the end of a job the parking process is much better as you get to choose how you want to park selecting from what is effectively; hard, medium and don’t park. The increase in fuel stations is good as in euro truck you could only buy fuel in a city if you had a garage upgraded. The coast roads look absolutely incredible (but with faster trucks in euro truck would be more fun there).
I know more trucks and roads are coming but I find myself thinking why don’t I just play euro truck instead? The current engines available are low on power and the GPS likes taking you down extremely small roads. Also The game makes the ‘highways’ have more bends in them than the motorways in Britain and Europe. The police surprise attack you every moment you are speeding and they are very sneaky arriving just after a 30 sign that I happen to miss seeing. When you finally crawl up to speed on a ‘highway’ you are forced to slow down as the road just arrives in a city or town that you have no idea about until you either get fined for speeding or crash into cars waiting for traffic lights!!!
In conclusion although American truck Simulator is a good simulator I still feel like Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a better game. On euro truck I have put in 110+ hours (had none steam version for a while) and I have experienced that game to about the full whereas American truck simulator I only have about 3 hours of which I know isn’t a lot but still it is difficult for me to recommend.
So in it's current state I cannot recommend this game, with more trucks and roads in future this may alter my view.
*Disclaimer*
I know more trucks and roads are coming and I know that you can get mods for removing the police and increasing engine sizes but I wanted to play this game properly but despite this I wasn’t levelling up very quickly and I wanted to see what truck options were available so I had to use an XP cheat mod so I could see the options.
Edit:
The traffic light situation was improved but the game still isn't as good as ETS2

One of the greatest games ever made.
Combat targeting is a bit annoying with mouse + keyboard (no controller support) but it gets easier to deal with the longer you play. The rest of the controls are good.
Graphics are still good for their age (in my opinion), the comical art style helps it age well. The level design is memorable and the music is amazing. The characters are wonderfully styled, characters all have unique proportions like big hands and feet compared to the rest of their body. Guards have their caps pulled down over their eyes for a stern look, traders wear goofy tall hats, Thunder is a giant warrior.
It's great fun watching your own character change as you progress through the game. You become older, more battle hardened, taller and more buff. You have full control over how good or evil your character is and your actions/appearance affect how the world views you. Later quests allow you to make some pretty major moral choices which is nice.
The XP and levelling system is simple which is nice. It's quick and easy to level your character based on your playstyle, you don't have to dedicate yourself to one thing. You've got melee weapons, bows, and spells and you can use them all however you like.
This is definitely a game everyone should play at least once. Doesn't matter how old it is, it's a classic now. There's plenty to do in the game for a long single playthrough but it also has replayability if you want to try being the opposite of good/bad or inbetween.

EDIT 2017-12-17  I am happy to report that my earlier problems with black screen computer freezing upon exit of game have disappeared.  The problem was with my GPU driver.  Once I updated my graphics card drivers the problem went away.  I have changed my review to positive and can't wait to really enjoy this game now that I have no problems.
---------------------------------------
I wanted to like this game.  I've been a fan of Koei's ROTK series for many many years.  I even own the Japanese language versions of ROTK even though I don't speak the language.  In other words I'm comfortable with playing games like this.
Three Kingdoms: The Last Warlord reminds me very much of  the Koei series on the same subject.  This game definitely has a Chinese flavor to it that I find fascinating.  One can clearly see the difference between Japanese style games and Chinese style games.  I'm enjoying that aspect of this game.  Yes it would be helpful to have a manual instruction book in English because not all of the concepts in this game are easy to understand.  I'm sure there will be one available as this is an early access game with a small team putting it together.
It pains me however to give a negative vote for this game simply because of one glaring problem I'm having that no one else has mentioned.  The game plays fine for me when I start it up.  Very stable both on the strategy map and the battle map.  Where I'm having a problem is trying to exit the game.  When I press the 'Quit game' button my computer screens goes black and my system becomes unresponsive.  I cannot even Ctrl-Alt-Del to recover.  Instead I have to power cycle my computer and deal with disk drive scans upon restart every time I play this game.  I have spent the past 2 weeks trying to figure out what is happening but I can't find any problem.  No game has ever given me this kind of problem.  I will change my recommendation if this problem is fixed.

Get ready to experience the latest and greatest psychological horror game in the infamous "Professor Teaches" series! This time, the player is tossed into the terrifying world of PowerPoint 2013. The gameplay, format, and pacing remains true to its predecessors, so veterans will feel right at home, and newcomers will have no problem quickly getting in on the action!
When this brilliant choose-your-own-adventure style game begins, you'll find yourself face-to-face with some crucial options that will affect the final conclusion of the game in a creative and profound way. You'll be faced with the daunting and sometimes intimidating task of selecting your path from choices such as the "Main Menu", "How to Use This Course", "Legal Notes", "Index", and "Glossary".
The "Main Menu" options start you down the main storyline of the game, while the remaining options serve as tutorials and preparation for the horrors ahead. Throughout the main game you'll be greeted, taunted, and even chastised often by the booming voice of God himself, as he leads you through the main story, testing you and timing you as you complete the critical tasks necessary to escape from the dark and twisted world of PowerPoint 2013. Only those who can endure this pain and push through to the end will be granted their freedom, and subsequently the satisfaction of having completed one of the top psychologically jaunting experiences available on any modern gaming platform.
Will you be victorious? Or will you fall victim to the greatest evil?
It's highly recommended that you play this late at night, in the dark, and with your headphones cranked for the best experience.
