It's like Ark, but darker. Building is better, but the game as a whole is quite early-early access. Animations are not the best, stuff sometimes just appear out of thin air and there are bugs. Regardless, whoever likes Ark can find like 70% their things here.

Imagine if Alexander the Great's empire hadn't collapsed, but managed to hold onto and encompass everything east of the Ural Mountains. Then in the 1930s, the Emperor becomes Hitler sans Final Solution and starts World War II. Oh, and there's magic-based nukes and a legendary race of sexy Jedi ladies (no I'm not making that up). Thus is the world of Valkyria Chronicles.
It's hard to give this game a recommendation. As much as I'm enjoying the gameplay, there's so many little problems with the mechanics that add up to a big leech on that enjoyment. First and foremost is the lack of saving during battles. This wouldn't be an issue if the gameplay were faster, or at least more fluid. Even in the early game, one battle can take well over an hour to finish. Sometimes you just don't have that much time to waste on a game. A simple addition of checkpoint saves would have taken care of the problem nicely. Alas, you must slog through each battle start to finish. Because JRPG, I guess.
Secondly, the cover system is a joke. Why only sandbag barricades? Why can't I crouch behind a waist-high crate? WHY, GAME???
Third, grenades are an even bigger joke. With an effective range of maybe 20 feet, getting close enough to hit someone with one puts you WELL within range of endless gunfire. Their only purpose seems to be destroying sandbag barricades and artillery—and nothing else, not even wooden boxes.
GRENADES DO NOT WORK THAT WAY. Good night.
Other than that, the game is all right. It doesn't bog you down with a huge amount of different units and mechanics, easy for even beginners to strategy games to get into. There is a fair amount of grinding required to get your unit/equipment levels up, but that's JRPGs for you.
On the plus side, if you hate anime storylines, you can skip through 95% of the cutscenes and just get to the shooty-shooty-bang-bang.

It's truly an alien world... And the enemy AI is actually challenging and crazy smart, which is just astounding considering this is a game from 1998 and how lame AI often still is today. The game is really challenging in general, and it is very long.
When I think of a true JOURNEY of a game, I think of this very Unreal right here. No ♥♥♥♥ing Tournament, just plain♥♥♥♥♥original Unreal 1 right the ♥♥♥♥ here. It is positively... UNREAL, the places you'll go in this game. The very definition of an adventure. People always going on about how great Half-life is, but I honestly feel this game might be a notch or two more amazing than Half-life, for the same sorts of reasons Half-life 1 was/is awesome. And I do ♥♥♥♥ing LOVE Half-life. This game... This game gave me feelings, guys. Real ♥♥♥♥ing feelings. I was truly in awe. This game should be recognized more, and it has my 100% recommendation, especially considering the price.
The expansion, Return to Na Pali gives a bunch more levels for even more Unreal goodness and continues the story directly where Unreal 1 left off, but the player character is suddenly given a voice, and I think that goes against what the original Unreal was about. He'll (you'll) talk in between levels in some dumb kinda unncessary monologue about what just happened and what's going to happen next. So Return to Na Pali is the same fun as Unreal 1, but with some mediocre new narrative style. So even including Return to Na Pali and Unreal 2 (which goes even further into the voiced characters, try-hard hamfisted story ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t territory, and is really quite a different kind of game altogether), there truly hasn't been another game quite like Unreal since Unreal came out all these years ago, and while the Unreal Tournament games aren't bad, I think it's a damn shame Epic (Mega)Games never made another game as incredible in the way Unreal was. Here's hoping for a really good current-gen remake of some sort; this singleplayer Unreal truly deserves another chance in the spotlight. Or perhaps a whole new Unreal game altogether, if they can nail it like this one did, and take away from the stains of Return to Na Pali and Unreal 2. It is one of the most amazing experiences I've ever played, and I wish more people could understand what I'm talking about by playing the game for themselves. So go do that, reader! It's totally worth it, trust me on this one. That so few people talk about this game just astounds me. And there's also multiplayer, yes.

Do you enjoy intrigue? Do you find your life lacking in fictional assassinations of royal houses? Do you find yourself missing a bit of crusading action on a cold winter's day?
If the answer is "yes" to any of the above questions, look no further, for Crusader Kings II is here to rescue you and bring you to the era of crusades and conquest! Beginning in 1066, Crusader Kings II lets you pick any count, duke, king, or emperor that existed in Europe at the time. You can play as William the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, before he became William the Conqueror. You can try to avert his invasion as Harold Godwineson, or play your kings right and bring the French Capet's into England.
The game features an extensive system that lets you achieve domination through intrigue, either through plotting or reckless assassinations. Another brilliant selling point? The AI doesn't play to win. It's programmed to play into its role. A lunatic character may attempt reckless tactics that wouldn't have any chance of winning. A paranoid character might imprison people left and right. So you never quite know what to expect.
Along with all these things, the game offers a whole aisle of DLC to suit your every need. The Old Gods will let you extend the timeline to the invasion of England by the Sons of Ragnar in 867, and let you reform the Norse faith and become Fylkir. The Sword of Islam lets you play a muslim leader, letting you enjoy the wonders of decadence and all that accompanies. Rajas of India brings you to India, and lets you experience Hindu and Buddhist culture first hand as you struggle to become the greatest ruler in India.
The game also features a massive amount of mods, placing you in any of a number of universes. Are you interested in  Arthurian England? There's a mod for that. Maybe you're a Song of Ice and Fire fan? You can play as the Stark or any number of their allies or enemies in the Game of Thrones mod, if that's the case. You can also drop into Bethesda's Elder Scrolls universe with the Elder Kings.
There will be endless hours of fun, that much I can almost guarantee.

The crafting system is very deep, but it does rely on RNG a little too much (its a korean developer after all).
But this game is NOT at all optimized well. Even a high end machine will have some issues. The small # of PVE dungeons are glitched. Housing is a joke because of hackers.
And, furthermore, it's Pay 2 Win since the best gear is crafting and with RNG, you need to invest millions in gold.
I wanted to love this game. I enjoyed having my own thatched farmhouse, doing my daily farming and livestock tending. Crafting here and there. Going on trade runs. Trying to hi-jack the enemy factions trade runs.
What killed this game for me is its truly shoddy handling by XL Games and Trion. I won't bother listing what they did wrong, as that list is a mile long. Time after time they screwed up the game more and more, because of bad management. I mostly blame XL games, as on the coding side of things, a lot of the issues could have been fixed. I feel like Trion has their hands tied in a lot of decisions as well so I don't FULLY blame them.
Best example of bad management: the day the new continent of Auroria was released, where it was basically a race to build on 1 of 4 spots a castle for your guild, 90% of the playerbase could not log in. So the guilds the got the castle, it came down to luck - and there are people that prepared for weeks to do this and lost out. I stopped playing shortly after. Theyve released some new content since then but I am doubtful the game is much better.
BTW, I played this off steam, so thats why I dont have any logged hours.

OH BOY WHERE TO BEGIN!
Disgaea is my favourite game series of all time and after waiting literally 3 years later it finally made its debut to steam! Although it had a rocky start on launch day NIS did a good attempt to fix all the problems and although the game is playable for the most part, the rest of the problems can be fixed with the
that Kaldaien made so I strongly suggest using it if you want a better experience. Port issues aside, let's discuss about the meat that is Disgaea!
The best way to describe Disgaea is that it's Final Fantasy Tactic's crazy uncle who overdosed on drugs and alchohol. Compared to other tatic's games such as the aforementioned Final Fantasy Tatics, Fire Emblem  and X-Com, Disgaea gives you so much freedom and allows you to be as creative as you want to be! Literally every humanoid class can use any weapon skill with any strategy that opens up to many possible combinations (e.g. mage's with guns and archers with axes) and the absurd level cap of 9999. On top of that, the Item World, although archaic in the first game, is an excellent random dungeon if you want to spend time spelunking and improving your items!
Now if you don't like grinding in videogames or can't tolerate an excess amount of grinding, I strongly suggest staying away from this game series as it is heavily grind based later on in the post-game/side-game, where the real meat of the game takes place.
Out of all the entries in Disgaea, the main story in the first game is probably the best imho. With the original trio Laharl, Etna and Flonne, they make the story really enjoyable as it's mostly comedic and self-aware of it's own absurdness. Granted it does an excellent job when being serious as well so don't jump in thinking its all fun and games!
Voice acting wise it can be a hit or miss for many people. I personally enjoyed the english dub of this game as they did a pretty good job in voicing the characters and I expecially love Barbra Goodson, Michelle Ruff and Sandy Fox for their roles as Laharl, Etna and Flonne respectively. They pretty much made the game for me and even to this day they still reprise their roles for the characters. And ik that Etna's original voice actor from the PS2 version didn't carry over and although I did like her old voice, I prefer Michelle Ruff voicing Etna since I'm more used to her voice than Amanda Winn Lee's. If you don't like hearing the dub there's the option to switch to japanese sub so it's up to personal preference.
Btw, 90% of all the non-port problems that are in the first game have been fixed and improved on in Disgaea 2 and onward! This includes monster unit equality, faster level grinding and more challenging ordeals :) With that being said, I recommend playing Disgaea PC as it not only does a great job introducing you to the game's mechanics but also shows how the series has come far 13 years later.
Edit 04/21/16: Completely forgot to talk about the music in Disgaea. Simply put, its GOD LIKE and I want everyone and anyone to listen to it. I give it a sardine/10 its too good m8.
Edit 08/22/16: Now Pleinair, Adell, Rozalin and Overlord Zetta can be recruited and playable! I waited nearly 6 months for Pleinair to be playable and NIS has delivered :)

It's a cute and fun game and I do recommend it. And don't worry, even if your math skills are a bit lacking, this game won't be hard on you whn it comes to pricing items. So buy cheap, sell high, and most of all have fun! Capitalism, ho!!!

Recettear.. I wasn't sure what to expect when I saw this game, but I bought it because it was on sale and seemed moderatly interesting.. How wrong I was. Monderatly? This game is amazing! It's such a refershing change on typical RPG's!
Owning your own store is pretty interesting, you have to keep earning an increased amount every week or you're screwed. Seems boring right? But somehow bartering prices for both purchases and sales with your customers is rather exciting (Except when a certain little girl tries shopping). As you progress in levels, new features are added like taking orders for item.
For item gathering itself, you have the option to buy items from the Market and Mechants Guild, aswell as items customers are trying to sell. However the best and obviously most fun option, is hiring an adventurer and going out to dungeons to slay monsters, find chests and collecting items to sell in your shop. The combat system is EXTREMELY basic, you have your movement keys, an attack button and a special attack button.. Thats it, but somehow the combat still feels great and rewarding. While you start out with a single adventurer, you eventually lock others of a different class, each with their own moves and differences. Whats cooler is these aren't just random characters you fight with, each one of them has their own personality. You see them at the town center, pub, church or even shopping inside your store.
And these adventurers aren't the only ones with personalitys! There are quite a few characters in the game, and while not all of them have names, you can see a general personality and gain familiarity with them. The random man will typically buy goods for this much, while the little girl won't do it for more than this. You can see aspects of their daily lives in town, and with the familiarity you can actually get feelings towards people shopping, good or bad! You'll know this person likes to haggle, these people are cheap or these people will accept higher prices.
This is a great twist, and while the idea of it might not sound great, it is. It brings a fresh and great idea with excellent exacution, with an art style that never goes bad! Even $20 is a great price for a game!

TL;DR
If you want to play the beginning and have fun, sure, go ahead. It'll be lots of fun. However as you progress, many issues become glaringly obvious and makes the game less fun.
While this game is quite fun, it easily begins to lose its charm over time. In the beginning, it's all pretty fun, leveling and learning about skills and everything. But there are so many small things that form into a big issue. The amount of grinding is way too much. Yes, I expected grinding from a MMORPG, but this is too much. For a class advancement, expect to give out a little money or run three to five dungeons over and over and over on the premise of a rare drop. Want to be able to use more than 4 skills at once? Pay up for 4 more slots! Want to be able to use more options? Pay for more slots. Inventory? Pay up. There's no way to get them without paying unless you wait and wait hoping for an event that allows you to earn them. PvE is easily repetitive and uninteresting after a while, and PvP is broken. If you run a dungeon, you'll likely have one player riding a paid mount and kills almost everything before you can get to it. PvP? Not including the amount of laggers you can find, but to even stand a chance most of the time you need to pay money. See a cool looking costume that also gives stats? $30. Per costume. And all costumes have a cheaper price, but they're only temporary. Many PvP items that hold an advantage are either temporary, or you have to pay for them. It's quite ridiculous how much they want you to pay, and that's not even all. Not only that, but the older characters are usually useless compared to the newer characters. You wanted to play Elsword, the main character? Well too bad, you're going to have to try harder because you likely picked a weak character compared to, say, Add or Lu/Ciel. I tried to like this game, I made some good friends on it, but it doesn't seem worth it. I honestly can't recommend this game unless you want to just jump on for a few times and try it.

What happens when you combine World War 2 with Anime? Ancient forgotten weapons, cute girls in military outfits, raceism against people with purple hair (???) and a School teacher / environmentalist who becomes a war hero.
Gameplay 8/10 - The game mixes turn-based strategy gameplay with a splash of real-time and pulls it off excellently. From trench warfare to tank combat, the game manages to keep it fresh with each new map and although the combat system is far from realistic it still manages to be lethal enough to keep it interesting. You'll need to flank fortified positions, use grenades and tanks to tackle opponents in cover and stay out of the enemy's line of fire at all times. Enemy tanks prove to be an almost insurmountable foe for any soldier not equipped with a rocket launcher, even they have to tread carefully around them. Meanwhile your own tanks prove to be excellent sources of mobile cover for your squishy infantry, the overall gameplay is satisfying and fun.
However, there are a few gaping holes in the gameplay balance and most maps can be cleared easily with 2-3 soldiers once you know where the exploits are. This wouldn't necessarily be a problem if not for the new game plus expert levels basically requiring you to use exactly those strategies to S rank them. This put a pretty big damper on the replayability of the game but the 1st play-though was fun from start to finish barring a small number of poorly designed maps.
Story 9/10 - The game is full of colorful characters. The core cast is full of shonen stereotype characters but even so the execution is excellent. Even the characters who are out of the spotlight of the main story are enjoyable. Every soldier on your squad is a unique person with their own quirks that come though their voice acting and even their gameplay before you ever bother to read their personnel file that contains their backstory. Don't expect any grim and gritty war-drama, the overall tone is absolutely a Shonen underdog story with the main character overcoming impossible odds at every turn. Still, in spite of the overall positive tone when the characters have those ups and downs you feel it along with them.
Graphics and Sound 8/10 - The character models and objects aren't particularly high-polly so there are some jaged edges visible occasionally. Aside from that though the game pulls off the anime/manga asthetic perfectly with vibrant colors and clean, crisp visuals. Explosion, smoke and bullet effects are intentionally cartoony looking, not particularly impressive but they fit with the overall theme. Muisic and voice acting are also solid.
Overall – If you like turn-based strategy games, tanks and shonen anime, you'll love this game.

Conan Exiles is the latest Sandbox Survival game by Funcom. With that said let's dive into my review!
I have spent a few hours playing. Let me start with my play style. I am a twitch streamer. The game was live streamed all through my experience. I went through the setup of my own server to play on. This was a feat to set up a server and took me numerous times of going through the server setup making small changes each time until the server popped online. (from the server launch to showing up is roughly 10-15 minutes total)
Once the game was launched and online I noticed a couple small problems. If you searched for servers and then clicked the refresh, I basically had to shut down the game and log back in to have servers show up. Exiting out of the game often caused a glitch where it shows "running" in steam. Which forced me to use the task manager to close the game in order to launch it again.
Once I had all the minor things smoothed out I went to actually run the game! Which I noticed the game when running basically shut my internet off in anything OUTSIDE of Conan Exiles. No google chrome, no Edge browser. No anything. It was like it shut my internet off outside of the game. This was a small annoyance. With a small deal of patience though I noticed that it worked itself out. It still does this at the time at writing.
When in game connected to my server everything worked flawless making my character and logging in. Once in game I noticed a small bit of rubber banding and lag (my ping to my server fluctuated from 4-40 depending on my music playing etc.)
The game itself plays like a standard survival game. You are left to your own devices and must survive. I will say that death seemed to come swiftly the first couple minutes of the game until I had the swing of it. I am a MOBA player mostly. So survival games are not quite my thing. This is no fault of the Devs. I found no real fault in playing the game however. Everything functioned how it was supposed to.
I did notice when killing a mob I got a lore piece named XX_lorepiece_10. This is expected in an early access game. Be aware that they do exist.
When I had an issue with server setup (going back a small bit) I was able to find all the answers on the forums or in a short google search. Through trial and error all was well. Please be patient and try different things. DMZ is your friend as you set things up and get the server running at first. Do not leave it DMZ'd however. It just removes a massive amount of issues.
I want to give the dev's a +1 to all the floppy dongs and bush in the game. Is it necessary? Absolutely not. Does it add something to the game? Yes. Tons of laughter as a sword and board equipped naked barbarian runs up on you and twerks while saying "Look at it! Rawghghrhrhr"
Would I recommend the game? Absolutely. As long as you have patience and realize that the game is EARLY ACCESS. It will have issues. If you are impatient. I would say to pass it up and wait for a more stable build.
Funcom seems to be active in the discussion threads. Throwing advice out regularly and keeping the community going. The server support (although windows only) and the mod support at launch of early access is a great addition. Being able to use my own server in my home and play my way increases the value of the game. At 29.99 the game is about industry standard and competitively priced.
Load up your rigs boys. Extend your package, open your boxes and hit that desert naked folks. You won't be disappointed, even with the bugs.

You are the spirit of a murdered police dectective in modern-day Salem and you must find out about your murder before you are able to move on. The story itself is very interesting and there are some tie-ins with the Salem Witch Trials.
Pros:
Story is interesting and engaging.
Art Style - I liked how they mixed things and structures from old Salem into the modern world in the spirit realm
Side Stories - There are a few side "missions" where you try to figure out how other people who also cannot move on have died or the meaning behind it. The game deals with numerous kinds of deaths, some not so pleasant, in a mature, grounded fashion.
While we're on the subject of different deaths, the game handles many kinds. Suicide (intentional or not), accidental (drowning and drunk driving), murder (not just of the main character), and plague to name a few. While they're not all side "missions" these people are found throughout the game and I really like how it doesn't shy away from the darker side of the mind.
Cons:
Quick Time Events - there aren't a lot but they're a pain to do and the combinations change.
Credits - 10 minutes, give or take, of unskippable credits
Overall, the game was very enjoyable and I highly recommend it if you're into these types of detective / story games.

Okay, let's keep this short: the sequel, Phantom Renaissance, is a much better game, and it's got my actual review explaining why the series is basically the best turn-based strategy/tactics games I've ever played. Compared to this game, it has all the same mechanics, better graphics, and more units. The only reason to buy this one is for the singleplayer missions, and it's got a LOT of them. So either:
1. You already have Phantom Renaissance, in which case all I have to say is that this one has as many missions, and they're just as good. The AI is a little worse, and falls for cheap tactics much more frequently, but it's really not a bother.
2: You don't have any Massive Assault game, and you're wondering if the Massive Assault Collection is worth it. In which case... that actually depends on if you have a friend(s) who likes turn-based strategy/tactic games and might want the Collection too. Yup. You see, neither this game nor its sequel have multiplayer capabilities, while Network is nothing but. So if you just want to play singleplayer, you're better off getting Phantom Renaissance now and then deciding whether to get the 'extra mission DLC' once you've beaten it, because it'll only cost you €2. If you're also interested in multiplayer... while there's quite a lot of players still playing Network 2 (their site says 185 right now), you're really gonna want a friend if you want to play regularly. And if you do, you're better off getting the Collection even if you don't want this game in particular.
...Right, was that clear enough? Basically, don't even
this game's existence until you've played Phantom Renaissance.
In any case, I still love the hell out of extra missions, so this is definitely a recommendation for me!

Alrighty, I've been playing this game for quite a while, and it's been a treat watching it develop towards launch. Now that the time is finally here, I'll try to break down what makes this game such a gem.
The premise of the game is simple; you, the player, are in a tabletop game against some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wizard called The Dealer. That may seem harsh, but, trust me, you'll hate this guy by the time you finish story mode. He's a card sharp and a cheat, and he quite shamelessly weights the deck against you at every turn. This becomes particularly apparent towards the endgame, where you can die on the first board due to the insane limitations he can put on you in terms of both combat and curses. That doesn't make him a bad character, however. The Dealer is quite effective as an antagonist, and his growing desperation as you (whom he implies to be a meathead jock adventurer) mow down his court is somewhat reminiscent of a DM growing exasperated with a party that refuses to die.
The nature of the game is a Shoggoth monstrosity that can shift its genre at will between choose-your-own-adventure, Arkham-style brawling, tabletop RPG, and roguelike. To be honest, I could spend hours trying (and failing) to describe it in any decent fashion. Watch a video of it. Jim Sterling's Squirty Play is a good one; it's the release version, and you get to see the reaction of someone who: a) has had no exposure to it, and b) was expecting something very different.
Basically, what makes this game great isn't really the gameplay; the individual parts of it are rather bland. By itself, the combat would be mindlessly dull. By itself, the board game would be ridiculously unfair. By himself, the Dealer would still be a jerk. It's the smooth integration of all the facets of this game that make it such an amazing catch. I'm not sure it will ever be considered a "great" (although one can hope), but it certainly has all the markings of a cult classic.
Pros:
+Very simple and effective gameplay
+Good voice acting (although it IS only the one voice)
+Lack of backstory allows the player's imagination to do its thing
+Although the individual sections of gameplay aren't unique, the combination certainly is
+Will shamelessly kill you without truly punishing you
+Doesn't interrupt gameplay; even on death, you can immediately jump back in
+Endless mode is pretty entertaining
+No ♥♥♥♥♥♥ crafting systems
Cons:
-Combat can be a tad wonky
-The optimization is quite iffy; it will tank your CPU for no apparent reason sometimes. Seems to occur more prominently later in the game. This'll probably be fixed (and it's ALOT better than it used to be), but it should be noted.
Niggles:
~It feels like some of the event triggers are a tad insane, particularly the ones with multiple RNG draws. I still haven't completed the River encounter.
~You can wind up in positions that can break the game in your favor; I've had more than 1k health at one point due to a bit of RNG luck after finding the Ring of Poverty.
~Flame golems are ridiculous. They take a lot of hurtin' and they dish out even more. When they show up in multi-monster encounters, it usually means a wipe.
~The Dealer is an incorrigible cheat. No really, he's a prick.
I'd give it a hearty thumbs up. Buy it.

Played this game since early access and it's only gotten better upon release.  This is a wonderful blend of deckbuilding, board games, and arena combat.  It features great organic storytelling with individual encounters stringing together a journey towards a big boss that you play in sessions.  The combat is smooth, fluid, and highly skill based.  You are dropped into an arena for combat and you need to fight, break guards, and counter your opponent to kill them before they kill you.  Outside of combat, you make choices and take chances to advance your story and unlock new cards for different encounters.
It's a magical experience where you feel immersed in a world even when not fighting.  The game is very heavily RNG based, but I'd say it is more reliant on skill than other rogue-like games.  You can still get screwed by RNG, but you can survive a surprising amount through sheer force of will and skill.
Musically, the game is superb, with memorable battle music, suspenseful main themes, and a very peaceful shop and certain encounter music.  The best part though is the narrator, who is equal parts friend and foe, your companion through the game who both tries to kill you, but also encourages and balances your experience.  Every line of dialogue from him is quote worthy and awesome.
Graphics are...one of the games few problems.  Card art is great and even the 3d designs are cool, but it's a bit low quality and prone to clipping.  Numerous times I've played the game and monsters or my character will get caught in scenery or the character models will freak out rag doll style at the end of combat.  Most of the time its not game breaking, but it can be annoying.  And there are a few bugs that need to be worked out.  More than once, I've had my music and sound effects fail on me.
These are minor annoyances for a highly unique and surprisingly addictive game though.  Highly recommended.  Fair warning though, the final boss is total BS and feels very unfair, so be prepared for a little frustration.

I never expected that this game would become the single game I've played more than any other in my twenty-five years of gaming. The character/dynasty depth goes far deeper than the simple character portraits alude to. The challenge of taking a simple count and surviving, then thriving, is what I'm all about. I usually strive to form a large kingdom or empire, then I settle in with no intention of expanding. I prefer to build alliances and defend my Faith. When I inherit large swaths of territory unexpectedly, I begin decades long plans to give it up. The biggest challenge is powerful neighbors. Sometimes I am forced to wait for a hundred years or more to slowly get what I want. Timing is everything. You'll spend countless hours making plans, and twice as long struggling with unexpected calamities. Simple traits like 'craven' or 'lustful' will give you nightmares. The game deserves more than my recommendation, and I easily rate it 100/100. Hands down, the greatest game I've ever played.

Recettear.. I wasn't sure what to expect when I saw this game, but I bought it because it was on sale and seemed moderatly interesting.. How wrong I was. Monderatly? This game is amazing! It's such a refershing change on typical RPG's!
Owning your own store is pretty interesting, you have to keep earning an increased amount every week or you're screwed. Seems boring right? But somehow bartering prices for both purchases and sales with your customers is rather exciting (Except when a certain little girl tries shopping). As you progress in levels, new features are added like taking orders for item.
For item gathering itself, you have the option to buy items from the Market and Mechants Guild, aswell as items customers are trying to sell. However the best and obviously most fun option, is hiring an adventurer and going out to dungeons to slay monsters, find chests and collecting items to sell in your shop. The combat system is EXTREMELY basic, you have your movement keys, an attack button and a special attack button.. Thats it, but somehow the combat still feels great and rewarding. While you start out with a single adventurer, you eventually lock others of a different class, each with their own moves and differences. Whats cooler is these aren't just random characters you fight with, each one of them has their own personality. You see them at the town center, pub, church or even shopping inside your store.
And these adventurers aren't the only ones with personalitys! There are quite a few characters in the game, and while not all of them have names, you can see a general personality and gain familiarity with them. The random man will typically buy goods for this much, while the little girl won't do it for more than this. You can see aspects of their daily lives in town, and with the familiarity you can actually get feelings towards people shopping, good or bad! You'll know this person likes to haggle, these people are cheap or these people will accept higher prices.
This is a great twist, and while the idea of it might not sound great, it is. It brings a fresh and great idea with excellent exacution, with an art style that never goes bad! Even $20 is a great price for a game!

Do you enjoy intrigue? Do you find your life lacking in fictional assassinations of royal houses? Do you find yourself missing a bit of crusading action on a cold winter's day?
If the answer is "yes" to any of the above questions, look no further, for Crusader Kings II is here to rescue you and bring you to the era of crusades and conquest! Beginning in 1066, Crusader Kings II lets you pick any count, duke, king, or emperor that existed in Europe at the time. You can play as William the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, before he became William the Conqueror. You can try to avert his invasion as Harold Godwineson, or play your kings right and bring the French Capet's into England.
The game features an extensive system that lets you achieve domination through intrigue, either through plotting or reckless assassinations. Another brilliant selling point? The AI doesn't play to win. It's programmed to play into its role. A lunatic character may attempt reckless tactics that wouldn't have any chance of winning. A paranoid character might imprison people left and right. So you never quite know what to expect.
Along with all these things, the game offers a whole aisle of DLC to suit your every need. The Old Gods will let you extend the timeline to the invasion of England by the Sons of Ragnar in 867, and let you reform the Norse faith and become Fylkir. The Sword of Islam lets you play a muslim leader, letting you enjoy the wonders of decadence and all that accompanies. Rajas of India brings you to India, and lets you experience Hindu and Buddhist culture first hand as you struggle to become the greatest ruler in India.
The game also features a massive amount of mods, placing you in any of a number of universes. Are you interested in  Arthurian England? There's a mod for that. Maybe you're a Song of Ice and Fire fan? You can play as the Stark or any number of their allies or enemies in the Game of Thrones mod, if that's the case. You can also drop into Bethesda's Elder Scrolls universe with the Elder Kings.
There will be endless hours of fun, that much I can almost guarantee.

This game is definitely a game where you make your own fun. You take the role of a character and you really pretend you are that character. Then you can work together or take advantage of the people around you. If you don't put in an effort and instead expect the game to be fun on its own, then you're probably not going to have a good time. This is not like most games.
You can't join a game and expect there to be an experience, and since this game's community has a problem with people joining only to be afk, which in this game is a seriously annoying problem, sometimes you'll have to play an entire 30 minute round with only a few people, which really ruins the entire round.
There are also a lot of small issues. Controls are a bit clunky, which is mostly fine, but still annoying. If you're playing the free version, you are limited to one scenario, which means you're missing out on a third of the game. I'm not sure if paying the subscription fee is worth it, unless you're really dedicated. I think they said they're going to rethink this, but I'm honestly not sure.
This is going to be a really strange comparison, but I'm going to compare the game a bit to DayZ. Most of the fun is from your experiences with the players. The world and tools alone aren't all that interesting, and if you just buy DayZ without having any idea what it's about, explore the world a bit, ignore everyone else, and die, then you're going to have a pretty miserable experience. Where games like DayZ shine is the golden moments like, I dunno, staying alive wounded in a cabin with your friend, desperately hoping that you won't get hurt and the stranger outside the window isn't there to kill you. Few games give you that experience.
The issue with Velvet Sundown is that experiences like that don't happen as often. My first round was destroyed because there was only two other players actually playing. There were three people afk, making playing the actual game impossible.
My second round went better, but afk players still meant that the round didn't play out properly. My third game was amazing, where I played a doublecrossing thief who made money off of working together with an alliance, then backstabbing them in favour of a second alliance. It was a great experience, but I'm not sure if that was worth one and a half hour of waiting and hoping that the afk players would come back to life. I have 2 hours of gameplay in this game, and I've only played these three games.
I'm not recommending this game, because the average person browsing this page because they saw Cr1tikal or Giant Bomb or whatever playing this game is NOT going to enjoy this game. It's free, but I don't think this is worth it for you. You really need to put a bit of yourself into it to make a good experience, and that's not something people are used to.

This game is pretty entertaining dispite it being a little hard learning what to do. The tutorial only tells you how to start a conversation with somebody. It does not tell you how to play, because it's completely up to the player on how they will go about their mission to complete your task. This game is all about conversations.
Basically there are agents of two different companies. Each company needs a data chip to keep their plans from being exploited.  Those data chips are found by players that aren't in the companies, just normal people, and they can choose to give the data chip away for either info on other people or cold hard cash.
Watch out for agents with tazers. They can steal datachips and info from you, so make sure to show your correct CID to other agents of the same company, and never mention or talk about the data unless it's with another fellow agent.
How other players find these datachips is by getting a task to search the ship for them, and can be found in a drawer. Other players cannot take the data chips, only you can. So it gives you the choice of either selling it for money or returning it to their owners.
There are a few roles that others can play, these are the ones I've tried and played against.
A religious man that wants to convert others to the meditation of Jesus Christ.
A man looking for others to sign his petition for saving the whales.
A girl/guy looking for their long lost red thong.
A drunk Russian that tazes somebody for fun.
A news journalist that takes photos of everyone.
A Drug Dealer that can sell or give away drugs to others.
A Man/Woman that needs to find an adopter for a young girl living in a poor country.
A Bartender that serves drinks.
A Woman asking for passports.
An agent that can steal data from others.
Now the question is, is this game worth my time? Well if you like investigative roleplay then this is for you, it's a point and click third person game. You basically find all the datachips if you're an agent, and if you're not an agent you get a task to complete that is pretty silly sometimes and entertaining if you know a way of going about it.
I was a bartender the first time I played. So my job was to serve drinks and find my favorite red thong. Which made me laugh. So people that talked to me, I was able to serve them drinks but I also asked around if anybody has seen my red thong, I said I was a famous male stripper and that thong meant very dear to me. So I asked a lady to see if she can find anything for me, and if she got the thong I would pay her for it. Eventually she did, and I gave her the money. Everybody starts off with $100,000 to do something with it. Either buying data chips or drugs, or a red thong.
Everybody on the boat is useful for something and when one person leaves it sometimes ruins the entire game for others trying to get the data, but not all the time.
I recommend this game to people that like to investigate, role play with other players, or help people sign your petition for saving the whales.

So, Funcom is back with another Conan game. This time it's a survival, RUST meets ARK kinda thing. Or that's what it's going to be when it's finished anyway. Right now, the game is...pretty lackluster. Expect stuttering, online server instabilities (servers getting wiped, disappearing and lots of lag), missing animations, items with big red boxes for images and plain wrong item descriptions (rope being labeled as daggers etc.) This game is in a very early stage, somewhere between alpha and beta in my opinion, and needs a lot of polish to justify the pricetag. The game is labeled as Early access and no doubt they'll be working on it a lot in the coming months, but don't buy it and expect a smooth playing experience, with plenty of content.
Graphics wise it's pretty decent, but I expect them to iron out a few things before going gold. Some clipping and graphical errors here and there but overall, totally ok in the graphics departement.
The biggest issue I have with the game as it stands now is the combat. It is atrocious. Animations are way off, and most of the time they're non-existant. You wildly swin whatever weapon you have at the enemy and pray to hit. Hitboxes needs adjusting and the overall "feel" of the weapons needs to be much better. It's kinda hard to explain but none of the weapons feel right. The best way to describe it is to say that it feels like hitting the enemies with the same stick no matter what weapon you are wielding.

Whenever this game is on a steam sale or bundle, I always want to go knight with a tower shield on my back... If your are new to the game. Please note the following:
1. Don't hit your own team members - Accidents happen, so say when you and a fellow team member kill a guy and your sword goes through the enemy and hits your team mate as well. Just say sorry etc... Also if you keep running into someone else's fight greedily trying to get the killing blow and you hit your team mate, your an♥♥♥♥♥ Same goes for someone interfering with your fight; you hit them by accident... unlucky them.
2. Stay off the catapult and ballista!!!!!!!!!!! Don't aim for the team objective where all your team members are gathering at... PLEASE! Only use them if you know how to. (Else everyone will kill you and kick your♥♥♥♥♥out of the match ASAP)
3. See that guy there with red on his armor? He was an agatha player with blood from the enemy he just slain! Make sure you know who you are actually attacking! (Hint: Red or Blue name shall appear at the bottom of the screen)

Pros
- Great mechanics intertwining turn-based tactics with first person aiming.
- Great art style (if you're into Anime).
- Lots of actual gameplay even if you skip the copious amounts of cutscenes.
- Very satisfying to take out enemy soldiers and vehicles. Great sound and visual design help a lot with this.
- Your squad members have a lot of individual character and flavour.
- Both English and Japanese dubs.
Cons
- Story is a little cliche and melodramatic.
- Copious amounts of cutscenes.
- Has some game-flow issues, such as making you double confirm a move or double confirm going to barracks. (Gets annoying after the 50th time it asks "are you sure you want to end turn?")
- Enemy turns can't be sped up. In some scenarios their turns take longer than yours due to game-flow issues. Ideally we'd be able to turn off/speed up enemy turns.
- Excessive loading around non-battle scene transitions. E.g. going from squad barracks to weapons upgrade takes way too long.
- Console-gamepad type menu controls and navigation. Could have used a lot of work to include mouse driven menus.
- Driving the tank is really sucky with mouse. TIP: Use your NUMPAD along with WASD. Leave the mouse out of the equation.

Valkyria Chronicles is many things: creative, innovative, clever, fascinating… And yet? Not actually much fun to play. There's a tremendous amount of interesting (and mostly positive!) discussion to be had about the design, but the overall experience is dragged down by consistent frustrations. Highly recommended if you're a turn-based strategy junkie AND interested in game design AND aren't inclined towards perfectionism. Much less so if you don't intersect all three of those groups.
The core gameplay of VC is a frankly brilliant fusion of turn-based strategy with third person shooter. Each turn, you can activate units a certain number of times, with each activation letting you move the unit freely about a 3D map and line up a single volley of shots. It's intuitive while also being totally unique, and elements like terrain and return fire work in a clear, logical way. Units come in 5 classes with distinct strengths and weaknesses, and each character has their own individual features (as well as chirps and emotes) to distinguish them from others of the same class. It makes a wonderful first impression.
The game manages to be less than the sum of its parts, though. Unit upgrades are based entirely on how many turns you take to beat missions, and these requirements - especially in the early game - encourage a breakneck sprint across the map. That leads to (for example) 4 of your 10 units rushing across a map doing all the work while the other 6 sit in base, never getting used. Which is fine (kind of) except that it's also easy for a unit to be killed in a single enemy action or turn if you take a wrong step, and pinning your success on so few units makes a single death reset-worthy. The result is a fiddly, save scum-y experience as you get derailed by fluke hits/misses, surprise enemies out of the fog of war, and so on. While some blame undoubtedly lies on the player (i.e. me), the "right" way to play is not the "fun" way to play, and VC trains you to do the former rather than the latter.
There are other issues as well - arguably useless character classes, unreliable character abilities, characters whose special unlocks make them totally unusable, buffs that are barely ever worth their cost, a very pretty UI that is not always helpful, annoying rules surrounding attack animations, tedious and unskippable cutscenes, and more - but the game flow is definitely the biggest hiccup. If you can resist the urges to execute everything flawlessly or spend time grinding on filler content, there's lot's to appreciate. It's just a shame that the game doesn't always seem to want your love.

This might be the most atmospheric game I`ve played so far. The envoirments, lighting and especially the sound design immerse you in this world unlike any other game. The haunting soundtrack assures that you almost constantly experience a feeling of dread and uneasiness. But don´t be mislead by thinking this is a pure horror game. While it does have quite a number of scares and tense moments, it´s focus lies on the atmosphere itself, which is in some moments almost unbearibly immerssive. That goes for both the underground and surface sections, although I personally prefer the surface levels due to their beautiful design and and lighting effects. Those aspects of the game are it´s strongest points, but it also has some flaws, the most severe being the characters, that are, with the exception of one named Khan, really bland. The way the stroy is presented often boils down to one of the characters blocking your way and explaining the circumstances of the current situation. This really sloppy form of exposition can be annoying at times, especially on repeat playthroughs. However, the atmosphere remydies those flaws, at least for me, and the story has a few highlights and emotional moments. I recommend this game to every player who enjoys a tense atmosphre, post-apocalyptic scenarios and desolate city landscapes, and just fans of FPS in general who crave diversity from the generic military shooter campaigns. I´ve played through Metro: LL multiple times and the atmosphere sucks me right back into the world of the Metro universe every single time.

This game is one of the greatest I've ever played. That's not an easy thing for me to say. Everything about this game is unique. It gets a perfect score in my book. Also, it has the all time greatest boss fight at the end of the game, hands down. I love this game to death.
The gameplay is the best part of this game, the game can twist and turn any which way when your progress is lead by pure luck. The way the card system works is very simple and easy to wrap your mind around. The combat is excellent and fluid, it's awesome to watch. The combat isn't just hacking and slashing, it's about timing blocks and dodging opponents you can't fight all at once. The combat is reminscent to the first Fable, in fact, much of this game really is a Fable game without the brand name, but the combat is so much more interesting here than in any Fable.
The graphics are lush and colourful. It has that wonderful atmospheric fantasy mood that Fable set so perfectly.
The sound quality is top notch for the most part. There is a few times when the sound does cut out but a simple restart fixes that immediately. The soundtrack is awesome and really has an epic vibe to it. I was even thinking of buying it if it's sold on Steam. It's one of those soundtracks that'll take me back years from now. I love the clanging of the swords and the thumping of swords against shields. The voice actor behind the Dealer is on the same level of deep and mesmerizing as Morgan Freeman. He's like an English Morgan Freeman, I can't stress enough how good of a voice actor he is.
The story line is interesting, it's not a normal storyline. You enter at the end of the adventurer's story. This is a retelling of all his adventures. So it's a game about retrospective and reflection. The Dealer makes very interesting remarks and ponderings that make me think on a philosophical level. What kind of game does that?
I love a game that I can put hundreds and hundreds of hours into. A game that has endless replayability and isn't limited by just having a storyline. This is one of those games. It doesn't ever have to end. There's an endless mode. There's also 200+ cards to collect. Each card is an encounter. Every game randomizes these encounters and even throws in some that benefit you and some that debilitate you to a certain extent. This game definitely earns its pay and has lot of bang for very little buck.
If you're on the fence about getting it, don't be. This game isn't hard to fall in love with. I'd recommend this game to absolutely anyone.

Hand of Fate is a really fun card game with beat 'em up elements. The game features two modes; Story and Endless. This will mostly be focused on Story, as I've not played Endless yet.
The game is fairly simple; the dealer will lie down cards on the table and you will move your piece onto the cards. Sometimes, this is linear, but sometimes it isn't. Some cards will activate things like visiting a shop, encountering baddies to kill, traversing a maze or coming up against a situation where, of 4 cards, you must pick the "Success" card in order to win. You will have, at the bottom right, three "stats": your health, your food & your gold. Every move consumes 1 food, but you'll restore lost health. Gold is fairly self-explanatory.
When you get an encounter card, you are placed onto a small plot of field where you will fight against monsters, ranging from goblins to skeletons, zombies and bandits. While variation is limited, it doesn't pull away from the experience. However, the fighting / combat is rather wonky; borrowing from the Arkham series, you will basically use WASD to move around and left click to attack. You cannot hard target a specific enemy, which can be a bit frustrating, but again, really doesn't affect the game greatly.
Situation cards vary, from finding a weapon in a crevasse to saving someone from being swarmed by enemies. Successfully "winning" these situations nets you a token from the dealer. At the end, all of your accrued tokens are counted up and you are given specific rewards based on the tokens. For example, I was tasked with defeated a knight that had been overrun by some skeletons. Once I defeated them, he told me I could keep the mace I was given prior to the fight, as his kingdom was flush with them. Once I completed the level, his token rewarded me with 2 Mace cards.
You progress through the 'levels' by travsering through the cards, finding that particular level's 'end card' and moving onto the next level. At the end of the final level, you will fight a boss. Defeating the boss gives you more tokens, which unlock things like weapons, armor, encounters and other varying cards.
One of the coolest things this game offers is the Deck Builder. On one side, your deck has cards for Equipment; weapons and armor and trinkets. The other side are your encounters, from visiting shops to situations. If the card has a lock icon on it, that means it has a situation / encounter you've yet to face. Drawing & defeating that card will net you another token.
Last but not least is the Dealer himself; an elderly mage who speaks to you throughout the game. His dialogue is superb and I found myself actively listening to what he had to say. The first level, I drew a card that had a goblin giving me a shield. The next level, I drew the card again and, in this very dry tone, he said "I think you purposefully put that card in there just to get an early shield." (or something to that effect) It's minor, but the fact he recognizes that made me smile.
I know my hours played as of writing this is low (think it's barely 2 hours), but honestly - the game is immediately fun. The combat is a bit wonky, but everything else excels so well that I don't mind. It doesn't hurt that the game also looks really good & sounds pretty good, too. I can't wait to jump back into the game and have more fun with it. :)

Disgaea is a fun parody of the RPG and anime genre, and tells its story through a colorful cast of characters and visuals.
Characters:
The cast consists of Laharl, a bratty, but oddly cool demon prince; Etna, his scheming vassal and lastly, Flowne, a loving angel-in-training who they call "Love Freak". Like I mentioned before, the cast are parodies of anime and RPG tropes, but they retain enough of their own personality to feel like actual people instead of simply jokes. Even the secondary characters are given variation in both their personalities and design. By that I mean there are no throwaway characters because each one feels so unique and different.
The Story:
Campy and purposefully silly, Disgaea’s story is rife with comedy and references, but not so much as to ruin the atmosphere. The serious moments are kept appropriately dramatic, but there are times when something goofy happens that can break the tension. These times; however, are kept out of the more serious moments.
Mechanics:
Despite its age the game’s system is still fun and its various features like “The Item World”, “The Dark Assembly” greatly spice up the game.  What would be an otherwise tedious grind is saved by conveniences and distractions offered by your ability to bribe or crush the assembly, or grab some stuff in the Item World.
The dungeon mechanics drag the game down a little, but overall, the game is fun to play, and not as easy as the cutesy graphics would make it seem.

This is an interesting murder mystery adventure game.  While it has some "action" components, it's closer to being a point and click adventure game.  Playing as the ghost of a detective, you have to search through various areas of town for clues about your killer.  I liked the depth of the story and it had enough twists to keep you on your toes.
With that being said, I do have a couple of gripes about the game.  Firstly, the enemies.  The "demons" (which I would have personally called wraiths given how they're designed, but whatever) feel like they were tacked into the game as an afterthought by some exec in a suit that decided the game needed some action to make it fun.  This in fact does not equal fun.  I literally groaned and rolled my eyes every time I heard the sound of them being zoned into an area.  They're not hard to kill or anything, you just use some stealth type gameplay to sneak up behind them and do what amounts to a 1 step quicktime event to kill them off.  Even when you fail, they still won't necessarily kill you since you can run and hide until they go back on their short patrol route.  I never died from them at any point.  Once you kill all of them off in that particular area, they never respawn (thankfully).  I found their presence interrupted the flow of the game and was just a major annoyance.  I feel like the game would have flowed a whole lot better if they'd removed them completely and just left it as a straight mystery game.
My second problem, the clue system.  This one is a bit bigger since it's the main focus of the game.  Searching for clues works sketchy at times.  If you get too close to one of the clues or have it not quite lined up on your view, you won't get prompted to press they button to get it.  This happened a whole lot more than I would have liked.  Given how the majority of the clues don't glow or give any indication that it's what you need to be looking at, it can lead to a lot of frustrated wandinger back and forth in the same area trying to figure out what you missed.  Also, once you have your clues gathered, you often have to patch 2-3 of those clues together into an "answer" for the current question you're trying to answer.  While the majority of them make sense, there were a few I ended up spamming through all of the clues to try to get the correct combination.
Play time for me was around 8 hours total.  This included me collecting 90-95% of all collectibles, reading every clue that I got, watching the ghost stories for the 100% collections I had, and listening to nearly all of the spoken text each random person has to say when you possess them.  If I'd wanted to reach 100% collectibles without a walkthrough, I could have probably added on a few more hours for wandering back and forth for an eternity trying to find the ones I missed.
Overall, this is a decent adventure game that's worth a look.
To sum the rest of this up:
+ Stylish looks
+ Good voice acting and sounds
+ Solid story that makes you want to keep playing
- Clue system is iffy at times
- Combat/enemies are annoying and probably shouldn't have been put in at all

I have been watching this game for sometime now, mainly because of Funcom's involvement.  I loved what they did with The Secret World and was hoping this game would match that one.  At the same time, I recognize that it is an Early Release game so I wasn't expecting a polished game.  In fact, there seem to have been some issues from what I read on the forum that related mostly to server performance.  Since I wasn't playing on a public server, I didn't have many of those issues to contend with so my review is able to focus on the game.
Funcom really didn't disappoint.  I find that the game is much more polished than I expected as well as more polished than ARK: Survival Evolved was when it first released.  The graphics are stunning, even on medium setting.  I had no problem with AI.  While I have not tired ranged fighting, I found that melee fighting was quite smooth and fluid.  The crafting and building in the game is pretty wide open and gives room for a lot of creativity and flexibility.  It present many more options than ARK in that you can sink foundation, stack foundations, and have no collision issues.
Funcom tends to have a thing for things being realistic and sticking to the lore.  From what I've explored, they stuck to the lore really close and have added some realistic aspects such as full nudity (which is optional) that fit with in the lore.  You fight human NPC's as well as animals.  The look of the gear, weapons and structures make me feel like I am in the age of Conan.  I have died countless times from food poisoning and dehydration.  To avoid starvation, you also have the option to become a cannibal.  I really am enjoying exploring all the cool stuff that is available.
It is an early release game and it has released with more content than most early release games.  The play is smooth, (on a private server at least).  So far we've only found one bug in the game.  The content is fairly limited but there still feels like there is a lot to explore and learn.  I really haven't encountered any of the issues that others have reported and feel that Funcom released a pretty solid game for an early release game.  I am eager to see how the game develops over time.

Mass Effect 2 is outstanding and worthy of the praise lavished upon it.  It definitely has some issues that are generally minor, and none of which are really game-breaking (as of the latest patch.)  Personally, I wasn't looking for more combat-oriented gameplay after ME1, but I guess that's the way of the wind. The story is deep, and excellent detail but not to the far reaching qty that the ES series has come to know. Now, I suppose it is Gears of War lite action, but with an emphasis with a richer story and character development.

When i started this game i quite enjoyed it but the more i played the more its flaws began to annoy me to the point i just lost interest in playing. The game is sort of a JPRG take on WW2 with the story loosely based on it (though with fictional countries involved) with squad based strategy combat. The story revolves around the neutral country of Gallia which is invaded by the Empire who are intent on using Gallias abundant Ragnite which is basically a fuel source. You play as a militia squad as they fight the Empire forces.
Good points:
- the odd mix of squad based strategy with JRPG elements and style actually works quite well
- the way combat works is quite good.You have a limited number of command points eachturn which you spend to move characters and have them attack. You can control the characters yourself moving them around and aiming at the enemy.
Bad points:
-the standard levels in this game are enjoyable as you've more freedom to approach it as you like but theres a good number of "gimmicky" levels, for example one where you have to stop an armoured car before it escapes, and the problem with these is its very difficult to beat these first time round as it takes a few attempts to figure out the right way to do it. Given a battle cant take up to an hour sometimes this gets very frustrating and while i admire the attempt to stop things getting stale these levels are just annoying to play as well as feeling more restricted in your approach
- at the end of a battle your awarded a class simply based on how quickly you beat the level and nothing else. However beating to beat a level quickly usually involves just rushing one or two scouts through the map and capturing the flag,which isnt really fun and makes a more tactical and thorough approach pointless. Given that a higher class rating means more exp and money for upgrades this is a problem.
- and on the subject of exp and money the only way to accumalate exp outside the story is through skirmishes which are replayable battles.Late in the game i found my squad was under-levelled and i was struggling in the story missions. My only option to gain more exp was to grind the skirmish battles which got boring real quick.
Overall this game was just disappointing. It shows a lot of promise early on but after 25 hours i'd just had enough and had no desire to play it anymore.

Oh, how I love this game. It's primarily a detective game, for people who are fans of other detective games like Sherlock Holmes, and who don't require endless action sequences. In fact, for a detective game, it has more action sequences than most others. It's like if Sherlock Holmes were a tattooed ghost who had to deal with demons (but with considerably easier mysteries to solve). Plus, because you're investigating your own murder, it gets so much more personal than other detective games. Plus, it's a helluvalotta fun being a ghost, walking through walls, possessing people and such. There are some things they could have done differently, but those things are mostly superficial, like using more character models for the citizens randomly roaming around a town where so many murders have been taking place (these side characters also could have had more fun inner dialogues, to make it more fun to possess them and read their minds). And the story itself was very short and ended rather suddenly. But I've never played a game where I wanted so badly to get every single achievement and solve every little side mystery I encountered. I enjoyed dealing with the demons, and squealed like a little girl every time one caught me trying to execute it. It's fun trying to avoid them and leap from hiding place to hiding place. Overall, as a fan of classic detective stuff (like S.H.), the game was refreshing and invigorating all at once. I just wish I could've made the citizens' lives a little more scary when I poltergeisted or possessed them.

It's a really good game - that is, if you like an visual novel/tactical RPG hybrid.
The story revolves around Squad 7 of Regiment 3 of the Gallian Militia, in a time where the Empire and the Republic are at war on the continent Europa (in a lot of European languages that's the name for Europe), where the Empire decides to invade the independent nation of Gallia (roughly situated about where Latvia is in real Europe - the Empire spans roughly modern-day Russia) because the rare resource of ragnite is abundantly presented in Gallia's soil. While this stays the main storyline, during the story there comes a second plotline along which reveals more sinister details about an past race which once ruled over the whole of Europa.
You play the game by selecting 'chapters' in a 'book', which then get narrated and animated - or it launches the combat module if you've selected an fight. It works pretty good, it can be sensitive sometimes though.
The combat itself turn-based but with control points for controlling the amount of units you can move, and movement points for how far an unit can move in a single turn. At first you'll need to adjust perhaps to it, but you'll get quickly used to it. It works flawlessly and can be fun to play.
Something to note here is the game doesn't shy away from touching historical happenings: the First Europan War for example happened because the crownprince of the Empire got murdered, akin to the murder on crownprince Ferdinand of the Austrian-Hungarian Empire which caused World War I. (The game takes place during the Second Europan War)
It also doesn't shy away from touching the treatment of Jews and Gypsies in Europe during the first half of the 20th century, nor does it shy away from the horrors of war. I can only commend the creators at Sega for this - although it isn't the first time the Japanese dare to touch subjects which European and especially American studios are quick to turn into mindless stuff.
The storytelling while not as powerfull as some of the Western RPGs of the last decade, is still pretty good. The combat works flawless, and it's a joy to play those battles - be prepared for ambushes sometimes. While the AI is not OP it isn't dumb either - it makes tactical mistakes sometimes, but that adds a bit to the feeling of 'Hey, I stand a chance'.
8/10 rating from me for this mature game.

Before I continue writing my review on this game, I got to say that the PC port of Valkyria Chronicles is one of the best, if not,
best port. The game was originally exclusive for the PlayStation 3 back in 2008. The game was well received, but garnered low sales that would put the sequels Valkyria Chronicles 2 and 3 on the PSP. I actually never heard of this game before until a few week prior to the PC release on November 2014. That said, I will have to give a standing ovation to Sega for putting an effort to make the PC port well optimized in 1080p (or more) at 60 FPS (or more). Sega has my attention and I will present this review.

Valkyria Chronicles focuses on Welkin Gunther, a son of a legendary general who fought in the First Europan War, leads a platoon of some adults and teenage volunteers to defend their country against the invading forces of the Imperial Alliance. The game presents a mix of tactical strategy and third-person action that is very unique in the strategy game genre. Does this game deserve your attention?
The story takes place in a “fictional” European continent where the Second Europan War was fought primarily between the Atlantic Federation (think of all of the European countries, in a geographical sense) versus the Imperial Alliance (Russia, in a geographic sense). Gallia is a “neutral” country where it contains a unique resource known as Ragnite. Thus, the Imperial Alliance invade Gallia to get Ragnite to fuel up their war resources. One of the greatest parts about the game is how well the developers use analogies from World War II into the game and its execution is well-received. The analogies ranged from weapon designs (like the Gallian Scout weapons that look like the Soviet SVT-40 to the Imperial weaponry comparison to the real-life MP40 and STG44, and plenty others). The analogy extends to vehicles and geopolitical conflicts.
The character developments in the game are highly impressive, particularly with the relationship between Welkin (protagonist) and Alicia Melchiott (deuteragonist). The themes in Valkyria Chronicles consist a good mix of “light” moments (like hope as an example) and “semi-grotesque” themes of war (such as discrimination/racism, personal ambition over soldiers’ lives, and others themes that will unravel later on). Some reviewers criticized the game as being not serious on the themes about war. Honestly, I don’t think that the game is supposed to be depressing and a good mix between “light” and “dark” is best suited for the game. The story starts really slow in the beginning and actually begin to progress as you reach a certain point in the story. The plot is pretty good in most area while few scenes are a bit “awkward” in terms of sudden shifts between a sad event to a “positive motivation”.
The gameplay in Valkyria Chronicles is turn-based, but it is very unique because once you click on a character to choose, you can actually control the character to move to any location in third-person you like as long you have enough Action Points (basically, the movement bar). Experience points and money are earned by Ranks (like A, B, C, and D) by completing an objective within a certain number of turns (Example: Getting a ‘A’ rank within 3 turns or less to get the maximum amount of exp and money). However, it is possible that you can actually kill all of the enemies on the map, complete the objective, and still get an ‘A’ rank in the majority of missions (except for a few of them).
With the exp and money, you train your soldiers based on classes Scout, Shocktrooper, Lancer (Anti-Tank/Explosives), Engineers, and Sniper rather than individuals. The money are used up to upgrade weapons, buy tank parts, and purchasing “reports” from a reporter in certain chapters in the story. The game would last you a good 30-50 hours if you play the game in a smart, tactical manner or have an “OCD” on getting an “A” rank on every single mission in the story or a mix of both (like I did).
The game does have some faults, particularly when it comes to classes. Reviewers argued that Scouts are too overpowered, but in my view, it is best to say that scouts are too reliable since they have the most movement bar and top-tier weapons like the ZM Kar 8 (the game's version of Soviet PTRS-41 that can obliterate any enemy, even medium and heavy tanks if you shoot it in the back). Engineers are useless in the game since you won’t repair your tank very often (depending on your play style) and Scouts are the better alternative. There are some bugs in the game that is related to the monitor refresh rate (if you play it on a 144 Hz monitor like I did) in certain missions in the story. PC controls are a bit awkward when you control the tank. There are a few moments in the story that has some poor “transitions” (an example would be that an upsetting moment happened in the story and all of a sudden, some of the major characters wanted a medal for their part on a major battle in the next cutscene as if that upsetting moment never happen or affected them).
The game is often compared to XCOM when it comes to gameplay. This may be true, but Valkyria Chronicles is very unique since you can actually control the character in third person instead of the computer doing it for you when you command the character to move from Point A to B, in bird’s eye view. The game engine is very aesthetic and presents the story very well. I’m glad the Sega released Valkyria Chronicles to the PC and I am very pleased to hear that a (possible) new Valkyria Chronicles game is being trademarked (and hopefully in development) thanks to the PC sales. The default price of $20 is a good deal, -50% off is a great deal, -75% is a perfect steal. Valkyria Chronicles is one of my top games for 2014 due to its unique strategy gameplay and superb PC port optimization. I am looking forward for the new game that is being trademarked (or possible PC ports or revamp for VC2 and 3). This game has my highest recommendation for any strategy gamer who want to find something original, unique, and beautiful.

Unreal was released in 1998, following ID's Quake II, and the series became destined to compete ever since. It revealed the powerful Unreal engine to the world, and as a technical achievement was absolutely groundbreaking. I got this game for free, and I still feel as though I paid too much for it. Let us see why.
Normal mode seems to be too punishing for any player at any level. The first three levels are there to let you have a feel for the game, but as you get further (I stopped at level 8), the game gets harder at an exponential rate.
You build small cute castles for a while, and suddenly you have the honour of building these 4-storey structures with random fires, moles, chickens, raining clouds, and knights trying to reverse your progress.
You have to constantly battle the moving pieces on the belt, with the damage these annoying 'enemies' do, with your mouse. You will definitely feel like a clown 15 minutes into the game.
Yes, it's a unique game. But I feel it's not worth my time and concentration to have to find a piece, click-hold on it, and then see a chicken fly by trying to steal an already laid piece, let go of the piece I was holding, drag the fireball, waiting for the chicken to land, kill it, AND THEN finding the piece again on that friggin rotating belt, putting it on the ground, only to find that I'm running out of time. Oh, don't even get me started when a mole destroys the base of an almost complete structure. That was what made me write this review.
I'd probably never play this again. Lucky I didn't pay anything for it. The price tag is DEFINITELY not worth it. Go spend it on some other better titles.

I have plenty of problems with this as a game, but I guess a lot of them are down to me wanting a wargame with a light animu gloss and getting an animu with a light wargame gloss. The system of movement is counterintuitive and jarring, the structure is a rail you ride until the predetermined conclusion and there isn't much more to it than that. The most offensive thing about the gameplay to me is probably the jarring gap between meticulously aiming at a target and then having a dice roll dictate that you miss it. I don't have a problem with a dice roll making me miss a target, but why are you letting me aim specifically at it beforehand? So sure, I found the game parts frustrating and uneven, although most of them were very easy.
But I'll be damned if now that I've finished, I don't find myself sort of missing its world and characters. I don't have many problems with the story. It's ludicrously basic and simple but that's not necessarily a bad thing. All of the characters have little arcs, and there are things you like about all of them. I could have done with a bit more military discipline in their interactions and at one point there's some hackneyed 'we're a family' garbage that made me gag, along with some other saccharine anime stuff. But that aside, it does what a story is meant to. There are things set up early in the story that pay off later, and the characters that you've come to like ultimately band together to triumph over adversity and save the day. It's essentially solid. I don't think I'll ever be interested in playing it again, but I enjoyed it well enough as a nice little story, which is basically all it is. I also deeply hated the pig with wings, but mercifully it's not actually in the game all that much.
So if you think you'll enjoy a nice, colorful little war story with some very light strategy elements, give it a try. I even got choked up a few times, particularly by Selvaria. Oh, and if you're into that sort of thing this game features both Akio Ohtsuka, the voice of Solid Snake, and his late father Chikao Ohtsuka, in several scenes together.
