Honestly, the game is plain boring. For a linear shooter, this game does little to none in terms of game mechanics to keep the player interested. Although the atmosphere is relitevly strong and engaging, the level design and game mechanics are lacking.

The game truly shines when you are in the outside areas. You get to see a wonderfully designed wasteland that is a feast to the eyes. In addition, I am from moscow myself and it was interesting to see my city from this perspective. Unfourtunatley, you do spend the majority of the game underground, and it would be fine, if it wasn't so poorly lit. Lighting in these areas is absolutely terrible. Neither does it feel natural, nor helpful with the game. It isn't pretty either. The interior designs, yet clevery adapdet to the post apocalyptic setting, do not look appealing or interesting to look at. The mutants look like five year olds draings, no joke, my brother can draw better and he is five. Some animations look like they are taken from a 2001 game. The original Half-life had more believable animations then some of the animations in this game.

The game doesn't do much to keep the player interested. all you do is walk, aim, shoot and interact. The game doesn't require much thought to it, even the stealth sections do not require you to think, there is already a layed out path you need to follow to stay undetected. But be careful, the moment a tiny spec of light shines on you, you will immideatly be detected which will just trigger another gunfight that doesn't even feel nice or authentic. What's worse, when I tried reloading checkpoint to give stealth another go, the game would load on the moment I got detected! The level design is terrible as well as you often get lost as the games isn;t always good at showing you the way forward. The boss battles are an absolute dissapointment. Basically your bosses are bullet sponges that just require you to throw grenades at them and fire your whole stock of shotgun ammo into them to kill them. No thought put into it. In addition, when you get hit, there are no indications of it. You do not hear some kind of a sound and if you do it doesn't even sound that painful. Your only indicator that you are hurt is a letter Q in the top left corner telling you to heal up.

The atmosphere is great in this game, especially outside and especially towards the end. What ruins the expirience though, is disgusting voice acting in the English version. If you are Russian, just play the game in Russian. The story is pretty decent with a few nice twists and turns, yet the ultimate ending (whether you get the good or a bad ending) is not satysfying or interesting. I found the bad ending better as it was more unpredictable.

ATS very much looks, feels and plays like ETS2. Whether that's a good or a bad thing is very subjective. It's perfectly understandable that some people call it a glorified DLC and that there isn't much content at the moment. But let's be honest, the game is also priced as a glorified DLC :)
The base game consists of the standard assets and the state of California. All other content is added in the form of DLC's This can be both free or payed DLC. Like in ETS2, new trucks will be added to the game for free. Currently, due to licensing issues, there are only the Peterbilt 579 and the Kenworth T680. SCS already has a few more trucks ready to roll out as soon as they have the approval. The first two new states are also added as free DLC. Nevada was released together with the base game and Arizona will be added soon, altough soon can easily take a few months in SCS terms ;)
Graphics and performance have improved over ETS2 but not by a huge margin. I think ATS looks a bit better with improved textures, especially the roads. It's also more detailed and has way more variety in the scenery, while in the stock ETS2 map it was just more of the same. The engine also seems to be better optimized, wich results in a bit smoother fps. Only 64-bit is officially supported this time. SCS is offering an unsupported 32-bit version for a limited time, wich can be obtained via de Betas tab within the game's properties.
The game can perfectly be played and enjoyed with a controller. Settings like sensitivity and deadzone can be adjusted for the analog controls. Off course, a keyboard also works but... don't, just don't. For the full experience, a steering wheel is highly recommended, just as much as with a (semi) realistic racing game. It's a complete gamechanger. If you also own a TrackIR, great, another gamechanger! All SCS' trucksims have native support for this device.
A neat new feature are multiple ways to park your trailer. Not in the mood for difficult parking but just pressing Enter is to fake? Just do it the easy but 'legal' way and just drive your rig forward in the designated spot. However, this will off course result in less XP than you would have gotten when parking like a boss.
I do have some minor complaints. ATS still has the same simplistic road network that ETS2 has. Second, the scaling of the map; it's smaller than ETS2's scale. I can understand that they had to do this since the US is such a ridiculously large country. I just would have wanted it to be a bit larger. Travelling from city to city is over just to quickly. Than there's the AI -_- It has improved over ETS2 but it's far from perfect. There are still many AI drivers who never passed their driving test and somehow managed to get a car. Remember those creatures in ETS2 who stopped on the highway to let you merge? They're not only living in Europe. The game also doesn't have much variety in AI vehicles. Well, noting that the modding community can't fix. ATS has the same extensive modding support that made ETS2 a huge success. That also puts the lack off standard content a bit in perspective, unless you don't want to use any mods. At the time of writing, there are already lots of mods available, including drivable trucks, cargo's, AI vehicles, skins etc. Map expansion are just a matter of time.
SCS took their sweet time to release this game and many expected a bit more content at release. I'm sure they will take care of this, like they did with ETS2. That game is well over three years old now and is still being worked on.
In the end SCS delivered the quality that we come to expect from them. If you played and like ETS2, you will feel right at home in ATS. Even with it's flaws and weaknesses, it's still that ultra relaxing driving experience that so many people love.

Being a fan of ETS2 (nearly 400 hours played), I can't be disappointed in this game. SCS has stepped up the technical aspect on ATS not only offering breath-taking visuals and better performance while keeping the same specs, but also other minor options that are very wel appreciated by enthusiasts of these kind of experience.
I love how now they've added the real gear patterns for EF transmissions. Long are the days of modifying .sii files to obtain this. Other cool options like a toggle engine brake were added as well, among other little things that while insignificant, always made you wish they were there on ETS2.
The map is simply fantastic in terms of detailing. Sure it's smaller, but remember this is the beginning. Also, compared to ETS2, this map is not repetitive at all. In ETS2 you had the same pre-fabricated highway and almost all the cities were square-shaped and look-alike.
Trucks are okay. Only two, but they are very well detailed and further in the progress you can unlock many parts for them. There is also the option for mods, thanfully.
Physics are still a bit floaty, and not what I would consider simulation, but taking in mind that you drive really slow, it doesn't bother me at all. That's if you're playing the game as it was meant to be played; with wheel, shifter and pedals. Speaking of which, getting yourself a Logitech wheel is a DEFINITIVE MUST is you wish to enjoy this at its full. ETS2 made me buy one last year and I have not regret it one bit.
Sound isn't too impressive. I am an audiophile, and also very sabby when it comes to cars, trucks and engines in general. Call me OCD, but if there is somethign I do not forgive in simulators or car games in general, is bad sounds. They've got the samples right, but the pitch on them is all over the place. Often, the truck sounds like it's reving higher in 1200rpm than it is in 1700rpm. That's what's called a loop effect, and it's just a sign of laziness on the sound developer. Thankfully, as with trucks, there are mods to fix this (which I have thanks to a friend who is also probably the best sound modder in the truck Simulator series).
My last thoguht would be that for all giving a negative review. Don't see ATS as a new game, but see it as a new platform. Remember how ETS started and how it slowly grew with time. ATS is the same. New states will be added, as well as trucks. In a year this game will be massive. And hey, you're paying $20 bucks for this wonderful experience, which is also an indicative that the game is still in expansion.
And last, don't discard ETS2. ATS as it stands now is just an expansion to it. If you see it that way your complains will be unfounded.

This is one of those ominous blind buys I do on impulse once in a while. I bought
because it looked weird enough, especially since I'm not a fan of fantasy games. I liked the idea of a random card-based dungeon and I'm a fan of old adventure books. So, HoF landed in my checkout cart for 18 EUR (20% off at the time) and I started playing while I had some vacation.
Although the graphics aren't next gen or even really good it uses colors that look great (not that horrible pastel stuff a lot of games use at the moment) and especially the dealer animations were really fun to watch. He rolls his eyes at you if you take too much time, he tucks on his wristbands once in a while and his dealing animation is still so cool to watch even after so many rounds. Also, his voice acting is just amazing. It fits perfectly, the lines are nicely written and you always feel this play between the arrogance of the dealer and his goodwill. Even without a real background story and any personal events he feels like a real character, a really cool feat to accomplish if you ask me.
The drawings on the card decks are also really fun. They look great, have just the right amount of detail and always give you hints of what to come without revealing too much about what they do. Some are like tarot decks (with conceptual or more abstract themes -- your event card deck that creates the dungeon), some just show you different equipment/resources, and some are based on French decks: boss enemies are jacks, queens, and kings; the numbers from two to six depict a minion spawn of two to six enemies, the suit determines the different types of enemies.
The gameplay is also pretty cool. People call it roguelike and trading card game based but I didn't get the feeling of any of that. Of course you have randomly generated dungeons. Of course you have some elements of TGC's in there (like receiving new cards for your deck if you win a round, creating your own decks, and managing resources) but the game reminded me a lot more of those adventure books I read as a child... ("If you want to go down to the basement turn to page 278, if you just turn around and run away turn to page 141.") The basic idea is that you move your figure from card to card to reveal new and unknown challenges. They may be good ("You find a Maiden that grants you a wish") or they might be horrible ("Someone ambushes you!"), but pretty much every single card is unique and many offer various interesting different events, depending on your choices.
The game can be very unforgiving. As someone who has played Dark Souls I'm probably not allowed to say that but the later levels can go twenty minutes and your hero will be in amazingly good shape but then everything will fall apart within one move you make. This bummed me out more than once but never enough to
restart the game.
The sound overall is not really good, especially in fighting sequences, and the music isn't entirely special (although it never really bothered me, which is a good thing, I guess). The fighting mechanics are very much like those from the newer Batman games but they feel a lot heavier and simplified. They still managed to add a lot of diversity by all the interesting equipment in the game. Basically every single item above starting gear level has unique abilities that force you to adjust tactics (especially later in the game). Still, there are less than a handful of basic enemy types and the bosses aren't all that different except from one special ability, more hit points and more devastating attacks. In the end you beat them  all up by mashing 'X.'
Another thing is: There is not a lot of end game to enjoy. After finally finishing the last story mode chapter (about five hours into the game) the only thing left is endless mode which doesn't even have a save-game option in case you're into one good run. So there's no way to drop into the game for a few minutes and play a round. The good news is that the developers are working on DLCs, but I couldn't find good info wether it will be more story mode missions with progress items or just new cards.
Finally I want to mention the price. The game is nicely produced and definitely is fun to play but with a pricetag of 23 EUR I feel those five hours could've been
of fun with some more levels like aces for each suit (or what about the full jack to king sets of lava golems and mages?). There wouldn't have been a need to draw and story-board twice as many cards, I just want to do a bit more before the game will go stale.
Drawn in by nothing more but 'uh, thos cards look cool,' and the fact that I liked the idea of adventure books since I've been a child I think the game turned out great. I felt very nostalgic, even though I had my XBox controller in hand instead of a book. The ambience and voice acting is amazing while the fighting would've been more interesting for me would it have been old-school with dice throwing. Still, while the story mode lasts and while you still feel new stuff coming, you will be entertained, even if you're not a fantasy fan. I think my 18 EUR found a good place to be, if you get it for 50% you already have a
deal. I wouldn't buy it for the full price since the content is not as extensive as it could or should be. Finally, you might be disappointed by the looks of the character who is not costumizable and ugly
I am an idiot. I totally forgot about the
level that pops up after you beat the last regular boss (not trying to spoil too much here). So there might be quite a bit more time than 5 h in the game, the final boss is insanely hard at first so you can easily spend 10 h to beat him (just a guess, might be more, might be less).

I stumbled upon this game when it was on promotion and thought it might just be a generic point & click adventure game so I didn't expect much from it. However, after playing through the game I was so glad that I found it becuase it gave me such a joyful experience and it made me hunger for more games like this.
As soon as the game menu showed up, I was intrigued. The black-and-white menu was like a stage with spotlights focusing on your mouse cursor as you scroll through it and the backgroud music was very cheerful and relaxing as well, all of which made me feel like I was sitting in a theatre waiting for a movie to begin.
The protagonist of the game is a projector with a human body, which you may already known from the game's name and screenshots. The story of the game is very simple: projector face wants to make friends with kids, but apparently, a projector can't speak, so it's not gonna be easy for him to accomplish his little dream. Projector face wants to make the kids happy, but it always gets messed up by himself in the end, which makes you laugh at his ackwardness but feel sorry for him when you see him frustrated. The soundtracks fit the game perfectly as if they're connected to the mood of projector face. They're delightful when projector face meets new kids but immediately switched to the sound of howling wind when he becomes upset. The cartoonish artstyle of the game makes projector face even more likeable. Although most of time the game made me smile, the ending left a bitter taste in my heart.
Another feature of the game that stands out is its narration style. The game takes inspiration from the silent films in the old days as it uses intertitles to push the story forward, which is brilliant in my opinion. It brought me back my sweet memories when I first watched Charlie Chaplin's films many many years ago.
The puzzles in this game are logical and interesting. You need to collect all sorts of items and figure out how to use them correctly just like other point & click adventure games. In the meantime, you also need to keep an eye for film reels and reel frames, as projector face likes to show films for the kids. There is some replayability if you want to get the hidden achievement or just to enjoy the colorful world in the game again.
My only complaint about the game is that it's too short. It took me less than an hour to beat for the first time and the game ended when I was still immersed and enjoying myself. It's not a big deal anyway as the game was good to the last drop for me.
Considering that the game lasts merely about an hour, the full price may be too high for some people, but from the perspective of a point & click adventure games' fan, I think the price it's fair. To be honest, I'll definitely buy this game again for 5 bucks if I could, just to show my appreciation to the devs.

7/10.   If you enjoy story driven games, this game is a good fit.  A well fleshed out storyline with excellent voice acting, cinematics, and live action gameplay.  I didn't find any silly time wasting quests or non-sensical gameplay at all.
I had no idea what the gameplay would involve, and it's an interesting mix.  You are a detective who becomes a ghost and needs to find out who killed you and why. So, lots of investigations.  To me, the investigative parts of the game are most like a hidden object game.  You walk around a small area and find the clues to solve the inquiry.  Very straightforward.  There is a bit of action involved with demons to dispose of. You play stealthy while sneaking up on them.  Later in the game, it gets more intense with up to 4 demons simultaneously and can be a little challenging to sneak up on.
There are clues, letters, special bad guy info bits, historical parts, human mind reading, and some side quests too.  I didn't enjoy these as much.  They just aren't interesting and add little to the game story.  Mostly, the human mind reading gets boring to the point where I stopped bothering to read minds one third of the way through the game.  There are also ghost stories to unlock.  Some are good, some are so-so.  I liked the asylum one best.  Those are optional and require going through the rooms quite a bit more to search out hidden unlockables.  If anything was time wasting, that was it.  But, it's not mandatory.
To me, the story dragged up until about halfway.  After the cemetery I was hooked and kept on playing without any lack of interest. Before then, I was getting a bit bored, so slow gameplay and story up until midway.
Two things that stood out to me that may interest others:
1) It's not an adventure game.  Don't go in expecting an adventure game of any kind.  This wasn't clear to me from the onset until I had been playing a bit.
2) If you like action or fast paced horror games, this may not be for you.  This game is laid back, not terribly scary, and takes it's time.  More for the detective story fans IMO and fans of hidden secrets.
The ending is good and don't watch a vid of it please or it really ruins the experience.  If the initial half of the game wasn't so slow and a bit scarier, I would probably rate it higher. Still a good game, lots of love went into it, and it's optimized very well too.

I absolutely ADORE this game! It is definitely, without a doubt, one of my favorite games.  I just love the art style, the soundtrack, the gameplay, the characters, the story, EVERYTHING! The story made me both laugh and cry and I was drawn into it from the get-go (although I could have lived without that romantic sub-plot). I still get back to this game at times and still love every minute of it.
However, I believe that the ranking system is completely broken and I wish it had gone in another direction. It is only based on how many rounds you complete the mission on, which means that you can just basically rush it to the finish line with one character, not kill a single enemy, and get an A-rank. To me, that’s just mind-boggling, because why design such an incredibly satisfying combat system with so many different mechanics which make way for so many different dynamics?  I mean, when I first discovered that I could kill two or three enemies at once by either placing a bomb between them or carefully positioning my stormtrooper in a way that the missing shots still would hit another enemy behind, I felt like a BADASS.  I really took time planning my route, placing my troops on the field and making sure I kill all enemies on as few rounds as possible.  For me, it was like playing an intense game of chess.
Many times I would have completely swept the field clean of enemies and completed the mission on less than 3 rounds. I would lean back proudly in my chair after the match and think that there is no way I could get anything other than an A-rank and later see a B or C-rank pop up on my screen. It was so frustrating that I was not rewarded for actually making most out of the combat system and being really skilled at it. All I needed to do was to pick a scout and run to the finish line to get an A-rank. WHY?!?! It is like playing a game of chess with the main goal being to reach the other side as quickly as possible. So you could just pick a chess piece and make sure it reaches the side unharmed, but you would totally miss the whole strategic gameplay aspect which is the essence of chess and what made chess so popular.

The fact that they have a trait on a character that will most of the times, if activated on the field, chose not to shoot an enemy because she a pacifist is just beyond me. It was extremely annoying and it did not suit my play style so I would most of the times just reload my last save until she actually shoots the enemy I want.
It is clear that this game would like to show another side of war that is not centered on killing every troop out there, which I would accept if the gameplay wasn’t so freaking good and if there were actually different secret routes you could take to reach the finish line quickly.
Even if the ranking system is one major issue I have with the game, Valkyria Chronicles still is one of my favorite games and very dear to me. Hopefully we will see a sequel sometime soon!

PVP - Granted, server lag was HORRIBLE, but we did end up in a few battles with dudes last night. Overall, we r3kt those guys, but it was definitely worth saying that I can't really judge it until servers get fixed.

I can see how this game might disappoint others, as there is so much more it could do as a survival horror and as a detective game, but for what it is, I think this is a brilliant game, and there are enough items and secrets to find to give it replay value. I guess because of the different path options of another certain "poltergeist simulator" if you like i.e. Beyond Two Souls it is often a shame when I play games like this now and there aren't multiple endings (even Silent Hill 2 had different endings on replays), but I guess we are a little spoilt, and this isn't trying to be a David Chase or a Deus Ex game.
The idea itself was so novel and appealing I knew I had to grab this eventually, it reminded me of the basic premise of the old PS2 game Shadow of Memories in which you travel back in time to solve your own murder. In this moody, supernatural almost LA Noire style of setting I knew I couldn't resist. It wasn't until I played it I realised it's all set in Salem, so given that the backstory and local folklore have a large presence in this game, this was one hell of a bonus for me given my interest in the witch hunts and magic.
The music and atmosphere didn't disappoint. The backstory and tragic history is incorporated into it very well, and the way in which this game combined supernatural elements with crime scene investigation was really inventive and original.  As said, there are things you can miss as well, but this is mostly side missions. I guess few games if any have really matched LA Noire in this department.
The graphics look great, can't fault the voice acting either. In terms of the horror elements, as a puzzle game it's challenging enough, but seeing the same ghouls everywhere gets very repetitive very quickly, and it just becomes a chore of running, hiding and timing. It's different enough but just has no variety, still I can see how hard it is to do something really novel and inventive with the ghost-themed survival horror format. Especially if you are a ghost yourself.
Overall great game worth getting, worth experiencing and worth playing again, just don't be too disappointed by the length and lack of variety in gameplay....Salem does allow for some exploration, though.

Soul Suspect is a good, unique game with an interesting story.
First thing I'll say is that if you dont like being confined within a level boundary or anything like that then you probably wont like this game. Yes you play a ghost and can walk through many walls, but you cant walk through all of them, obviously you have to be kept in the game somehow, and I accepted that and enjoyed it.
The game is humerous, has some funny dialogue and is a slow paced mystery game as you attempt to solve your murder as well as several other peoples in the game.
You can take control of people in the investigation, gain information from them, then use all the clues you found to build a picture of what happened.
You will investigate several crime scenes throughout the game, some are to do with the main story, and several are just extra investigations there for fun.
There are plenty of collectables in the game to help form a backstory, you dont have to collect them but they are good as they give you a history on the main character and the town you are in. The town being Salem and is heavily centred around the Salem Witch Trials.
There are several areas in the game in which you will do your main investivations, when completed you can always revisit them to look for things you didnt find before.
There are nice details throughout the game like random ghosts that are just there in the background and vanish as you get close to them, other ghosts that you can help to move on, and even ghostly buildings, such as original structures that no longer exist in the real world but you cannot pass through them as they are real to you.
If you want to play something a bit different, with a unique story, humour and lots of collectables for you to find then give Murdered: Soul Suspect a go.
I may not play this game again as the fun is in the mystery and trying to work out what has happened, but its still good to play a first time.

Overview: Adventure
Watch the movie Ghost, replace Patrick Swayze with an ex criminal cop and replace Whoopi Goldberg with a teenager, throw in some supernatural elements and you have the basic foundation for Murdered Soul Suspect.
The gameplay is a mixture between investigating areas for evidence and stealth sections. Investigating areas is basic, you walk around until you get to item/object you can interact with. A few times you are given a list of clues and must select the right clues in order to advance, as far as I can tell there is no way you can fail any of these. No matter how many times you get it wrong the game will always let you keep choosing until you get it right. As a dead man you have a few tricks which you can use, such as possessing people to influence them or causing disturbances in the environment to distract people.
The second portion of gameplay involves stealth which can be a bit frustrating at times but it does help break up the gameplay a bit. Every once in a while you will have to hide from demons, luckily, if they see you, you can easily run and hide in hiding spots until they decide to stop searching for you. Sneaking up from behind and pressing the appropriate buttons will kill them.
The game is also littered with collectables that give back-story to characters or provide history of the surrounding locations.
There are a few side quests but they are very basic and amount to nothing more than investigating an area until you found everything.
This is not an action game. If you enjoy point and click adventure games you will find this somewhat enjoyable. The problem is this game offers very little puzzle solving and the entire game can be completed in 4-6 hours. I do however commend Square Enix for publishing a game like this.

Crusader kings 2... an incredibly involving, steep learning curved, heartless, bloodthirsty strategy game that has me pulling what little hair i have left out.
Reasons for my hate:
The tutorials are difficult to learn from, guiding you through things in a step by step manner but without imparting understanding of when to use what tools.  I learned more from a single let's play from its first 30 minutes than i did from going through the tutorials twice.
The difficulty curve is insane.  I have tried starting on what has been said to be some of the easiest starting points in the game, primarily in Wales and in Ireland.  Every single ♥♥♥♥ing time I try to unite the kingdom, I get ♥♥♥♥ed over royally pretty quickly.  My first games I managed to unite Wales and then just get run over by england, and only in the last couple attempts did I avoid that.  I then went ahead and tried Ireland, only to barely get it united before revolts and all my hard work gets undone (regardless of using my vassals armies and not my own or not).  This last game I've finally managed the most I had for a while, Getting both the kingdom of Ireland and Wales at the same time, in spite of a ♥♥♥♥ing rubber banding army strength of Scotland to pretty much always match my own army strength, regardless of improvements or losses from wars, and then I get a revolt I cannot prevent despite going over ten saves back to try and redo things, and then a war comes from Scotland and England to try and claim Ireland.
This game has been ♥♥♥♥ing conspiring to ensure that no matter what I do, within 200 years everything gets undone and all of my time has been wasted.  There's no difficulty setting or slider, and rather than feeling 'oh, i could have done something else', I feel that the game is rigged.  Even if I don't know enough about the game's designs, if a player gets to the point after numerous attempts of doing things differently or trying to learn and still fails, then feels like the game's cheating them, that's bad design.  I don't give a damn about how much there is for me to do in it anymore because it never ♥♥♥♥ing matters.
tl;dr
-No Difficulty adjustment
-Ruthless AI
-Acheivements in territory easily undone
-Difficult to learn on your own
-So much wasted time
-Requires Rogane
-Tests sanity effectively.

An excellent choice for anyone with a love of strategy games, political thriller, or murdering babies.
If you've never played a Paradox Grand Stategy game before, they are quite expansive while also being a complete mess in UI-terms, which is pretty much true of Crusader Kings II.  You will have no idea what in the world you are doing, what button does what, or why things happen until you've clocked in over a hundred hours.  With a buggy and less-than-helpful tutorial that apparently doesn't work on the demo, you're either going to learn from many, many mistakes or by viewing the numerous Let's Plays or tutorials on the internet.  The game is also very menu-based, which could be a turn off for quite a number of people.  The map rarely matters unless you are moving troops around or looking to see where the various realms are located.
Past that barrier of entry is quite the enjoyable experience, thankfully.  Hundreds of years of medieval history at your fingertips to mold and shape, to drive woefully off course or to just watch as the AI manages to do that itself (The Scots conquered England?  Sure, why not!).  It is not a game that sets goals for you, however, you must make your own.  Will you raze all of Europe to the ground as the Mongols, or resurrect the Roman Empire?  Expand your domain across all the known world, or stay a small nation that tries to weather the tempest around it?  Reclaim Jerusalem for the Jewish people, or elect an Inbred son as the Pope?
And yes, there is baby killing.  And regular killing.  You will enter this game thinking your have morals, but you will leave it having the blood of hundreds of innocents on your hands, for the sake of 'realm stability', to get your more intelligent son on the throne, or maybe just because they refused to come to your feast.  You will also be killed quite frequently, from jealous kinsmen to angry peasants.
Also you can now get horses or cats to be the Pope, which is pretty cool.

It's a sort of strategic storyline simulator with heavy emphasis on intrigue, warfare and diplomacy. You control a character who is the member of a dynastic house in the middle ages. You may start as a powerful emperor of a vast realm, a mild-mannered duke or count with a modest holding, or a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with little hope of success. When your character dies, you control his heir, and when that heir dies, you control his heir, and so on. If you have no heirs and your death results in your titles being lost to another house, the game ends. The central objective of the game is to promote your house's survival and success among competing factions within your empire and enemies without.
At this time I have about 480 hours on CK2. Each playthrough is about 80-150 hours for me, so I've played 4 complete games from start to finish, and about halfway through a fifth.
I've spent about 20% of my time managing my family: marrying off daughters, raising wards, boosting traits and skills. Another 30% I'd spend on warfare: putting down revolts, seizing new land from neighbors, and the occaisonal crusade (really crusades are probably the least important thing in crusader kings). The remaining 50% of the time I'm investigating factions within my realm, weakening the powerful dukes, placating the unhappy dukes, and destroying or imprisoning the dukes who are both powerful and unhappy.
Graphics are good for a strategy game. For the most part you're looking at a map of Europe and moving numbers around on it. The significant AI computations for the hundreds of characters on the map probably tax your system enough as it is. The interface has some quirks and inefficiencies but it's still very managable. The sound effects are acceptable, though if you didn't already, you'll learn to hate screaming babies.

Let's split this up:
First, the game itself. It's a strategy RPG with a wild, sometimes self-referential plot, several jokes, references to movies and TV shows, led by a lovable cast of characters. Gameplay wise, the game's main feature is the possibility to take the characters all the way to level 9999(yes, four nines in a row), several over the top attacks, combo possibilities, and the geo-panel system, all adding to a highly replayable game.
Combined with the "Item World", where you can go through randomized stages to strenghen your gear and even acquire some of the strongest in the game, and with the several endings and new game +, this will keep fans of JRPGs entertained for hundreds of hours. I had over 250 of those back in the PS2. Highly recommended.
Granted, some mechanics are rather dated, but there's nothing obnoxious enough to disturb the enjoyment of the game.
Now, the port. Look, it's a 13 year old game. The original was on the PS2, and this version is based on the PSP port. Personally, I expected the game to be a straight port and locked to 30fps, and I would have been fine with that for this game, but they added new surface textures, a new interface, and high quality character portraits. The character sprites themselves have not been touched, and offer the same pixelized style from back in the day, witth an optional "filter" that basically blurs the images(meh).
Otherwise, the game has no real resolution options, but seems to run at your desktop resolution when in fullscrenn, and has a "Depth of Field" and "Background Blur", which to me, end up just bluring the top and the bottom of screen, and an option for SSAO, which at the very least makes the game jitery.
Upon release, there were random performance issues, but the first patch seems to have fixed most of those. Avoid the needless SSAO option and it should run fine. I barely scratched the surface of what the game offers with this review, and can't recommend this game enough.

Stellar optimization work from NIS! Now that the ugliness of pre-patch Disgaea PC is behind us, I can comment on the game proper.
Disgaea PC is a remake of the oldest entry in the Disgaea series: Disgaea 1. More specifically, it's a remaster of the PSP release, Afternoon of Darkness. The good news is that the new graphical editions are welcome ones: new backgrounds being the main draw. Sadly, some very simple additions that could have improved benefitial are lacking. Most glaringly, there's no in-cutscene "skip cutscene" button, which is a feature every Disgaea game from 2PSP onward had that made things much less frustrating. The game is also extremely slow compared to later entries, lacking the high-speed movement and camera options that later games possessed.
All-in-all, Disgaea PC's biggest shortcomings lay in the fact that it's a straight port for all practical purposes and doesn't include anything that would help make the game feel like it was released in 2016. Additions like more camera options, higher movement speed, a skip-cutscene button, and the improved "cancel options" system from later games could have helped bring this dated game into the modern era of Disgaea.
All that said, however, if you can get past the datedness of the game's mechanics, you've got a really solid SRPG on your hands here, and a new definitive starting point to the series. It's a wonderful title in a wonderful series, just be prepared to feel a bit irritated by the age of the experience. This is a faithful rerelease. For better and for worse.

Being a fan of ETS2 (nearly 400 hours played), I can't be disappointed in this game. SCS has stepped up the technical aspect on ATS not only offering breath-taking visuals and better performance while keeping the same specs, but also other minor options that are very wel appreciated by enthusiasts of these kind of experience.
I love how now they've added the real gear patterns for EF transmissions. Long are the days of modifying .sii files to obtain this. Other cool options like a toggle engine brake were added as well, among other little things that while insignificant, always made you wish they were there on ETS2.
The map is simply fantastic in terms of detailing. Sure it's smaller, but remember this is the beginning. Also, compared to ETS2, this map is not repetitive at all. In ETS2 you had the same pre-fabricated highway and almost all the cities were square-shaped and look-alike.
Trucks are okay. Only two, but they are very well detailed and further in the progress you can unlock many parts for them. There is also the option for mods, thanfully.
Physics are still a bit floaty, and not what I would consider simulation, but taking in mind that you drive really slow, it doesn't bother me at all. That's if you're playing the game as it was meant to be played; with wheel, shifter and pedals. Speaking of which, getting yourself a Logitech wheel is a DEFINITIVE MUST is you wish to enjoy this at its full. ETS2 made me buy one last year and I have not regret it one bit.
Sound isn't too impressive. I am an audiophile, and also very sabby when it comes to cars, trucks and engines in general. Call me OCD, but if there is somethign I do not forgive in simulators or car games in general, is bad sounds. They've got the samples right, but the pitch on them is all over the place. Often, the truck sounds like it's reving higher in 1200rpm than it is in 1700rpm. That's what's called a loop effect, and it's just a sign of laziness on the sound developer. Thankfully, as with trucks, there are mods to fix this (which I have thanks to a friend who is also probably the best sound modder in the truck Simulator series).
My last thoguht would be that for all giving a negative review. Don't see ATS as a new game, but see it as a new platform. Remember how ETS started and how it slowly grew with time. ATS is the same. New states will be added, as well as trucks. In a year this game will be massive. And hey, you're paying $20 bucks for this wonderful experience, which is also an indicative that the game is still in expansion.
And last, don't discard ETS2. ATS as it stands now is just an expansion to it. If you see it that way your complains will be unfounded.

Period games are always a pleasure to experience for the effort put into their style. High fantasy and glossy sci-fi are endless, so titles that hearken back to antiquity or forgotten decades bring a welcome change of pace. Projector Face makes the most of its Great Depression-era silent film look, and fortunately has enough adventure game substance to match the style.
From a forgotten attic in the woods comes The Projector, a peppy little reel-to-reel that you might remember from elementary school if you're as ancient as I am. Somehow The Projector forms a body out of a pile of old clothes and sets off in search of that most precious of treasures, friendship. This is easier said than done for a machine-man with no mouth, and that's where the puzzling in this adventure game comes in.
Every couple of screens you'll encounter scruffy children to befriend, but with no way to speak you cannot get their attention. Some exploring and puzzling in the area will reveal a film reel and bits of film you can splice together into a show for the children. The aforementioned puzzling is the usual finding/combining/using items, luckily with more sensical solutions than a lot of adventure games offer. You'll have plenty of challenges to overcome, with none holding you up for too long, I'd wager.
The charming story is told solely through actions and silent film title cards. It's a great feel for the game, especially paired with the dilapidated environments of the Great Depression. There are drawbacks to the silent film theme, though, as your mute protagonist cannot describe items or give any feedback on puzzle attempts besides shrugging. And while the art style is perfectly fine the animations are severely lacking, as is the sound design outside the old-tymey soundtrack.
Projector Face will last you about an hour, during which the story will run you through a surprising spread of emotions. It might not be particularly long or challenging but the puzzles are solid and getting things done is plenty gratifying. The game picks up once you start entertaining the children with your films, and has a few twists and turns before settling into the ending. Any fan of adventure games will find something to love in Projector Face, even if it is short and sweet.

This game, just this game.
I have so much praise for it that I don't even know where to begin, but I'll try to sound it off.
-The gameplay is a breath of fresh-air because it's this unique blend of third-person action game with occasional stealth elements and exploration based adventure game with some crime scene investigation and mild puzzle-solving thrown for good measure. I have trouble really classifying it because I've never played anything quite like it, and it really managed to form it's own gameplay identity instead of being a clone of something else or fitting neatly into a pre-defined gameplay genre.
-The graphics are also really pretty relative to how easy on the hardware it it. I was able to max it out (with AA turned off) at 1080p on a 750ti and it was rare that it dropped under FPS.
-The story is brilliant and actually managed to have a couple twists that I really didn't see coming because of the way it played with my expectations near constantly and intentionally set itself up for common tropes only to subvert or play with them.
-The art design is great and does this thing where it creates interesting eviroments by blending the real-world with ghostly left-overs of the past.
-It was interesting how it turned no-clip into a game mechanic.
-The bonus stuff like the side-missions and ghost stories were cool.
I guess there is some cons, though:
-The stealth sections can get tedious because the Demons tend to be a little to smart and aggressive, I often found myself trapped because they got stuck in the alert state and wouldn't go back to the posts no matter how well I stayed hidden.
-Some poor optimization, I know I said it runs well but it does tend to suffer from really inconsistant framerates, it can be at 55FPS one minute and 100FPS the next and the Vsync is useless because it looks it to 30FPS instead of to your screens refresh rate.
-Some of the items are to well hidden, I missed out on two of the Ghost Stories because I just could not find the last items for either, and one location even locked me out of room that the levels last item was presumably in.
-No kind of map, even though the "hub" area is pretty huge and maze-like.
-Short, I spent just over 10 hours on it and that was a playthrough with a lot of messing about and finding A LOT of the bonus items. I imagine it would be under 5 hours if you ignored the side-missions.
-Price, I think $30 is pushing it. I paid $4 during a sale and I'd say it's not worth more than $15, so wait for it to go on sale.

Unreal has quite simply got to be one of my favourite games of all time, they simply don't make games like they used to!
Back in 1998 Unreal had very impressive graphics and had far better gameplay than the likes of its rivals. The basic plot is that you, Prisoner 849, are aboard the the prision ship Vortex Rikers when it crashes on the planet Na Pali. From there on out you have to fight to survive as you trek across the planet looking for a way off.
Also included in this pack is the expansion "Return to Na Pali", which adds addtional content and game-play.
Unreal has recieved several updates from the community so the game can not only be played, but run at a decent level of graphical quality. Some of the models are a bit '1998' looking still, but even that is being worked on. There is of course many mods, maps, skins and all the usual community content out there to exend the game in ways you see fit.

I found myself getting stuck on level fifteen, this was the hardest level in the game, while the game is short, it's just the right length before the gameplay started to feel stale.
I am very much looking forward to playing RIP 2; hopefully this will add some more mechanics.
Definitely recommend trying this title.

RIP is a 2d top-down defence game. The premise of the game is to defend against hords of enemies using your rotateable turret. You can pick one of three characters, each having a unique trait. Characters can't be switched in-between levels, so once you pick one you have to stick with them until you complete the game. Each level starts with you with a simple machine gun, while other weapons need to be collected from special enemies (ie  ones carrying containers). Weapons have unlimited ammo, but still need to be reloaded between clips. Other pick ups include health,nuke and shield. You have limited health, which when depleted will end the game and force you either to restart the level or go to the main menu. Experience is earned through killing foes and when you level up from enough of it, you can choose a permanent perk (e.g. increase health/damage/fire rate) You can choose to replay the levels you previously completed up to with the same perks you chose previously.There are various enemies such as close range guys, range, explosives etc. The music and sound effects are quite forgettable. Furthermore, the graphics aren't good (ie. very low detailed) either. There is no storyline to the game.
With a plethora of better defence games on the market, I recommend you buy them instead and give this a miss.

American Truck Simulator was a long awaited gem and did not fail to impress upon it's release. It handles reminiscent of Euro Truck Simulator 2 just a change of scenery and vehicles. For being released a little less than a week the modding community has been busy and has released many high quality trucks and mods to improve upon an already great experience.
Pros
-The sounds are much more full than they are in the games European counterpart, these trucks actually sound like trucks.
-The scenery is breath taking and nostalgic, capturing the atmosphere of the west coast pretty well.
-The mod community has been busy and released many great mods.
-The ability to control just how much simulation you want at any given time.
-Great price.
-Everchanging map due to the upcoming release of Arizona and other states DLC
-The music that you can find in the radiostations enhances the experience.
-Weight stations where you can be called to have a truck inspection.
Cons
-Traffic AI can definitely use some polishing.
-The railroad crossings are taken straight from ETS2 and repainted.
-Police AI need some polishing (these kind of things can be expected from a brand new release.
-Unless you have TrackIR, or patience enough to use hat controls, looking around to see oncoming traffic can be a pain in the neck.
-You only start with two types of trucks (though customizable many different ways), mods can help fix that and SCS plans to release more trucks for free in future updates.
ATS has many features that ETS2 did and some of its very own.
-Ability to manage multiple garages, trucks and hire drivers/run your own company.
-Radiostations with relevant radio stations such as country, classic rock, metal, alternative and other genres.
-Weight stations, sometimes it will require you to pull in to get a truck inspection.
-Pretty good recreations of landmarks such as the golden gate bridge.
-The ability to do some pretty heavy customization/personalization of your truck, mods further enhancing this.
-Many more
If you were a fan of Euro Truck Simulator 2, you'll definitely like American Truck Simulator, the game is well worth $20.00 in my opinion and i really find it enjoyable, being able to drive around on such a wide open expanse, with your choice of music is therapeutic in nature and is really good for stress relief and escapism.
The attention to detail is great and you can get some true enjoyment from it. I'd definitely reccomend this game to any simulation fan, it's a really enjoyable experience and has alot of future potential as well.

When I first played Unreal I was just a stupid kid. I hated this game as a kid. I couldnt' get used to the movement, the enemy AI and guns at the time. But I recently bought Unreal and Unreal Tournament 99 and 2004 on GOG. So I thought I should do a review that gives the game justice.
Unreal basically is a game where you are a prisoner that crash lands on a planet. Your goal is to get out alive. You go from alien ship to building killing loads of enemies while solving puzzles with fast precise movement and strafing. Not plot heavy, but hey, it's a old school FPS it doesn't need to.
Now that I'm 20, I love this game to death. I play the DRM free version of it actually. The main reason I love this game is because it's old school. I love the old school genre of FPS Games like Serious Sam, Doom, Blood 2, Painkiller, and recently DUSK.
The movement is so amazing. It feels like you are actually experiencing an earthquake at one point and that is just an achievement in it's own right. The movement is one of the best things about the game. I love it.
The enemy AI is some of the best I have ever encountered in a video game, they are difficult to kill, but yet they seem fair to the challenge of the entire game. When you kill a boss, it feels like you are strong and have accomplished something.
The graphics are amazing too (Well, in 1998) As with Half Life's Gold Source Engine, Unreal uses it's Unreal Engine 1, making it revolutionary for the time being. Many other engines followed in the coming years leading to Unreal Tournament 4 (Or UT 2017) which has continued the arena based shooter franchise.
Overall, the game is fantastic is still holds up with the original Unreal Tournament.
But before I end my review, I want you people to stay away from the Sequel Unreal 2 The Awakening. It ruined any chance of a Unreal 3 due to it's clunky shooting and slow movement controls and bascially having nothing to do with the original Unreal. It was obviously made for consoles as it was released on Xbox. But Unreal Championship was like a launch title and that was better than Unreal 2!
Whatever. I'll just stop my blabbering here. BUY THE GAME! :D

The RIP Trilogy, along with the other Meridian4 games, are among the first games I've bought here on Steam. Most games published by Meridian4 are 'OK' games. As far as I know none of the games are amazing but none of them are garbage aswell. Same goes for the RIP trilogy.
The RIP Trilogy, obviously exists of three games:
-RIP
-RIP2:Strike Back
-RIP3:The Last Hero
All three games are pretty much the same; Kill all spawning enemies, Pick up powerups/weapons and level up. The only real difference I can come up with would be the fact you controll a stationary base cannon in RIP(1), whereas in the other two games you'll be able to walk around and in later in the game, you will be able to controll vehicles.
Gameplay is standard but fun and quite addictive. You could compare it to 'Crimsonland' which, most likely took this game as an example. The weird thing though, while many people rate Crimsonland positively, I do not get the negative ratings about this trilogy. It's obvious a lot more work has been involved in the RIP-Trilogy compared to Crimsonland, just look at the screenshots.
The RIP-Trilogy is not perfect and it's not for everyone but I believe fans of the genre won't be dissapointed.

I fitting sequel to an amazing game.

Of course this is a personal review, you may not share my opinion but I honestly feel this game was made for me.
Renegade and Paragon dialougue options are more important than ever and the choices feel relevant and can genuinely have a massive impact on character interactions. You are either the devil or the angel on Shepards shoulders.
Now, at first I was a bit uncomfortable with the combat changes, eg. ammo replacing the overheat system. It didn't take long to settle into it however, ammo was never scarce and I loved the satifaction of knocking back enemies with a shockwave. I think it has improved over the previous but I do miss the weapon customization.
Omni-gel is gone, replaced with two mini games for hacking and bypassing which was a tad annoying but they were never stupidly difficult. It was a relief to not have to stack up on omni gel or convert weapons when you reach the item limit. The research system works well but unfortunately meant madatory planet scanning. Planet scanning was a slow process but the need to improve is essential and you will know why.
There are loads of lovely personal touches sprinkled throughout the game and the choices from ME1 do translate very well into ME2.  I won't go over the DLC to avoid spoilers but I very much recommend Lair of the Shadow Broker, especiialy if you are a fan of Liara.
And of course, this game is stunning to look at. My favourite place would be Illium.
I reommend this game to the mass relays and back.

First of all, make sure you play the first game before playing this in order to get the most out of the narrative experience. There's an important thematic transition that takes place between the first game's winter setting and this game's blossoming springtime. I guess the idea is Death/Despair to Life/Hope.
Anyway, this is an interesting series. Metro 2033 is a full-on survival horror game, linear and story driven, similar to Half-Life in structure. The sequel, Last Light, while identically linear, places a heavier emphasis on stealth and action - with the human factions having a stronger gameplay and story presence - with less focus on the solitary horror type scenarios of the first game.
If you're like me, and are the kind of player who generally shuns horror games, then you'll be pleased to hear that this game and its predecessor are two standout exceptions to my general boycott of the genre. While one or two levels were uncomfortable to play, the story and context were grounded and engrossing enough to encourage me to press on. That's an unusual turn for these games to take, as I tend to strongly dislike the feeling of being in a rat maze that most scary games tend to engender. It's a testament to the well-told story and truly immersive gameplay found in both of these games.
Sorry for the stream-of-thought review. I'm really tired and can't think very clearly. Just wanted to pop in and drop a strong recommendation to anyone reading this - even those who typically shun scary games. Think of this as part two of one long game.

Definitely a beginner early access title, maybe a bit early for that as well, due to the amount of content I wouldn't have bought it if I didn't trust Funcom. They never disappointed me in other games, so I hope for the best in the future.
Bugs, lags, lack of content: if you don't tolerate them, don't even open games with the early access sign and leave now, because you'll pull out every single hair you have. Or still have.
ARK: I didn't want to compare them. Seriously. But the crafting, leveling (and how it handles death) system is just the exact copy which is a good system, but still a major let down to me. I didn't want to purchase a reskin of a game I already own, so I'm seriously considering a refund until it gets out of EA.
Shelter system: I hope more weather effects or attack of monsters will come in the future, where you need to get into cover to survive. It adds a meaning to the whole building proccess. Right now you have to get cover from the sandstorm, which really is scary. And fun! I love sandbox games, but they usually feel like two different games: lego and survival. The two rarely has anything to do with each other. If this shelter thing and altars to the gods where you can give them sacrifices, wheels where you can break your thralls is the direction this game goes, it's a certain success. Meaningful/useful buldings and decorations otside of crafting stations and walls, that's what I miss from other survival games.
Story: I love the idea of huge tablets containing hidden lore, but right now there really is nothing deep. I definetly hope for more, the locations are perfect for it. I still shiver when I think of the huge arena entrance guarded by the giant snake or the huge cavern full of spiders. I still have questions after finding some ruins full of newly built building stands and people. Are they rebuilding? Harvesting the stone? What happens there? Why are they surrounded by werewolf like creatures? Why is the city full of dragons? All of these cry for lore and friendly (?) npcs, gods, journals, quests, whatevers, a narrative and it seems to me the map was designed with this is mind. Most sandboxes only make you move and leave your settlement for more resources, I hope this time there's gonna be story to the places you visit as well. I found an aquaduct, which had a lore table, even though it was short, it instantly made the game more immersive.
The thrall system is super awesome, the religion aspect as well. This game has a great potential, so even if you don't buy it, if you love the genre, keep an eye on it.
Oh and one more thing, as a female player: just... just... thank you. :D

Others have already talked about why this game was the defining moment in SRPG titles which bridged the quality gap from La Pucelle and ushered in a new era for gamers who like to beat the hell out of their game.
If you like SRPG titles at all, if you like extra challenges at all, if you enjoy the sheer joy of customizing your army of brohans and moeblobs to hell and back with a deep, intentionally abusable, system of skills and character growth: buy this game without any hesitation.
More than likely, however, you already own Disgaea on consoles/handhelds and you want to know how the port stacks up.
You will not see the loading screen at all while playing this game. I cannot ever hope to properly convey to you how much of a wonderful thing this is unless you go from the ps2 to this port and see the difference yourself.
This is orders of magnitude more important than any other feature added to the pc port: abusing the game's grinding mechanisms often requires constant recycling of levels to the point where one might suffer the thought that the loading screen is where one spends most of the time in the console version.
This pc version does not suffer that at all with the added benefit of a large screen to experience the game with.
There are crashes; as they fix some issues with the game for others, they've been introducing new crashes for those with no problems. As far as I can tell, the majority of these crashes can, at the time of this writing on March 6th, be avoided by turning off all of the pc specific features, but many users have reported a memory leak that will randomly strike.
The devs have not abandoned us and have been steadily pumping out patches and interacting with us on the forums; I am not worried at all about the future of this title.
With this in mind, should you buy the port?
Absolutely. This is the definitive version of this game and any bugs that exist are steadily being addressed.
If you haven't played this game yet, you will likely be better served by other reviews which talk about core mechanics, but I should mention that you will find no better SRPG series available on pc (and, perhaps, beyond).

Sometimes it's hard to make new friends. Sometimes it's hard to even talk to someone. And how it must be hard when you're all alone, you don't know who you are and you have a movie projector instead of your face.
Projector Face is essentially a traditional point & click adventure game true to the concept of Adventure Game Studio engine. However it brings some unique concepts to its genre. The hero, a sort of a projector-man, decides to leave his solitude and comes into town to look for new friends … for anyone to speak with. Soon he discovers it’s hard to speak with someone, because ... in fact, he can’t speak at all. And the only way how to say something is to play a movie from his projector. It’s not so easy though, he needs to find a perfect spot to show the movie on and collect all movie pieces to stick it together. In this moment the game has elements of hidden object, because the pieces of film are sometimes quite hidden. Playing the entire movie can be done in certain places only and without this show for local children, which is always really surprising for them, game can’t proceed.
All is followed by a very nice stylized hand-drawn graphics, and although the authors suggest that a simple character animation is caused by a low budget, I think it fits the game well. Story is narrated by illustrated frames like from the silent film era with nice background music during play.
Overall I must say that despite its very short playing time I enjoyed playing the game and generally this topic makes you think more about movies, art and how it communicates with us.

Pros:

-The word "incompetence" will be the word that hangs in your head after playing. I doubt they knew what a video game IS.
-You are narrowed down to two missions, one of them being a TUTORIAL.
-Apparently, there's a map rotation for that one mission, but as much as I've seen, it's a straight-up lie. Sea of Fire is the only scenario in this game available to non-premium members.

I remember playing Fable the lost chapters after having read in a magazine about all the cool stuff you could do.
Unfortunately for me, I believed it was only for Xbox, which I didn't have at the time. I then turned my head in a Best Buy and my eyes widened. It was for Windows! I asked for it, as I was so excited. This was one of the few times my mom allowed me
what I begged for. I asked if I could go to the car early just so I could look at the manual (I was that excited).
As soon as I got home, I played Fable. Unfortunately, our computer's GPU could only muster the game on the lowest settings. The ground and sky was whitish (though contours of the ground were still visible). The effects were gone, and it was quite lifeless thinking back. However, what mattered at the time was the little adventure in there that I played for countless hours alongside the original Halo CE.
This is a very good Action RPG. The "good and evil" aspect of it is pretty loosely tied with what actually happens or matters in the game. Whether you're good or evil matters very little beyond appearance.
Personally, I consider it a classic game of it's time that's overshadowed by the pure mediocrity of it's sequels
(however, fable II wasn't that awful I guess).
The interface is a little limited, and suffers a bit due to it's age, however, when you're playing, who cares?
It's still satisfying to shoot your overpowered (but well earned) magic, as well as swing around a weapon you just found
that doesn't do as much damage, but just looks that cool.
It's a game that accomplished what an action RPG involving a silent protagonist ( I think it would have been interesting to put in sex/race options, as building a character you identify with would be assisted by such options for some players).
The writing's pretty crappy, and the world is somewhat unbelievable, but it is in that we can enjoy the camp of it.
We can focus on the hilarity of quicksaving and slashing someone down in a quick strike and taking out the pretty pathetic guards that try to stop you raiding pie stores and weapon shops.
There's something inherently enjoyable about that.
It set the standard for me when it came to building a character in an ARPG (something that has yet to be truly exceeded, as most ones we play today are either first person, or have a preset character.
You don't take the actualy character motivations seriously because the world is just too much like a storybook to care about anything more complex than a simple fight between good and evil (and there is no in between, and they treat it more like they support different football teams than a true moral dilemma).
I think it's great for a first play through for both good and evil though, however I already played this years ago.
Thinking about it, I wish I'd saved my money, as I don't see myself ever playing this one again.
However,I don't know how well this has truly aged, or whether more seasoned RPG players will dig it.
If you've never played, I'd pick this up on a sale, and give a simple, fun, immersive, and memorable playthrough.
Otherwise, really think about whether you're going to play through this game again.

This cute little bartering game, with optional extras, is a cute time passer. So your dad is out to save the world, cool right? WRONG! Anyways, this leaves you alone with the choice of having everything you know and own reposessed, or working for a slave-driving fairy in an item shop she puts together in your house so you're not forced to live in a card board box. Recettear in a nut shell is like I said before a bartering RPG. You constantly sell items hopeing to have enough to pay back your next deadline. The value of items constantly changes as time goes by and the story is fun with a 'special' kind of humor. I enjoyed it, but it's not for everyone. You work for the merchant guild, but there is an adventurers guild. The adventurers in said guild can give you a chance to go into short dungeons as a chance to gain more items at a 100% profit margine. My entire main story experiance took like 9 hours, I had to get the swing of things at first, but after I caught some momentum it was a breeze keeping up with every deadline amount including the last one before the deadline is a problem. I really only entered the dungeon twice, maybe 3 times. Just long enough to beat 2 bosses, which were both easy. I mostly just sold items at a great profit margine using increased priced items and did more then fine speeding right on through the game. Definatly worth the $10 I spent! (It was on sale)

Quick Review:
This is the basic game I remember playing on the original XBox. Both fun and frustrating at times.
Pros
- Installs and launches flawlessly under Windows 7 Professional (my first concern, didn't see it addressed anywhere else)
- Supports high resolution, AA, and high textures/details (just be sure to disable VSync)
- No hesitations, hiccups, etc (unlike Fable Anniversary)
- Has the original, cartoonish graphics that just go better with the atmosphere of the game
Cons
- Only (natively) supports the use of keyboard and mouse
** You CAN get around this by using 3rd party keyboard to controller mapping (xpadder, CTK, JoyToKey, etc)
- Saving is a bit screwy (I may be mis-remembering this though), see bottom of review for details
- Does not have Steam Accomplishments/Badges
Bottom line, pay the $10 for this version and you don't have the "better" graphics that actually make the game look worse. You won't have the slow-downs, stuttering, etc, You'll need to look into a keyboard to joystick program if you are dead set on using a gamepad, but the game is easily played with keyboard and mouse.
A Note On Saving: This game has set savepoints that you must reach or your progress is lost.
Examples:
- Starting the Game: Finish a few quests to get Gold to purchase a gift... but if you complete only two of these quests and quit, you have to start over. You have to complete the town to get an "Autosave"
- Guild Training: Go through the basics and a few tests, but don't complete the final step of getting your badge? Too bad, even if you saved mid-level, you now have to start the training over from the very beginning.
Basically, you need to fully complete quests to the point that you see the words "AUTOSAVING" (or something like that) appear on screen.
BUY THIS VERSION AND NOT THE ANNIVERSARY EDITION!!! This one will never be on sale, but at $10... it's a steal!

It's not often that a game reaches deep down inside you and pulls at your gut like Valkyria Chronicles does. The art is amazing, blurring the lines between hand drawn and animated, blending the best parts of a visual novel with the motion of anime. The voice acting is superb, featuring well-known artists such as Fred Tatasciore (Incredible Hulk), Nolan North (Desmond Miles, Deadpool), and Laura Bailey (Serana TESV). The story is gripping. It depicts the small, resource-rich nation of Gallia torn between two military superpowers as they try to remain neutral. You watch the polar-opposite characters grow into a tight-nit family as they are called from their humble daily lives to the seemingly unassailable defense of Gallia as Squad 7, 3rd Regiment of the Gallian Militia. In the midst of a humble video game story set in a fantasy world, you will find yourself reexaming your opinions toward the second world war, allowing the story to open up venues of understanding that you may have missed the first time around in history class.
All in all, this is a game that I can unequivocally recommend. It's both familar, and new. Do yourself a favor: buy all of the special reports from the embedded reporter and play them as you go. Also, watch the credits through to the very, very end. You will not regret it.

You play as a cop with a family history in gang violence. While tracking down the Bell Killer you wind up being killed by him. Now you must master your new ghost powers to solve the mystery of who the Bell Killer is.
The game has an interesting story and presents it very well. All the different ghost mechanics work quite nicely and really give the game some uniqueness. The atmospheric graphic imagery and sound do a great job at being creepy while staying true to both the spirit world and the living world.
KILL DEMONS!! How about no... I mean combat is done in a pure stealth approach by hiding and taking them down, but overall it ends up feeling like a giant gimmick to make the game double the length. The sheer amount of waiting you have to do is just annoying during these sequences. I don't mind the demon floor traps, but the actual demons looking for you I removed with an ini edit. Here's how to make yourself invisible to them so you can just ignore fighting demons.
Go to...
...\Murdered Soul Suspect\FateGame\Config
Open...
DefaultAIPerceptionData.ini
Change...
StimTypes=(TypeName=Player,BaseTypeName=Ghost,Result_Awareness=High)
To...
StimTypes=(TypeName=Player,BaseTypeName=Ghost,Result_Awareness=Unaware)
I tried to spoil as little as possible during this review. The great atmosphere and piecing of clues together while doing using your ghostly abilities is pretty fun. It can occasionally feel under developed and shallow so you may find yourself thinking about how amazing this game could have been. I doubt it will get another similar game sequel, but I think another game that used these mechanics and improved on them would be a real treat.
I'd suggest not paying more then about $10 for this game. The story is great, but not all that long if you use the ini tweak and ignore combat along with ignoring the collectables.
