TL;DR: Great game. However, if Steam is on sale, consider buying the Fable Anniversary edition instead if you've never played the original. Better graphics.
By the time this review is written, Fable Anniversary costs about $3, while Fable TLC costs about $9.
------------
Fable offers much in its story and world-building. It tells you of a boy in a quest of a revenge and discovery of his family background. Fable is built upon the wondrous land of Albion, clearly inspired from medieval England with fantasy twist. With its quirky humor and distinctively English feel (from its music and architecture), Fable offers an interesting gameplay for those interested in story-driven RPGs where you can influence the world.
This is the game that introduced me to the wonder of freedom of choice in RPG. Coming from playing JRPGs, I'm used to playing RPG like reading a book: following one story after another with side-stories in-between, doing errands, taking cities and NPCs in the game as it is.
When I played Fable, everything changed.
I can flirt with and marry townsfolks. I can steal items from shops. I can kill ordinary NPCs. I can make my fame (or infamy) not just through errands, but through little actions I did in the game. And what I did reflects on my alignment: the bad thing I do reflects on my dark side; the good thing reflects on light side. The world responds to my action. This seems to be common today, but back then in 2003 such feature is a rarity.
Great game. However, if Steam is on sale, consider buying the Fable Anniversary edition instead if you've never played the original. Better graphics.

American Truck Simulator was a long awaited gem and did not fail to impress upon it's release. It handles reminiscent of Euro Truck Simulator 2 just a change of scenery and vehicles. For being released a little less than a week the modding community has been busy and has released many high quality trucks and mods to improve upon an already great experience.
Pros
-The sounds are much more full than they are in the games European counterpart, these trucks actually sound like trucks.
-The scenery is breath taking and nostalgic, capturing the atmosphere of the west coast pretty well.
-The mod community has been busy and released many great mods.
-The ability to control just how much simulation you want at any given time.
-Great price.
-Everchanging map due to the upcoming release of Arizona and other states DLC
-The music that you can find in the radiostations enhances the experience.
-Weight stations where you can be called to have a truck inspection.
Cons
-Traffic AI can definitely use some polishing.
-The railroad crossings are taken straight from ETS2 and repainted.
-Police AI need some polishing (these kind of things can be expected from a brand new release.
-Unless you have TrackIR, or patience enough to use hat controls, looking around to see oncoming traffic can be a pain in the neck.
-You only start with two types of trucks (though customizable many different ways), mods can help fix that and SCS plans to release more trucks for free in future updates.
ATS has many features that ETS2 did and some of its very own.
-Ability to manage multiple garages, trucks and hire drivers/run your own company.
-Radiostations with relevant radio stations such as country, classic rock, metal, alternative and other genres.
-Weight stations, sometimes it will require you to pull in to get a truck inspection.
-Pretty good recreations of landmarks such as the golden gate bridge.
-The ability to do some pretty heavy customization/personalization of your truck, mods further enhancing this.
-Many more
If you were a fan of Euro Truck Simulator 2, you'll definitely like American Truck Simulator, the game is well worth $20.00 in my opinion and i really find it enjoyable, being able to drive around on such a wide open expanse, with your choice of music is therapeutic in nature and is really good for stress relief and escapism.
The attention to detail is great and you can get some true enjoyment from it. I'd definitely reccomend this game to any simulation fan, it's a really enjoyable experience and has alot of future potential as well.

This review will be in separate parts when ever I want to complain about the game. But every bit of this review is constructive criticism.
First three areas explored in:
I am already offended by this game for its lack of social construction. This game's dialogue seems to have bits and pieces of an idea together but are poorly sewn together. If you are a private investigator or an FBI profiler you will be saddened by this game. For the dialogue choices seem to route you to the same answer, but are shallow in complete thought. I get the idea behind this game being the main story line but my problem with this game so far is not your maneuverability, or lack of direction. But more or so to the approach this game takes when it comes to solving the cases. It seems like the person who created this plot forgot that detectives constantly talk to themselves while piecing together a story. Though to be fair it says in the text right there what it wants you to do. But it should be stated by the detective to help people figure out what is going on. The text floating around as you try to piece things together will throw you off guard as soon as a change of course happens within the solving of each small puzzle.
While trying to figure out one thing it suddenly switches... but our friend the detective doesn't say much and it quickly moves on to the next thing. So you miss what the text changed to, telling you what you are supposed to look for now, at that very split second given moment and you guess wrong. Worst of all is the clunky UI. You mess something up it freezes you... pauses.... backs out.... brings up several different separate tab screens for each object which suddenly takes away the purpose for searching it, (which is why I say again it would help if the detective was constantly talking to himself in thought to keep the main point in focus.) And quite frankly leaves me bewildered at what happens when you "try again."
Maybe the approach to this method should have used better sorting options.... Throwing things around all the time makes me think this detective never carried around so much as a book. Possibly carried around a recording device seeing how disorderly everything being displayed becomes.
Just imagine that every time you came up with the idea behind a string of events you got angered, and suddenly threw up all the information you just looked at in frustration... only to come right back to it, to string everything together again, as all the papers fall to the ground and you have this game. I think the creator... if he is or was a detective... must have had little to no patience himself in each case. Possibly due to extra ordinary means like time or money allotted to his investigations. Maybe a sergeant or person's interest was a timely manner. I am still willing to give this a second try but it is so demanding on your eyes, more or so than your brain, that it causes you to lose concentration quite easily.
And the demons? My goodness. Talk about an annoying trap puzzle that springs up like a jack in the box that malfunctions a lot. I get the idea behind exorcising ghosts... but uh.... how does our detective friend just suddenly know how to exorcise a ghost exactly? Was our friend the detective a priest? There is no mention of him being one in his own background... But just barely minutes into the game, you have the ability to exorcise a ghost without having to read any books about it. I think this game would have been a lot more interesting with the setup it seemed to hold. In which I think the Detective originally did not know how to exorcise ghosts until later in the game. But I guess the devs thought it would be too annoying to make players fear them so early. Yet it would have been a lot more fun and made more sense if the ability wasn't there until you figured it out.
This game seems to be targeted at kids more or so than adults seeing how there are some "way too soft" spots that spring up like a bad smell. You will literally yell at our detective to "JUST GRAB HER F***ING ARM!" When it comes to solving one of the cases. I want to slap the detective for being so.... retentively sympathetic, yet wise cracking at certain times.
Also the girl? Best idea ever when it comes to surprising your audience when you finally meet her for the first time. But there was one inconsistency that happened at the cemetery... She complained about not being able to see him... even though she was holding a flashlight... Then a few minutes later she has no trouble seeing them. Could have been the lamp post nearby but uh.... She did shine a flashlight on him.
Last three bits:
Am I ever more disappointed in a game? This game answered that question. Incredibly short game. I am sad. I am so sad after completing this game.
The best puzzle is the ending.
I think the issue is that the development team behind this had an astonishingly awesome idea.... but I think budget cuts really let this game down. This game had some real potential but it is so short lived. The ending seems to be pasted together. But at least it did create one hell of a mind ♥♥♥♥. It is just too bad the whole time you believe one thing because of your own abilities... and then there is another. What the hell.
Too short. Way too short. My final complaint? Some of the "side missions" are broken.

American Truck Simulator is SCS Software’s latest bafflingly enjoyable trucking simulator. ATS is effectively ETS2 with a few improvements and new locations, in the form of California and Nevada for you to explore with Arizona coming as a free update at some point. The map scale in ATS seems to be smaller than ETS2 and while that does mean you get around faster it also means that you can’t have long journeys like you could in ETS2 which is also contributed to by only having two states. ATS has only launched with two trucks but there are a couple of others ready to be released once licensing has been sorted out by SCS with more trucks in the works, all of which will be free updates.
ATS is certainly a good looking game and it boasts visual and performance increases over ETS2. Both trucks are well-designed and look great, especially with the shiny paint jobs and the scenery all looks good too. The towns and cities also look good but due to the map scale they feel pretty small, with the exception of Los Angeles which is relatively big for the game. The UI and menus are all the same as they were in ETS2 and are still just as easy to use as they were. The new trucks have come with some in-cabin differences, namely an electronic display and a built-in GPS. Both of these have several display modes to choose from which are all pretty helpful.
Being a trucking simulator, ATS’ gameplay consists of hauling cargo from one company to another between cities. One of the new features in ATS is ‘special’ destinations for cargo which will depend on what kind of cargo you’re hauling, for example if you’re hauling construction equipment you might have to drop it off at some roadworks just outside one of the game’s cities. On the topic of new features, weigh stations are also new and you’ll sometimes receive a message to pull off and have your truck weighed when you’re passing one.
Back to the actual cargo, while there’s not as much variety as there was in ETS2 with DLC there are still enough cargo types to keep things interesting. As was the case in ETS2, unlocking certain skills will also give you access to new kinds of cargo such as flammable liquid or high value construction vehicles. The maximum trailer lengths have also been increased up to fifty-three feet whereas ETS2 had a maximum length of forty feet. These longer trailers can provide quite the challenge, especially when you’re dealing with tight turns.
ATS also lets you build up a fleet of trucks and drivers to bring in extra income for you. While early on you’ll probably need bank loans to buy new trucks, once you’ve got yourself established expanding your fleet will become far easier. Despite the fact your hired drivers can only earn up to ~$20,000 per job, having a form of income other than the jobs you’re completing yourself is incredibly handy, especially if you have loans to pay off. Garages to house your fleet are available across both states currently in the game and start with three truck slots with an upgrade increasing that to five. While you do start with your own garage it only has one slot available which is occupied by your truck so you’ll need to upgrade it to three slots before you can hire new drivers. The trucks purchased for your drivers can be upgraded/customised, just as your own can, and you can also switch around your trucks whenever you want.
Upgrading and customising your truck is one of the main areas where ATS is inferior to its predecessor. Right off the bat, only having two trucks (that’s not two manufacturers, that’s two single trucks) massively limits the customisation though each truck does have a couple of different presets though they aren’t unlocked until you’re a higher level and levelling up takes quite a long time. Customising the actual trucks is also pretty underwhelming, most parts of the truck only have two or three different options, such as bullbars, and some of the options that were available in ETS2 simply don’t exist anymore, such as a beacon. Hopefully this will improve once SCS has sorted out more licensing but for the time being it’s definitely one of game’s negative aspects.
The other main problem with the game is the map scale I mentioned earlier. A twenty in-game hour journey now takes somewhere in the region of thirty of forty minutes, depending on whether or not you’re in-line or below the speed limit. While this kind of scale would be acceptable if we had access to the whole US, when you consider that a twenty hour journey is pretty much the longest possible journey in the game’s current state it’s pretty disappointing. Of course, if you do prefer getting your jobs done quickly then you may actually like this but I feel like most ETS2 fans will be somewhat disappointed.
One last thing I’d like to touch on is just how relaxing the game, for the most part, is. Just cruising through California and Nevada with your favourite music or podcast on is incredibly enjoyable and relaxing, perfect for after a long day’s work or after you’ve been playing something a little more stressful. If you don’t have any music or podcasts to listen to, you can try out the game’s default internet radio stations (or even add your own, instructions available in-game) which feature a wide variety of music genres. The game does have some music that plays if you don’t have your own stuff but that only plays in the menus and loading screens. I did say the game is relaxing for the most part, the other part there is when you’re involved in some kind of traffic accident or you get hit with a speeding ticket when you’ve only just entered the new speed limit zone, while incredibly frustrating they don’t happen all too often so you should be nice and relaxed for most of your time in ATS.
ATS' current amount of content may be disappointing but the game does improve on ETS2 and will be enjoyed by its fans. If California and Nevada isn’t enough for you I’d suggest holding off on buying ATS until the Arizona expansion is out but otherwise go for it, the game’s pricing is reasonable after all.

It is almost a lesson in feudalism, in which a small number of land owners, most of whom used hacks and exploits get their land, control everything, and you have spend a LOT of real money to buy in to the aristocracy.
Think of it as Eve: Online in which all starsystems, indlucing nullsec, were given to the first people to claim them after launch, and where there is no way to evict tenants, even those who got their land via exploits or RMT, and the only way to gain a system and it's assiated wealth was to buy it with cold hard cash.

This is a very good game that lets you fight like a knight or barbarian. It focuses on melee combat and has a lot of gore and splatter effects which might be a bit disturbing at the beginning if you are not used to it. The game offers very good teamplay, easy to learn mechanics but it has such a huge depth that it is hard to master and the learning process will never end even if you put 500 hours in this nice game.
The immersion in this game is just awesome (if you play first person only like me) and you will feel like it is actually you who is fighting. Tactics from real melee fighting can be put to use effectively, e. g. if you fight 2 vs 1 you need to bring your opponent in the middle of you and your teammate and the teammate facing the opponent needs to focus on blocking while the other teammate should attack from the rear (you would be surprised how many people dont know this...). That is just one simple example but if you know some real life melee tactics you will be amazed how many you can actually put to use in this game.
However, it is a pity that most high ranked players prefer to exploit the game mechanics, for example by doing ballerina spinning moves in a fully armored knight or hitting during the wind-up phase with full power while facing you with their backs, but thats only because they dont know better and it is easy to counter once you got used to  it. Beginners will have a very hard time right now because on the low rank servers players usually do a lot of teamdamage or fight their own teammates at spawn and at higher ranked servers there will be a shock for them as they gonna get slaughtered by the veterans.
But dont let that discourage you, keep fighting and you will become a warrior! You will get better constantly and improve your timing and combat skill!

Only a couple of hours in but I can say this game has plenty to offer. I don't do multiplayer online with strangers so most of my time is singleplayer base building and getting my bearings.
Largest problem for me is the animations making combat feel very clunky and slow, causing everything to kick your♥♥♥♥♥from the very beginning. However you can learn the quirks pretty quickly, like that you regen stamina at base walk speed and the ai can't seem to attack and run at the same time.
The biggest strong point for me is the super simple crafting and low cost recipies for buildings. In ark I loved building the most but had to turn to mods for any good furniture or cosmetics. Here, it's not only in game but provides a function other than "Well, now I can sit..cool." If you wanna make your own personal village with slaves tending to your crafting stations, you're not only free to do so but very much able to with incredible speed relative to other survival sims.
Last point I care to make is the content currently available in early access as this is day three I believe. Yes it all seems very surface level and at first the game doesn't appear to have much depth but then I entered ghost/god mode and flew around exploring. There's entire city of the dead and city with hostiles to raid and fight to your hearts content with treasures to find inside. Really it's kind of up to you how you'd like to play as opposed to ark where the only thing to do was raid caves and tame dinos, after long enough there was nothing to use all your accumulated resources on that really felt like it mattered.
So, bear in mind it's early access and it'll be buggy and have stuff that's all wonky and weird. Don't buy and complain later that it's not finished. Enjoy it for what it is. You savagely beating naked people into submission so that they make weapons for you to fight an army of the undead.

Firstly, please don't let my hours fool you, I have many hours spread over various accounts.
Elsword is a side-scrolling MMORPG. It has a 2.5D perspective that works suprisingly well with the game's design.
It features beautiful backgrounds and some platforming elements. Even if you don't like platforming games, give
Elsword a go, I hate platformers, but I love Elsword.
COMBAT
In Elsword, the combat is simple, but complex. You use Z and X along with the arrow keys to pull-off combos and you have 4 skills to use. A S D C. You can also buy a BSlot to get 4 more Q W E R. You use your combos and skills to kill monsters and bosses through fields (Open areas where you kill monsters along with other random players) and dungeons (instances where you team up with 3 other players to clear a dungeon area along with a boss at the end.)
Now, If you are looking for an ultra-balanced MMORPG with competitive PvE and PvP, please leave. Elsword at its heart
is more of a casual game. To contradict myself, it does also contain many competitive aspects, just don't expect them to
be balanced.
But, please don't mistake this as me saying this game is bad and only for casuals. Elsword is very, very addicting and enjoyable as long as you don't take it too seriously. In order to enjoy this game, you will need to spend *SOME* money, but, contrary to what many people say, you don't honestly have to spend that much money. There are a few things that are more-or-less neccessary such as inventory expansions, but they are very cheap if you have any sort of income whatsoever. Other things such as Ice-Burners (Premium Costumes) (Costumes are cosmetic items that can be socketed in order to increase your stats) are not needed, thus you don't need to spend money on them, but they help.
This is where my previous statement comes in. Elsword is a breath of fresh air if you don't treat it like WoW or LoL etc.. Its enviroments are light and airy, the music is nice and relaxing, and it's very fun to kick back and enjoy a few friendly arenas on a Friday night. What I would say to you is, try out the game, see if you enjoy the core combat and skill system and, if you do, play it. Don't worry about class balance, don't get angry, just relax and you'll love this game.
Here's a list of things you'll NEED to enjoy the game if you really want to commit to Elsword. (Cost after the :.)
Inventory Expansions:  Roughly $20 per character.
Skill B Slot: $9 per character (But you can buy VIP, $10/month to get B slot on every character for duration of VIP).
Bank Slots: $~9
Overall, if you really want to commit to Elsword, buying VIP is a good way to kickstart your leveling and get some temporary BSlots (Btw, BSlots allow you to equip more skills.)
If you have any more questions about the game, either message me on Steam, or add me on Elsword. My IGN is Vjyorsk. I'd be happy to help with anything you need. (As long as I'm not busy :)).

The game is grindy, but also not grindy. There's a lot of levelling of items and characters and levelling skills up, but you can also go from level 1 to level 100 in 10 minutes. Your level 1 character can have level 100 stats. You can transfer stats from one item to the other and then sell off that item since that particular stat movement is all that interested you. The end-game content has higher level bosses and monsters and the grind won't be in grinding itself but management and seeing what you need next.
If you don't care for all of this and just want to play through the story it's the easiest game to begin right away and get into, since there's no 3 hour long cut scenes and 5 hour long exposition followed by 2 hour tutorials. An NPC in the HUB world itself outright tells you you don't need to know a lot of the more mechanical aspects of the game to get through it.
It's a long story with plenty of cutscenes dispersed in-between, but there's no terrain exploration or walking to get to the next battle, rather you jump into it right away. For an RPG it's got a ton of gameplay and leaves all the talking and exposition at segments of the game where its minimal and also sensible.
Apparently, this game is actually really bare bones and the later titles had an assload more content to them, which I find amazing. There's a ton to get through here and provided you take the time to learn it all, which isn't too hard or time consuming, you'll have hundreds of hours (seriously) to play through and stat manage. It's an RPG with level 999 but no grinding. If you don't wanna grind anyway then don't worry since story mode doesn't require it. Post game content does.In fact, you'll be tempted TO grind earlier on since the more you learn the more you want (especially when its easy). Hold off on it unless you want to stomp through story mode.
Anyway, for its price its definitely worth playing. If you're a fan of strategy RPG's it's worth picking up. I could write so much about how paradoxical this game is in that its grindy but also the easiest 5 minute grind of your life. Or how I started grinding a quarter into the game until I realized I don't have to at this point, and how the game is TEMPTING me to grind when I have minus 1000% reason to, which is odd because I'm not a fan of grinding but it's just so god damn easy to in this game if you know how to break it. The Disgaea series is meant to be broken in terms of grinding. And it's rewarding. And it's somehow stopping me from progressing the story even though I don't have to do it wtf. Game is really weird.

A truly unique game and experience, Hand of Fate is part rogue-like RPG with choose-your-own-adventure elements, part Assassin's Creed, Arkham style brawler, and part tabletop deck building game. The game lets you choose your own paths and craft your own story, and no two games are ever alike. A witty and snarky card dealer who sits across the table narrates much of your journey and adds his own personal commentary to the decisions you make and the fates that befall you.
The music is great, it's incredibly atmospheric and sets the stage and mood quite nicely. The voice acting is fantastic, the number of cards is large and varied, and the aesthetic is all around perfect.
The combat system is the only problem the game suffers, and even then it still works well. At times the animations can be a bit stiff and janky and there isn't much depth to it, but at the end of the day it's a nitpick to an overall fantastic game and experience.
If you enjoy rogue-likes, choose-your-own-adventures, deck builders, and story telling, pick this up.

Murdered: Soul Suspect is a different kind of game, but that doesn't mean its a bad game.  I never got around to playing it when it came out, money reasons mostly, but I was able to play it through a friend's library.  The game is based in Salem and follows the story of a cop who dies at the very start of the game (not a spoiler).  The "combat" in the game is mostly stealth based, there are demons, who you have to sneak up on to kill, and if they spot you, you must flee until they resume their normal patrols, but asides from that there is no real combat to speak of.  That is not a bad thing though, as the story is really nice and has a few pretty good twists in it.  The sounds in the game are really nice, and the screech that is made when demons pops up could catch you off guard, I know it did to me a few times.  There are papers, and different things to collect throughout the game, including area specific items that unlock hidden ghost stories to flesh out the town even more.  I played with my xbox one controller so I don't know how good or well the key binding is, but the controls were really nice.  I was actually quite surprised by this game, as I wasn't expecting the good story that I got.  This is not a game for everyone as there is not a whole lot to speak of for combat.  I really enjoyed the story, the somewhat unique combat system and the atmosphere.  Not much in the way of replay value, as I am not sure if there is a difficulty option, unless you wanted to 100% it there is not a whole lot of reasons to replay it.  8/10

Played almost an hour and have requested for a refund.  This game is no where near in the caliber of The Hunter Classic.  I have been playing The Hunter since the first year and have logged in over 1200 hours both on steam and their old web launcher.  This game is way to arcade driven for me.  The graphics are a mixed bag.  The animal models remind me of Cabelas animal models.  The developers have not made very good use of the Unreal 4 engine.  Tracking system needs a major overhaul.  Gun sounds need to be made from real sound samples.  I do like it has controller support and 3rd person which I wish was in The Hunter Classic.  I also like the way the unlock system works with the missions.  But for me I can see me finishing it in 3 weeks maybe and I don't see anything that would want me to continue to play.  I am not saying this game is totally bad just that it is not for me.   I really wanted to like this game enough to play it through but just to many negative points to make me spend my time to play it through.  Maybe in the future the devs will address the issues and make it have  more graphical appeal and fix the problem area's.  If you don't mind the fact that it is a bit arcade over realism and not graphically on par with The Hunter series then you might like it.

It's a version of Euro Truck Simulator 2 adapted to the USA.
Firstly, it seems that many players complain about the geographical inadequacies of American Truck Simulator, but the simplifications are in fact rather similar to what they did in ETS2. Presumably, the American players know more about driving in the US or the geography of California than that of Europe, so they suddenly notice the simplifications only now.
Secondly, for those that suggest that the map is rather small, remember that ATS includes 20 cities in California alone. On the other hand, ETS2 still has just 8 French cities and 4 Italian cities (3 at release in 2012), more than 3 years after release. (France is 1.5 times the size of California.) The countries in ETS2 with more cities, UK and Germany, only have more because the base maps for them were just imported from the old games UKTS and GTS.
Lastly, remember that the USD price of ETS2 at release, USD 40, was double that of ATS, so I think USD 20 is a fair price for ATS. If it still sounds too expensive, one can always wait until the price inevitably drops, like it has for ETS2.

To start this off, this game is mix between Mario Kart and a metaphorical hampster wheel. You simply run, jump, dive, swing, bounce off walls, and blow the stuffing out of everyone to get ahead of your opponents. If your opponent falls far enough behind and into the Red Zone, you will thus be out of the run. To win, you must be the last man standing in 3 runs.
That being said, the game is very, very fun. It's quick game that will require plenty of reflexes and reaction time. Very easy to pick up for beginners. But as you progress in the game, it will require more effort in each run.
Without further ado, here's the Pros and Cons of the game:
+ Simplistic art style
+ Local AND online play
+ A plethora of game-changing match preferences and items
+ Active Development team (A new update every day/other day)
+ Community involvement from the Dev team (That's how the best games are made)
+ Isn't very taxing on computer requirements (I run just fine on my Gateway laptop)
+ Quite easy to pick up
+ Controller support
+ Perfect party game
+ Workshop editor with a great building community
+ Good family-friendly gameplay (i.e No blood, swearing, etc.)
+ REBINDABLE CONTROLS
+ Simple acheivements
- Rather buggy as of the current update
- Higher ranked matches are more based on "Who knows the most glitches to exploit"
- Irritating online lag (randomly spiking to 999 ping before getting disconnecting)
- A sometimes functioning AI
- Random crashing on launch and in game
- Glitchy surfaces (You may get stuck in a wall for 2 seconds, which is life-or-death in this game)
- Not too many players online (Not really something the Devs can fix)
Overall, I would recommend this game to all my friends. Additionally, the game goes on sale quite frequently, so be sure to look for sales before purchasing the game straightaways. For the best experience, play with people you know, as it is far more fun playing that way. I'm personally looking forward to future updates, as the game gets better with each patch/update.
tl;dr Buy this game. Jolly fun.

Well I would like to say that is game is amazing, but it's not. I'm going to start with the good, and then list the bad and the ugly parts of this game.
The good parts of this game that they nailed on the spot.
1.character customization
2. leveling while in combat and crafting
3. the combat and skill customization to make your character unique to others
4. Mounts system.
5. the quest system is good.
6. Great tutorial
Unfortunately I only got to lvl 15, tried to get back on the next day, and the game could not load on computer. There are still a lot of things on this game that I have yet to explore or to experience and I would have enjoyed trying them out, but that leads us to the bad and ugly side of this game.
The bad parts of this game that throws this game in the garbage can.
1. Im going to start with the labor system. To give a general idea of how the labor system works is anytheing that you gather or create such as mining, gathering herbs, or maintaining livestock takes labor points. When you start off in the game you get zero labor points, and as a free to play subscription you only get 5 points every 5 minutes you play and none when not playing, which makes sense cause Trion wants to make money on subscription fees, which does give you more labor points to work with.
2. Crafting system. Sor far with the sandbox games Ive been seeing a lot of issues, and one of them is getting enough random matts (material that you get at random from opening bags droped from mobs.) So far I've came close to creating a sword but the the random matts stopped me in my tracks, which is depressing cause in mmo games crafting is essential and without crafting makes the game lose depth and interest. But it still has potential as long as you want to put your spare time in this game(mostly all your spare time) to just make a sword aor anyother item that you want to make.
3.Main quests the good part about the main quests it gives you a decent story throughout the game, but when I do the maain quests the tend to get stuck on the beginning of cinima part and the game crashes. It's a great idea, but it reality they messed it up cause the game to freeze in black screen.
Now the ugly parts of this game.
1. This game is not computer friendly because you may be able to play this game at least 4 times before something goes wrong, and it doesn't load. Pretty much your waiting for this game to load or waiting for this game to crash. Most likely your waiting for this game to crash. When it does there is a internet page that pops up saying what YOU need to do to make this game work on your computer. The page is somewhat helpful but it didn't fix my problem with this game. ANYTIME and I mean ANYTIME a game that can't play on your computer and the the company tells you how to fix it, and they don't fix it themselves is a terrible game design in progamming, and the company who is in charge is not getting my money to play this game.
2. This game is definatly a pay to win game for sure, cause you cannot craft hardly anything at all with a free subcription.

FIrst let me point out it is a Early Access.   SO please do expect bugs and fixes coming around.  Day one had issues with servers but dev team did a good job by releasing a fix ASAP.   For those complaining I am sorry but what did you expect.
I tried many early access game and am a survival crafting fanatic just watch my gamelist to see for yourself.  I bought and tried many of them.   This one takes the Cake! Don't expect a tutorial like most of the early access games.  Try it out search the web a bit for guides or info its already out there.
The crafting system is good easy no problem building or placing structures. Thats already a good thing.   You do gather a good amount of ressources to craft.  Good news ressources are everywhere and respawn at normal server setting is pretty good.   Yes you will grind but you will find satisfaction since gattering ressources also gives you xp to level up.  Crafting your house cause thats one of the first thing you will do to survive this land will give you also xp has for killing creatures.
The land is beautifull there is plenty of creatures to go around.  Prepare to fight!  Exploration is worth it.  Found some caves with interesting creatures inside that ended up with a run for my life.  Can't wait to get my gear up and explore it more.
I will tell you this don't get cocky.  SOme basic creatures became easy kils so believed  that I was the man ended up Dead eaten alive and now spawn in my house and am more cautious now hehe.
There is alot this game has to offer and with the devs talking to implement Magic and more on the long run I am very pleased.
Just look at some games like 7 days to die and how it evolved since day one.  I have faith in Funcom simply because this game day one is actuly very good hey its day one.  Take the time to take this in and imagine it in a few months what it can become.
I played solo/coop for a while just getting to know the game what items to choose to craft from the beginning makes a difference be aware.
Now on multiplayer server.  Yes you will get killed if you choose pvp yes your house will be destroyed and looted.  Make yourself friends build a community join a clan.   You made the decision to play on multiplayer server that is the point.
If this is a issue for you. SOlo play it or coop with some friends should be more then ennough.   You will still enjoy the survival aspect and leveling.
At the moment I have seen my share of freezes and crashes.  Mostly after death were my character wont move or simply seen a cutscene and ended up frozen.  These issues are on the forums and actuly got some advice and fixes that corrected most of the issues.  Know that you will live it and remember its just got out!  Stay calm close the game restart and it will be fine in most of the case.  If not post in the community explain your problem there are good peaple that are willing to help.

I purchased, but didn't log a ton of hours in the remastered first iteration of this game (36 hrs), but this 2nd one just feels right, and it's a homerun for Larian. I will start by saying I have only experienced the co-op of this game, which so far has been a load of fun to play with a good friend:
Areas to highlight:  The story telling is vastly improved, with exceptional voice dialogue (gaming industry wise). There are a ridiuclous amount of options for dialogue depending on your characters skills and tags. Rich orchestra sounds bring you back to some of your favorite RPGs of old. The game is gorgeous too, graphics are superb. Scenes are incredibly detailed, from brightly lit beach environments to dark, dreary dungeons. The mood is dark and sombre overall but clever writing adds in humor all along the way. HUD is intuitive and nothing new, co-op shared backpack screen is something to behold; very convenient. The combat is intuitive but high on difficulty, Larian does not hold your hand in this one. There are major things in the game that are not obvious which I won't spoil, and without the internet you'd miss a lot. Highly recommend playing without reading up on the game, it makes for a much better/realer experience. Those new to this type of game will repeat battles many times over on the harder difficulties. This is Turn-Based though, at it's best. Re-trying is half the fun, learning from your previous mistakes becomes essential. Winning a battle on the first go after using perfect tactics really feels satisfying.
Areas for Improvement:  We encountered minor bugs, a learned spell that wouldn't show up in the mage book, finishing a successful dialogue with a creature then clicking them again by accident only to have new dialogue that leads to a fight. Stuff that requires a reload but isn't game breaking, and occurs infrequently. The environment manipulation is incredible, and no other game has allowed players to control fights so well using it, however it becomes a bit too much at times with the blood, water and other puddles--often making magic-type characters useless since every attack hurts your friends and foes alike. Source spells are a great idea but would be nice to be able to use once per battle or game day. Current game makes it hard to accumulate source points for skills that truthfully really arent as impressively OP as they should be at that rarity. Lastly, the gold/bartering system needs a hotfix bad. You need to move a slider to hit exact gold value on both sides, without an option to go up by 1 or type in a value. This is a basic that has been overlooked.
Summary:  I look forward to logging many more hours before updating this review (so far at around 30 hrs). Recommended for anyone who loves old-school (or new) cRPGs or any 1-4 group of friends looking for a great game to co-op, just note it requires much focus, dialogue/reading and chatting, so I wouldn't recommend playing with a stranger. Also be prepared for 4 hr+ play times. It is almost impossible to make any progress in 1-2 hr playings. Congrats to Larian on a job well done, it's been one of the better RPG games I have played in years.  I would score D:OS2 9/10.

Part choose your own adventure, part ARPG, part deckbuilder - all well executed. Players build a deck of resources (gear/magic/abilities) and a deck of encounters which take the form of the dungeon/adventure you are about to take on. Cards are laid out to represent encounters during this journey. Each turn the player decides to where to move while managing health, food, and assets based on how encounters turn out. Encounters are split into two types: combat and choice. In the first you are given a number and type of enemy to defeat as well as any optional challenges dictated by encounter card and based on what cards you have enoucntered and equipped you take on your foes with whatever gear you have on in combat reminiscent of the Arkham series. In the second you are given a card-draw game, 4 cards representing the degree to which you succeed or fail. Upon proper completion of certain encounters loot is distributed and occasionally a coin which unlocks new cards (items/encounters). Progress feels fairly rewarding as you make it through the middle of the boss challenges and if that's running a little stale there's always the endless mode where you pit your cards against the game and see how long you can hold up. There's a lot to like here for $20.
All in all i'm super-happy with picking this up and can't wait to see it grow with new content. As it is with just this initial content the replayability factor here is hard not to notice and is a breath of fresh air.

SPOILERS BELOW! SPOILERS BELOW! SPOILERS BELOW! SPOILERS BELOW! SPOILERS BELOW!
In my first game I had to go around and keep an eye on another character at the request of the characters Father. I was apparently also a big drug dealer and I had a stash of drugs hidden away somewhere that I could give to someone if they had a special poker chip.
After chatting with a few other players my character ended up falling in love with the character she was meant to keep an eye on. Since he was so nice, I offered him the liqour cabinet key that I had in my inventory. Little did I know that was where the drugs were stashed. Then a big investigation insued with people pretending they were actually secret agents from the FBI and questioning people about the drugs, which was pretty amusing.
In the end the character I was meant to keep an eye on gave me a ring from his inventory and asked me to marry him... and then time ran out and the game was over. Great first experience... lol.
In my second game I played the same character and had to check everyone's passports, with the side quest being that I was a secret agent for a company and that another character in the game was a rival agent. So I went about collecting passports until one player was a bit reluctant to give me theirs unless I let them scan me. Knowing I'd be discovered as an agent, I delayed the scan and said I'd be back later.
I then got into a conversation with another player who had found two data disks. One with data from my characters company and one from the rival company. I then proceeded to give the $100,000 of cold cash in my inventory to the player in exchange for both disks. We agreed and exchanged items, completing a couple of objectives. Upon returning to the suspected rival agent, I offered him the rival company's data disk in return for his passport. He agreed, confirming my suspicions that he was indeed a rival agent.
After that I only had one passport left to get, from another player who was also reluctant to hand over their passport. I got a drink from the rival agent (who also happened to be the bartender) and went to offer the drink in return for their passport, but time ran out before I could secure it.
Overall, it was a fun experience. I'll definitely come back to this game, I just wonder how long it'll be before I get bored of the same free scenarios. This game could really (and I mean REALLY) benefit from more free scenarios (and maybe more paid ones to balance it out too). This game is very fun once you actually get into it and I'd love to see some more scenarios. Would be a real shame to only have a couple of free scenarios, and slowly see this game die because people are getting bored and don't want to pay for more... and I would love to be able to run/walk quicker. It seems to make gameplay slow... which is bad when you have a time limit in which to complete your objectives.
It's a bit of a picky rating... but I give this game a 7.5/10. If the slow walking issue is addressed and more free scenarios are added, you're looking at a solid 9 from me. :)

It's taken me about 8 years to get around to it, but I've finally mustered up the desire to beat Fable: The Lost Chapters - and it's taken me around 10 years to beat EITHER version of Fable. It was my first (quasi-)RPG on my first game console; so yes, I do have quite a few fond memories of this game in my youth. Does that mean that this game gets a rose-tinted reccomendation, free from the burden of actual critique? Far from it.
In terms of tone and presentation, Fable: The Lost Chapters is unique. It's one of the few fantasy settings in a video game I can think of that doesn't take much influence from Tolken: while some of the more tropey fantasy creatures such as Trolls and Nymphs are present, there are quite a few original creations, too. The artstyle and general world design echoes more traditional fantasy, giving the impression that one is, yes, in a fable. Top that off with tounge-in-cheek writing, a fantastic soundtrack by Russel Shaw, and vocal talent that is evidently from creator company Lionhead Studio's home town of Guildford, England, and Fable feels extremely fresh more than 10 years later.
However, the mirror-sheen production values can't hide a game that is, for lack of a better word, pretentious. Every mechanic, encounter, and story element is played up to be grandiose and epic in scale, but after the first few hours, the game clearly is clearly struggling to swim to the deep end of the pool.
The game's most notable feature, the morality system, is represented by "good boy" and "bad boy" scale (note: may not actually be what they are called in-game), and the extent of how much the game changes boils down to horns or a halo on your characters head, and wether or not townsfolk run away screaming or endlessly clap their hands above their hands yelling "AAAAAAAAYYYYYYYYYYYYY" (no, seriously). Most good boy points are aquired by saving people from attackers; most bad boy points are acquired by killing every non-combatant in sight. Even during major, story-influencing events, the choices are presented to you in a yes-or-no question asked by the game; the only remnants of what you did afterwards are an entry in your character's journal and villagers straight up telling you exactly what you did a few quests ago. The system is so arbitrary and easily-manipulated that you can go from villian to hero in a couple binary choices' time. Worried about a hard choice? Don't worry, the game will compansate you equally either way, so even if you choose not to do something that would be rewarding, you'll still get an alternative item or money for participating.
The combat and leveling don't leave much room for role-playing. You can level up your hero's abilities ad infinitum; sure, you'll specialize at first, but what will you do when you've leveled up your specialities' abilties nearly all the way and have spare expirience to spend on less-leveled abilites? As a result, the game's combat becomes all too easy and boring very quickly, and never compensates for your higher level. The game at least tracks how you play, so it gives you a nice illusion of having your own playstyle by giving you a title based on magic, bow, and sword use. By the game's end, your character will end up the same mary-sue every playthrough save for how many good or bad boy points you've earned and what clothing from the game's extremely limited wardrobe you've chosen to adorn your character with.
And the rest of the game is just fluff. You can get married! Except there is very little reason to unless you want to get underpowered weapons gifted to you from time to time. Prices vary between shops, so you can be a buisnessman and buy low and sell high! Except that the price range doesn't change all that much, and by the time you're buying and selling really expensive items you'll be rolling in too much dough for it to matter. You can buy houses and shops and rent them out! Except you make tons more money for completing quests anyway, and you don't have to go out of you way to pick up your reward that way.
Maybie my nostalgia goggles are broken, but even after understanding that Fable: The Lost Chapters didn't live up to the hype all those years ago, it still managed to dissapoint me. The whole game felt like it was one big lie that someone was trying desperately to show that it was true. Given the precendence of Lionhead Studios and it's rather hyperbole-prone founder, I guess I shouldn't be too suprised. Well played, Peter.

Don't believe the negative hype. This is a pretty good game. The complaints about the high-price might be warranted, but the complaints about the gameplay are mostly just the rantings of fanboys of other hunting games. The graphics are good, the animations are life-like, and the animal's AI is adequate. I have read complaints about the AI being dumb on the easier difficulty settings, and the high density of animals being unrealistic. I have only been playing on hard difficulty, and I have found it challenging to locate the correct species and land a perfectly-aimed shot. The user interface is straight forward and easy to navigate, and there is a number of graphic settings which can be modified to make the game run optimally for your system. Content wise, there seems to be a large amount of maps dipicting different geographic regions, many kinds of wildlife, and many different guns and equptment to unlock. There is no create-a-hunter or player customisation, but instead you are able to selct a pre-created hunter from a small list. That may be one of my only gripes with the game, but it's obviously inconsequential and not a deal-breaker. The game also supports xbox controllers, which some of it's competitors may or may not.

I will rate this game based on the following things:
Art/Graphics
Music/Sound
Content
Mechanics
Level Design
Art/Graphics - 10/10
The art looks very good and you can easily tell what something is supposed to be. The colors are very upbeat and fit the music well. The animations are very fluid and look very nice.
Music/Sound - 8/10
The music is all very good, however I constantly hear the same tracks over and over again and it can become quite boring. But the tracks that are present are not necessarily bad. Like I said before, it fits the art style very well.
Content - 10/10
There is about 11 or 10 official levels that you will constantly be finding new shortcuts in every time you play. There is also Steam Workshop with thousands of levels, including ones that are extremely bad but there are still plently of great levels. This game is super addicting and I've played for almost 48 hours and I haven't gotten bored yet.
Mechanics - 9/10
The main mechanic, running, is what you would expect. The other main mechanic, the grappling hook, is very fun to use and a player's skill with it can matter more than their running skill. Some of the power ups are better than others and can give players a great advantage. Some powerups can be avoided, but others cannot be which can and will be very frustrating.
Level Design - 10/10
(This is about the official levels, not the Steam Workshop levels.) The levels are all very different and offer lots of advantages to skilled players. The themes in the levels, like a library and a ship, make each level competely unique from the others.
Total - 94/100

I was put off this game initially due to negative reports about its length, and so the base price of £20 was enough to give me pause. However, when it appeared on sale for £5 I decided to give it a chance and I am very glad I did.
The star of this game is its story, where you play as the ghost of Ronan O'Connor, a detective in modern day Salem. For a large part it feels like a point and click adventure game where the emphasis is on finding the pieces and putting them together rather than on any sort of direct action. Gameplay revolves around investigations that are heavily reminiscent of L.A. Noire (another game I really enjoyed) except you can walk through walls and interrogating people is mostly replaced with possessing them to influence their mind. Perhaps owing to the length of the story (it only took me around 8hrs to complete the main quest, all side quests and most collectibles) both the story and gameplay never outstayed their welcome and remained entertaining to the very end.
The main negative in this game is the repetitive forced stealth segments where you are forced to sneak up on demonic spirits before a simple quick time event is entered in place of combat. I felt even after the first of these that it was an unnecessary mechanic designed as a buffer between me and the enjoyable parts of the game. I would commonly find myself sweeping an area of these "enemies" before returning to start the section proper. Thankfully, they don't take too long and aren't difficult, but this just emphasises how needless they are.
I would definitely recommend this as a sale pickup if you are even remotely curious.

Amazing game to be carried away by. Feature rich, good menu system (not the toned-down, controller optimized stuff you normally get these days), an amazing turn-based battle system, very good music and sound in general, very compelling graphics and art style. Characters are, as it's normal for the Divinity series, quite quirky sometimes, but the humor works well and already made me chuckle a few times.

I'm not a big fan of anime or the clichés tied to it, but Recettear does, on the surface, rather look like a game made to appease the clique of rabid otaku. This served as a deterrant for me, but it's only skin-deep: the try-hard cutesy voice acting is minimal and can be disabled, the story doesn't involve an overly emotional hero with amnesia, and there is no harem of scantily-clad children. That's the usual suspects taken care of.
Recettear places you in the shoes of a girl named Recette, in a fairly typical JRPG setting. It turns out that Recette's father — who is now probably dead, which is beautifully glossed over — accrued a significant debt, and she's to pay it off by turning her home into an item shop. Your primary goal is making money rather than story or dungeon progression, which is quite a twist from the norm. The story doesn't try to do too much, and gets out of your way pretty quickly.
Items can be acquired at the local wholesalers or in dungeons. Yep, dungeons: you can hire an adventurer, kit them out with your own gear, and take them dungeon crawling. They even have their own levelling system and skills, though the combat system is fairly basic and uninteresting. Then there's crafting, in which you discover new items by combining others.
But you own an item shop, so you should be selling items. This process involves judging your customers' budgets, haggling, buying from customers, keeping up with item trends, taking pre-orders and appropriately stocking your shop. Speaking of the shop, it's customisable through a range of carpets, counters and wallpaper. Your shop can even be expanded and the furniture can be moved around.
There's quite a lot to Recettear, but you're not thrown in at the deep end: everything is revealed at what I can only call a perfect pace. Just as I was getting used to one mechanic, a new one popped up. Once the main game is completed — that is, once you've paid back the debt —  New Game+, Survival and Endless modes are unlocked, with plenty more items left to discover and levels to gain. To gauge just how much content there is here, I completed the main game with only 33% of items discovered and a merchant level of 19 (of 50).
All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed this game and will probably be playing a little Endless mode, in which there is no looming debt to repay, for some time.

I am a die hard hunting sim fan so lets get that out of the way. I also hunt in real life, so that is out of the way. I have also played the hunter Call of the Wild for 170 hours and that is now disclosed as well. Lets talk Hunting simulator.
I waited for this game to come out as I am super upset with the hunter call of the wild and it being a beta released as a full game. Months later it is still a glitchy as hell game.
So jumping into this game my frustration is already high to see we have the same scenario here.  But...it doesn't seem quite as bad. Some of the glitches I found were graphical. Screen tearing. A lot of screen flickering and a very dark lighting system that keeps going to almost black depending on how your character turns. I am running a gtx 1080 and a brand new Ryzen 1700. With all settings on Elite I only get 62 fps in this game.
The graphics are ok. Not as good as the hunter. Even on elite the flower draw distance is only about 30m out in front of your character so you see them popping in all the time. The dark gamma with no adjusment really annoys me on this game.
Sound. is ok. You hear the same 6 bird calls over and over and the fox calls sound like the just recorded a clip from the hunter. Guns sounds are weak...and over all sound is nothing special.
Game play is based on a mission system you unlock gear for beating new missions. There is a leader board, but the missions don't tell you how to maximize points first go through. You can beat the main and secondary objectives which are stated, but then the game will tell you to shoot a red fox. Well if you don't you won't break the top 100 on the leader board. Frustrating...it might be...or you can just enjoy playing missions over an over to better your score. Depends on your play style.
I found it annoying a la hunter that even when crouched animals take off running from hundreds of meters away. Here we are on a huge map again but you have to crawl like a snail or spook everything a mile out.
This is an arcade game. In 10 minutes you will see 8 fox 4 sheep and 3 mule deer...on the first mission. So it is not a hunting simulator. it is a bag em and tag em shoot em up. But don't make a bad shot or you will be penalized. That I can agree with. What I don't agree with is shooting a fox 3 times with your main rifle before it dies. Not very realistic.
In the end I am dissapointed. I will say yes if you are die hard grab the game but the price for me was a turn off...WAY TO HIGH. should have been a $20 game. Its not as good as the hunter...and guess what the game released and on the same day they have a DLC gun pack. WTF That I don't agree with. Will I eventually get my $36 bucks worth....probably I think I can put in 36 hours....but who knows. My patience with these beta games released as full games asking for DLC purchases for things that should be in the friggin game is wearing super thin.
I'd give it a 6/10 with the just barely reccomended rating.

I have played this game for a couple of hours now, and so far I'm really enjoying myself. Ofcourse this game isn't a Battlefield, so the gameplay is a lot slower and is a bit harder to get into. Expecially tracking and finding the animal that your mission is telling you to shoot can be a little bit difficult in the beginning. But once you get the hang of it (PRO TIP: Use your map A LOT), it's so rewarding to get a clean shot and claim your prey. It also seem to get a bit easier to find the right animal, once you unlock some callers and other items like wind sprays and binoculars.
There are some small bugs gameplay wise, like an animal didn't seem to notice when I missed a shot next to them, but nothing game breaking so far. I don't really agree with a lot of the negative reviews of the terrible animal AI, so far they behave as I suspect them to do. I didn't have any issues with animals getting stuck or having weird behavior.
I like how much detail the developers have put into the graphics, from different weather conditions and plants that move when the player runs through them to clothes that get wet when you run through water or if it rains (though this is mostly only visible in third person view, and if you are like me you will not use it that much).
So far I'm really impressed by the amount of content available in this game. I only unlocked 2 levels, a few guns and some items, but seeing what is still locked I think there is easily 50+ gameplay hours before you have played through the campaign. They even have a drone to unlock!
I haven't played a lot of multiplayer yet, but it seems quite fun to play some of the missions with a couple of friends. Would be nice if it had split screen co-op though.
PRO's:
- Lot's of content
- HUGE maps
- A wide variety of animals to hunt
- Online co-op Multiplayer
- Both first and third person view
- Nice graphics
- Full controller support
CON'S:
- Some small bugs
- Gameplay could use some polish
- No local co-op
- No visual display of trophies from animals you have killed
Conclusion:
If you don't mind a more slow paced game and like exploring big maps, give this game a go. But don't expect it to be easy to get into, so give it some time to get used to and really get the hang of the game.

I have had my eye on this game since Rooster Teeth released a Let's Play on it a while back.  It looked like it was a lot of fun, but I had my hesitations about buying it since I do not have a ton of friends on Steam.
I bought SpeedRunners when it went on sale during the last holiday sale and I have not been disappointed one bit.  As soon as you load up the game, you play through a quick tutorial.  This gets you used to the game quickly and easily.  Since I was the only one of my friends that had the game, I jumped into a Quick Match and ended up losing two hours right away with it.
This game hooks you instantly, pun intended.  The matchmaking is quick, with my highest wait time being about three minutes.  Gameplay is awesome.  It is fun learning how to use each power up, when the best time to use the powerups is, and the rush of beating everyone is addicting.  One of my favorite things to do is using the bomb powerup on a Runner while then are climbing walls, and watching them tumble all the way back down to their doom.  With all that being said, the game can be a bit buggy at times, with lag issues only popping up occasionally and level issues happening at about the same rate.
If you want a game that you can pick up for ten minutes and play, or if you have several hours to kill at once, pick up SpeedRunners.  This game will not disappoint.

It's a version of Euro Truck Simulator 2 adapted to the USA.
Firstly, it seems that many players complain about the geographical inadequacies of American Truck Simulator, but the simplifications are in fact rather similar to what they did in ETS2. Presumably, the American players know more about driving in the US or the geography of California than that of Europe, so they suddenly notice the simplifications only now.
Secondly, for those that suggest that the map is rather small, remember that ATS includes 20 cities in California alone. On the other hand, ETS2 still has just 8 French cities and 4 Italian cities (3 at release in 2012), more than 3 years after release. (France is 1.5 times the size of California.) The countries in ETS2 with more cities, UK and Germany, only have more because the base maps for them were just imported from the old games UKTS and GTS.
Lastly, remember that the USD price of ETS2 at release, USD 40, was double that of ATS, so I think USD 20 is a fair price for ATS. If it still sounds too expensive, one can always wait until the price inevitably drops, like it has for ETS2.

This game brings something new to the table that I think many people will enjoy. There are aspects of strategy, roguelike, deck building, and hack n slash. It is assembled with very appealing visuals and executes its unique style very well.
While playing there were definetly qualities that established it in my mind as similar to classic choose-your-own-adventure games, and aspects of DnD. The set up of "randomized" events set up on uniquely simulated dungeon maps and illustrated through card play is spot on.
This is also one of the few games that is absolutely delightful when played in endless mode. It is almost as if the developer started out crafting a game based on endless mode, and put a well made story mode in to pull it all together.
That combined with the just-long-enough, but making-me-beg-for-more, pacing of the main game makes for an excellent experience.
In game dialogue between the dealer and player regarding events, bosses, successes, and failures just brings the whole experience home and puts it up among my top favorite games.
I love this game so far, and can't wait to see what they produce with DLC.
I highly recommend this game.

Previous game : Metro 2033
Both games came out at a later stage in a 'redux' version with graphic tweaks and
extra mini missions.
If you like the Metro serie, I recommend to have a look at :
1) The S.T.A.L.K.E.R serie : non linear shooter in a fall-out setting
2) Fall-out serie : role playing game
3) Cryostasis, the sleep of reason : Freezzzzzzing horror game with a mask (not on Steam)
4) A bit further away, the Dead Space serie
Bugs : At the start, had a lot of 'return to desk top', screen freezings, loading errors.
After mingling with the graphic settings, game ran smoothly
Graphics : Metro has been used in the past as a benchmarking game (FPS rate) for testing new hardware so very good.
Diffiiculty : played on hard level (+ survival mode) without getting frustrated, extends the game play with hours. Difficulty can be lowered during the game via the menu if needed.
Save Points : yes, each chapter is divided in seperate areas which automatic saves.
Not a big burden but sometimes it saves just when you want to explore the area for goodies or your healt status is low, grrrr !
Me and my guns : standard range of weaponry, can be bought in shops or can be taken from dead bodies. Each weapon can be modified with for example a silencer or a clip which can contain more ammo.
Mask : You need a mask when going outside or are exposed to toxic gases and replace it's filters when they are used up. Can you buy filters, nope, you need to find them in secret areas or on dead bodies. No filters anymore.....you die.
Pain point, you need to rush through these levels (hard setting) to finish the mission or what i did, first screen the area and memorize the path and location of the goodies, reload the mission and then start to rush. No time to enjoy the scenery, run Forest Gump run.
Rambo or silent assassin : Part of the game can be tackled in a sneaky way throw knives or use a gun with silencer to kill an enemy without alerting his 'Comrads'. Switch of lights to remain undetected. Crouch to be less noisy. However, the slighest wrong move and hell breaks loose. As with the better stealth games, when remain hidden and undetected, the situation returns to normal after a minute or two. Not with Metro unfortunately. Once compromished, Rambo you will be.
Story : derived from the book so there is more meat to the bone then with most of the other shooters.
What i will remember : levels with the radspiders that dwell in the dimly-lit tunnels
Manual : No but i think, shooters deserve a manual just to know the keyboard mouse lay-out.
Play time : stats are indicating about ten hours, i spend more then thirty hours.
Final judgement : well done guys, looking forward to a new Metro. Do mind looking at the save points and the mask / filter system.

Who doesn't love a good game of mini-golf?  If you don't, you are looking at the wrong product, friend.  Golf With Your Friends is exactly what it says on the tin.  An online mini-golf game, complete with Workshop and cross-platform support.  Going into this game, I was very excited, as it is 100% up my alley, and I even have friends to play it with!  Imagine that.  If you don't, there are open servers and the community is very active.  I can't judge the community in terms of play experience, due to only playing in private servers, but it's mini-golf so how bad can it be?
With all of that said, this game isn't perfect.  My primary issue with the game is that it isn't very well optimized.  I tested this game on an HP Envy 17-1181 (Core i7 940XM, 8GB RAM, ATI Mobility Radeon HD 5850) and on a late 2012 MacBook Air (Core i5-3427U, 4GB RAM, Intel HD Graphics 4000).  Both run the game smoothly enough, but the game caused audio issues with Discord on the Mac, and caused the HP to shut down due to overheating.  Granted, the HP runs hot normally, but other Unity games don't cause the computer to shut down.  To be completely fair, the game is in Early Access, so this issue should be patched out once the game goes Gold.  Additionally, unlike a AAA development team, the devs of this game are probably limited on their testing hardware, so they can't possibly make the game run perfectly on every computer.  So while the poor optimization is an issue I ran into, I'm not as bothered by it as I would in another game.
I'm normally rather critical of the Early Access model, as it can feel like a leap of faith to the consumer.  This game is very worth playing, if only to see just how high (or low, if you have skill) your score can get.  I ended Oasis with 100+.

Awesome idea but it just sucks.  I really really wanted to love this game, I've given it a few dozen hours of game play, but none of it has been satisfying.  I thought I sucked at it completely until I googled the tips and found out how I was being beaten, frankly its just breaking the game but it works, my k/d ratio went up to about par but it destroyed everything this game was about.  I don't think this game can be saved at this point.  Frankly the game has basically been abandoned by the devs and 'cash cowed' at this point.  There has been no new real development in ages aside from microtransaction stuff, which incidentally makes it really hard to instantly tell who is on which team at a glance or distance without looking at the color of the name at the bottom when you look specifically at them.  A massive issue in a game where everyone is melee and team members will kill each other thinking they're on the opposite team and not have enough time to confirm otherwise.  Seriously I know they're trying to not break the whole medieval thing but a easily visible bloody color tag on characters would be a MASSIVE quality of life increase.
This game's main mechanic is its melee, which is full of animation exploits and other issues you can use to basically make it look like you're a raver trying to fellate yourself but will turn you into a whirlwind of death against anyone who doesn't know the same techniques (google matrixing, dragging, or any chivalry melee tips guide).  Archery is something that should help level the playing field a bit but often is damnably impossible to land shots with an even tiny amount of random strafe.  Excellent archers often only land about 20-25% of their shots, and said shots don't usually kill when landing.  It can take 3-4 to take down a knight unless you get a lucky head shot.  Combined with the long long 'reload' time they're pratically worthless.  A melee can literally run up to you and chop you down while taking shots and still have health left over.  I seriously loved what this game was trying to do, it was an amazingly complex idea and one of the best attempts at a true melee mechanic game I have ever seen or heard of.  The reflex parry is.... okay it's certainly better than every other skill based block on the market but I have been killed while parrying perfectly far to many times to count.  I think if they sped up the animations it might be a slightly better game making the animation exploiting more difficult and leveling the playing field but honestly it would be a bandaid on the situation, not a true fix.
In short, as much as I hate to say it, spend your money elsewhere, you'll be sorely disappointed here.

28 Waves Later is a cleverly titled wave-based zombie shooter, brought to us by Dagestan Technology; the same publisher/developer that worked on the Hotline Miami clone, Bloodbath Kavkaz. Now, if you're familiar with the aforementioned game, then that one statement will already have said a lot to you regarding this latest release.
As far as top-down, wave-based shooters go, this title has got to be one of the worst; it's so bottom of the barrel the developer didn't even finish it. Yes, that's right, despite several delays that cumulatively amounted to over a year, Dagestan Technology still had the nerve to release this pile of steaming poo even though there are only three levels in the entire game. Once you kill all of the zombies in level three and speak with the scientist, he will tell you there are still more zombies that are alive but there aren't.
The only developer "support" in the forums are a total of four comments, saying that the game will be released "soon" sometime last year. 28 Waves Later released in March, 2017 and was obviously swiftly abandoned, as there are no indications that the developer is still working on the title, and he does not address the 3 pages of threads regarding all of the bugs. So forget the fact that there are only a handful of zombie models, the same repeating background, terrible enemy AI, that the gun clip can go into negative bullets and still be functional, the complete lack of health and ammo pickups... the game isn't even finished! To top it all off, the achievements don't even work.
And to think, Dagestan Technology is trying to sell this hunk of gorilla turd for $5.49 CAD at the regular price, it isn't even worth the $0.54 CAD at a -90% off sale. Absolutely inexcusable, and insanely familiar of the bullcrap that Lord Kres pulled with Journey of the Light. Murdered: Soul Suspect is hard to place into a genre, but the closest thing I'd compare it to is an engaging movie. There is a -lot- a person could dislike about this game, but somehow, the rich environment, colorful lore, and memorable mechanics salvage the gameplay and emphasize the decent story.
Without giving too much away, M:SS has you playing a detective in Salem (yes, that Salem), who ends up -- you guessed it -- getting murdered at the very start of the game. You spend your time throughout the game walking through walls, solving murders and helping other spirits find piece, all while trying to figure out your own killer's identity and motives.
Now while all that seems like a kickass idea, playing it out can be a little... boring. For one, there's not really much 'combat' in this game, and what little fighting there is, it's basically a game of hide and seek. You spend most of your time hunting for spots to press 'X', whether it be for the 200 or so collectables, clues to your case, or looking for objects to poltergeist. Your powers as a ghost are almost disappointingly limited, despite how cool it was the first dozen or so times you walk through a wall or teleport. The game itself isn't even that long --I 100%'d it within two days.
So why recommend this game? Part of it is the story, and the lore that's painted around it. The game isn't what I'd call 'new age horror'. There aren't jump-scares, there are creepy things and eerie stories. You're rewarded for exploration with collectables, which give bits and pieces of the story around you, and those involved. The graphics and sound do a satisfactory job tying everything together, but they didn't stick out nearly as stylistically as games like Alan Wake.
